## Online OET Course for Nurses & Doctors | OET with Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/

Online OET course for nurses, doctors & pharmacists: recorded lessons, personal writing correction, 1:1 speaking practice and 1,750+ verified score cards.

OET preparation led by Dr Ahmed Hesham, a medical doctor — recorded courses, personal writing correction and 1:1 speaking practice for nurses, doctors, pharmacists and allied health professionals heading to the UK, USA, Australia, Canada and Qatar.

With over seven years of dedicated experience in OET preparation, I have
helped thousands of healthcare professionals achieve the results they need
to advance their international careers. From doctors and nurses to
pharmacists and allied health practitioners, my goal is to make OET
success practical, achievable, and career-focused. Start with the OET course for nurses
or the OET course for doctors , or get your letters marked
through OET writing correction .

How to enrol
Every package is delivered through the OET with Dr Hesham Candidates App. Enrolment takes about two minutes.
1
Choose your package
Compare the packages below and pick the route that fits your profession and exam date.
2
Create your free account
Sign in to the Candidates App — or create an account in seconds if you are new here.
3
Pay securely & start
Check out inside the Candidates App. Access is granted after payment is verified — usually within 12 hours.

Pricing & enrolment FAQs
Quick answers about payment, access and choosing the right package. More exam questions live on the full FAQ page .
How do I enrol in a package?
Pick your package on this page, then sign in to the Candidates App (or create a free account). You pay securely inside the Candidates App. Access is granted after payment is verified — usually within 12 hours.
What currency are the prices in?
All prices are in British pounds (GBP £). If you pay with a non-UK card, your bank converts the amount to your local currency at its own exchange rate.
How long do I keep access to my course?
The access period is shown on each package card (for example, &ldquo;6 months from purchase&rdquo;). TutorBook comes with permanent access including content updates.
What is TutorBook?
TutorBook is a recall-based OET book (First Edition 2026) covering all disciplines. It is available on its own or bundled with eligible course packages — look for the &ldquo;TutorBook eligible&rdquo; badge on package cards.
Can I get a refund?
Our products are digital and most give immediate access, which affects the usual 14-day cancellation right under UK consumer law. Please read the refund policy before you buy — it explains exactly when refunds are and are not available.

Are the OET courses live or recorded?
The full courses are recorded video lessons with structured study materials, so you can repeat any lesson during your access period. The personalised parts are Writing letter assessments, private one-to-one live Speaking sessions and Q&A support.

Which OET course is best for nurses?

Do the courses include writing correction?
The full Medicine, Physiotherapy and Allied Health courses include 5 Writing letter assessments and 1 private Speaking session, and so does the Nursing Premium Bundle. You can add more letter assessments to an eligible course at any time.

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-course-for-nurses.html

Online OET course for nurses: 30+ hours of recorded nursing lessons, personalised letter correction and 1:1 Speaking practice to reach the NMC score.

OET Nursing
Online OET Course for Nurses
The OET nursing course from Dr Hesham is a recorded, nursing-specific programme for internationally educated nurses. It covers Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking with nursing letters and role-plays, personalised letter correction and a live 1:1 Speaking session, so you can work towards the NMC score: B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026

NMC-ready route
Learn the nursing method, then get corrected.
Most nurses do not fail OET on knowledge. They lose marks on letter selection and role-play structure. The course fixes both with nursing-specific practice and feedback.
01 Check your level Free placement test across all four skills.
02 Learn the method Recorded lessons with nursing letters and role-plays.
03 Get corrected Letter assessments and a live 1:1 Speaking session.
Who is this OET nursing course for?
The course is built for nurses who need OET Nursing for registration abroad and want one clear route instead of scattered free material.
Nurses joining the NMC register
If you are an internationally educated nurse working towards NMC registration in the UK, this course trains the exact OET Nursing tasks you will meet, alongside your CBT and OSCE preparation. The UK pathway guide explains the full NMC route.
Nurses stuck below C+ in Writing
Writing is where many nurses repeat the exam. The course teaches case-note selection, letter structure and professional tone for nursing readers, then corrects your letters so you can see what still costs marks.
Nurses heading to Australia or the Gulf
OET Nursing is also used for nursing registration outside the UK. Check your destination in the Australia pathway guide or the Gulf pathway guide , then prepare with the same nursing method.
What OET score do nurses need?
For the UK, the NMC asks for OET Nursing with grade B (350) in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ (300) in Writing. Other destinations set their own rules, so check the right regulator first.
Destination Regulator OET requirement Official source
United Kingdom NMC B (350) in Listening, Reading and Speaking; C+ (300) in Writing. Results from two sittings may be combined only under NMC rules. NMC: accepted OET results
Australia Nursing and Midwifery Board (AHPRA) For tests from 23 April 2026: Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350, Speaking 360 (all National Boards). OET@Home is not accepted. See score requirements . Australia pathway guide
Qatar and the Gulf Qatar DHP and other Gulf regulators Requirements differ by country and licensing route. Gulf pathway guide
Verify with your regulator before booking. Requirements, validity rules and accepted test formats can change. Always confirm on the official regulator page before you book OET or pay any fee.

Choose your Nursing package. The price is the same for Paper-Based and Computer-Based candidates. Nursing has its own packages: the Classic Nursing OET Course and the Nursing Premium Bundle. How does the online nursing course work?
The course is self-paced, but the route is fixed: diagnose, learn, get corrected, test yourself, then book.
01 Take the free placement test Check your Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking level on the free General English placement test (free account, results saved).
02 Choose your nursing package Pick the Classic Nursing OET Course or the Nursing Premium Bundle. If you are unsure, send your level and exam date on WhatsApp.
03 Study the recorded lessons Work through the nursing lessons for all four sub-tests and replay any lesson during your 6 months of access.
04 Submit letters for correction Write timed nursing letters and receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback.
05 Practise Speaking 1:1 Use your private live session to rehearse nursing role-plays and get feedback on structure, empathy and language.
06 Sit a full mock exam Check all four sub-tests under exam timing before you pay for the real test.
07 Book OET and release your results When your practice scores are consistently at target, book OET Nursing and send your results to the NMC or your regulator.
How do you pass OET Writing as a nurse?
OET Nursing Writing gives you 45 minutes (5 minutes of reading time and 40 minutes of writing) to turn a set of case notes into one letter of about 180–200 words. The reader is usually a health professional who will continue the patient’s care.
Discharge letters Hand a patient over to a community or district nurse, a GP or a family carer, with the care plan, medication changes and follow-up the reader must act on.
Transfer letters Move a patient to a rehabilitation unit, care home or another ward, focusing on current condition, mobility, risks and ongoing nursing needs.
Referral letters Refer a patient to a GP, physiotherapist, dietitian or other professional, stating clearly why they are being referred and what you are asking for.
What the examiner checks Purpose, content, conciseness and clarity, genre and style, organisation and layout, and language. A clear purpose in the opening line and a specific final request protect marks in several criteria at once.
The most common reason nurses miss C+ is selection: copying too many case notes instead of choosing what the reader needs. The course trains a repeatable selection method on nursing tasks, and the OET Writing tips show the core rules. If you already have letters written, OET writing correction shows you exactly what to fix.
What nursing role-plays will you practise for OET Speaking?
OET Speaking has two role-plays. You get 3 minutes to prepare each card and about 5 minutes to complete it, with the interlocutor playing the patient or a relative.
Typical nursing scenarios
Explaining a procedure, wound care or a discharge plan
Medication adherence, side effects and safe use
Lifestyle advice after diagnosis, such as diet, smoking or exercise
Reassuring an anxious patient or a worried relative
Persuading a reluctant patient to accept treatment or follow-up
How you are assessed
Examiners score clinical communication (relationship building, understanding the patient’s perspective, providing structure, gathering information and giving information) as well as intelligibility, fluency, appropriate language and grammar. A calm structure and patient-friendly explanations matter more than advanced vocabulary.
The recorded lessons give you nursing cards with expected ideas and useful language, and the live 1:1 session lets you rehearse them with feedback. Read the OET Speaking tips for the role-play method before your session.
How do you prepare for OET Listening and Reading?
Listening and Reading are the same for every profession, so nurses sit exactly the same papers as other candidates. What changes your score is method, not luck.
Listening (about 40 minutes) Part A is note completion from two consultations, Part B is short workplace extracts and Part C is longer presentations or interviews. Train prediction before each extract and write exactly what you hear, with correct spelling. See the OET Listening tips .
Reading (60 minutes) Part A is a strict 15-minute scanning task across four short texts; Parts B and C test detail, gist and inference. Use keyword anchors in Part A and eliminate distractors in Parts B and C. See the OET Reading tips .
The course practice library gives you timed papers with answer keys and rationales, and the separate Listening and Reading practice packages add more papers when you need volume before the exam.
Which add-ons help most before exam day?
Every package can be extended when you need more feedback. Add-ons are tied to your active course and are the fastest way to fix the sub-test that is holding your score back.
Extra Writing assessments
Add 3, 5, 7 or 10 letter assessments to an active course. Each letter is marked manually with an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback via WhatsApp. You can choose your own letters or follow recall-recommended tasks.
Private Speaking sessions
Book one or two live 1:1 Speaking assessment sessions. Each session covers different OET cards and ends with detailed performance feedback, so you hear exactly what to change before the real role-plays.
Full mock exams
Sit 1, 3 or 5 full OET mock exams across all four sub-tests. Writing and Speaking are assessed with detailed feedback, Listening and Reading are auto-marked, and each mock package is valid for 6 months.
Writing assessment packages Speaking sessions Full mock exams
Can you see real OET results first?
Yes. Before you enrol, browse the 1,750+ verified OET score cards from 2021–2026 shared by nurses, doctors and other healthcare professionals who prepared with Dr Hesham. They are grouped by year, so you can see recent results rather than old screenshots.

How does the online OET Medicine course work?
The course is self-paced, but the route is fixed: diagnose, learn, get corrected, test yourself, then book.
01 Take the free placement test Check your Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking level on the free General English placement test (free account, results saved).
02 Choose your Medicine package Pick the Classic course or a Full / Complete bundle. If you are unsure, send your level and exam date on WhatsApp.
03 Study the recorded lessons Work through 40+ hours of OET Medicine lessons and replay any lesson during your 6 months of access.
04 Submit letters for correction Write timed medical letters and receive personalised correction on your 5 included letter assessments.
05 Practise Speaking 1:1 Use your private live session to rehearse consultations and get feedback on structure, empathy and language.
06 Sit a full mock exam Check all four sub-tests under exam timing before you pay for the real test.
07 Book OET and release your results Book OET Medicine when your practice scores are consistently at target, then release your results to the GMC, or to ECFMG with your MyIntealth ID.
How do doctors pass OET Writing?
OET Medicine Writing gives you 45 minutes (5 minutes of reading time and 40 minutes of writing) to turn case notes into one letter of about 180–200 words, usually to a medical colleague who will take over or continue care.
Referral to a specialist Summarise the presenting problem, relevant history, investigations and management so far, then state exactly what you want the specialist to do and how urgently.
Discharge or referral back to the GP Tell the GP what happened in hospital, what changed, and what follow-up, monitoring or medication review is needed in the community.
Transfer and urgent referral letters Lead with the reason for transfer or the urgent concern, then give only the details the receiving team needs to act safely.
What the examiner checks Purpose, content, conciseness and clarity, genre and style, organisation and layout, and language. Doctors often lose marks by writing a chronological history instead of a letter organised around the reader’s task.
The course trains a repeatable method for letter purpose, case-note selection and a specific final request on medical tasks, and the OET Writing tips show the core rules. If your letters keep landing just below B, OET writing correction shows you exactly what is costing marks.
What consultations will you practise for OET Speaking?
OET Speaking has two role-plays. You get 3 minutes to prepare each card and about 5 minutes to complete it, with the interlocutor playing the patient or a relative.
Typical Medicine scenarios
Explaining a diagnosis or test result in patient-friendly language
Discussing investigations and treatment options
Breaking bad news with empathy and a clear plan
Responding to a worried or angry relative
Persuading a reluctant patient, for example about smoking or medication adherence
How you are assessed
Examiners score clinical communication (relationship building, understanding the patient’s perspective, providing structure, gathering information and giving information) as well as intelligibility, fluency, appropriate language and grammar. Doctors usually need to replace medical jargon with plain explanations and check the patient’s understanding.
The course includes 100+ Speaking cards across different scenarios, and the live 1:1 session lets you rehearse them with feedback. Read the OET Speaking tips for the role-play method before your session.
How do you prepare for OET Listening and Reading?
Listening and Reading are the same for every profession, so doctors sit exactly the same papers as other candidates. What changes your score is method, not luck.
Listening (about 40 minutes) Part A is note completion from two consultations, Part B is short workplace extracts and Part C is longer presentations or interviews. Train prediction before each extract and write exactly what you hear, with correct spelling. See the OET Listening tips .
Reading (60 minutes) Part A is a strict 15-minute scanning task across four short texts; Parts B and C test detail, gist and inference. Use keyword anchors in Part A and eliminate distractors in Parts B and C. See the OET Reading tips .
The course practice library gives you timed papers with answer keys and rationales, and the separate Listening and Reading practice packages add more papers when you need volume before the exam.
Which add-ons help most before exam day?
Every package can be extended when you need more feedback. Add-ons are tied to your active course and are the fastest way to fix the sub-test that is holding your score back.
Extra Writing assessments
Add 3, 5, 7 or 10 letter assessments to an active course. Each letter is marked manually with an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback via WhatsApp. You can choose your own letters or follow recall-recommended tasks.
Private Speaking sessions
Book one or two live 1:1 Speaking assessment sessions. Each session covers different OET cards and ends with detailed performance feedback, so you hear exactly what to change before the real role-plays.
Full mock exams
Sit 1, 3 or 5 full OET mock exams across all four sub-tests. Writing and Speaking are assessed with detailed feedback, Listening and Reading are auto-marked, and each mock package is valid for 6 months.

## OET Writing Correction Service | Letters Marked by Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-writing-correction.html

OET writing correction for nurses, doctors and pharmacists: letters marked with an estimated score, detailed corrections and WhatsApp voice-note feedback.

Writing correction
OET Writing Correction: Get Your Letters Marked
Send your OET letter and get it back marked by Dr Ahmed Hesham, with an estimated score, detailed corrections and a WhatsApp voice note that explains exactly what to change. Manual letter assessments are returned within 48–72 hours, excluding Fridays, for nurses, doctors and pharmacy candidates.

Score Estimated score for every manually marked letter
Voice note Spoken feedback sent to you on WhatsApp
48–72h Turnaround on letter assessment add-ons, excluding Fridays
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Updated 24 Oct 2026
One correction cycle
Write, get marked, rewrite. Repeat until the letter scores.
A corrected letter is only useful if the next one is better. Every assessment is built so you know what lost marks and what to do differently on the next task.
01 Submit a timed letter Your own choice of case or a recall-recommended task.
02 Get it marked Estimated score, corrections and a voice note.
03 Rewrite and resubmit Apply the feedback on your next letter.
What you get for every corrected OET letter
OET writing correction only helps when the feedback is specific enough to act on. Each manual letter assessment gives you four things.
An estimated score
Every letter is given an estimated score, so you can see whether your writing is near the grade your regulator asks for, or still some way off, before you book or rebook the exam.
Detailed correction
Your letter is corrected in detail: which case notes did not belong, where the structure lost the reader, which sentences need rewording, and which language errors repeat.
Voice-note feedback on WhatsApp
Dr Hesham explains the corrections in a voice note sent via WhatsApp. Hearing why a choice cost marks is often what makes the fix stick on the next letter.
Letters you choose, or recall-based tasks
Submit letters you have chosen yourself, or work through recall-recommended letters so your practice reflects the letter types candidates are meeting in recent exams.
How OET writing correction works
The process is simple. What matters is that you write under exam conditions and use every piece of feedback on the next letter.
01 Write under exam conditions
Use the five minutes of reading time, then write the letter in the 40 minutes allowed without notes or templates. A letter written slowly with help tells you very little about your exam score.
02 Submit it for assessment
Send your letter with the case notes it answers. Manual assessments in the letter add-ons are returned within 48–72 hours, excluding Fridays.
03 Read the corrections, then listen to the voice note
Go through the marked letter first, then listen to the explanation. Write down the two or three errors that cost you most; they are your focus for the next letter.
04 Rewrite, then write a new letter
Rewrite the same letter with the corrections applied, then attempt a different case. Improvement shows when the fixes hold on a task you have not seen before.
What your letter is marked against
OET Writing is assessed against six published criteria. Corrections and feedback are organised around the same areas, so you know which part of the letter is holding your score back.
Purpose Can the reader tell straight away why you are writing and what you need them to do? The purpose should be clear in the opening and supported to the end.
Content Have you included the case notes this reader needs, accurately, and left out what they do not? Relevance matters more than completeness.
Conciseness and clarity Is the information summarised efficiently, without padding or repetition, so the reader can take it in quickly?
Genre and style Is the register right for a professional letter and for this particular reader, whether a specialist, a nurse, a care home or a patient?
Organisation and layout Are paragraphs grouped logically and ordered by importance, with a layout the reader can follow without searching?
Language Are grammar, vocabulary, spelling and punctuation accurate enough that nothing gets in the way of the meaning?
Common reasons OET letters miss a B
Most candidates who are stuck at C or C+ are not short of English. They repeat the same few habits, and correction is the quickest way to spot them.
The purpose is buried The reader reaches the second paragraph before learning why the letter was written or what is being asked of them.
Case notes are copied, not selected Every note is transferred into the letter, including history the reader does not need, which hides the information that matters.
The tone does not fit the reader A letter to a patient's relative written like a specialist referral, or a referral that sounds casual, loses marks in genre and style.
Information is out of order Paragraphs follow the order of the case notes instead of the order the reader needs, so the urgent point arrives late.
The closing request is vague The letter ends without a clear request or next step, which weakens purpose even when the rest is strong.
Small language errors repeat Tense, articles and sentence boundaries go wrong in the same way on every letter. Once someone points the pattern out, it is usually quick to fix.
For a method you can use on every task, read the 11 OET Writing tips .

How long does OET writing correction take?
Writing letter assessment add-ons are marked manually and returned within 48–72 hours, excluding Fridays. Writing Assessment Packages in the learner app give a Detailed Writing Assessment Within 15 Minutes, with criteria-aligned feedback, from the time a completed letter is submitted.
Who marks my OET letters?
Manual letter assessments are marked by Dr Ahmed Hesham. Letters submitted through the app's Writing Assessment Packages are assessed using Dr Ahmed Hesham's Exclusive OET Rulebook, with detailed, criteria-aligned feedback; personal correction by Dr Hesham is the separate manual service.
What feedback do I get on each letter?
Each manually assessed letter comes back with an estimated score, detailed corrections and a voice-note explanation sent via WhatsApp. You can submit letters you choose yourself or letters recommended from recent recalls.
Do I need to be enrolled in a course to get my letters corrected?
The 3, 5, 7 and 10-letter assessment add-ons are for candidates enrolled in an eligible course and follow that course's access window. The Recorded Writing Crash Course bundles and the app's Writing Assessment Packages can be bought on their own.

Yes. Manual letter assessments cover doctors, nurses and pharmacy candidates, the Writing Crash Course is available for Medicine, Nursing and Pharmacy, and the app's Writing Assessment Packages are open to all disciplines.

## OET Score Calculator 2026: Grades and Regulator Minimums

By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Updated 24 Oct 2026
Listening Reading Writing Speaking
Check my scores
How is OET scored?
Each of the four sub-tests is reported separately on a scale from 0 to 500, in steps of 10, and each score maps to a letter grade. There is no overall score: regulators look at each sub-test on its own.
Grade Score range What it usually means for registration
A 450–500 Above every common regulator minimum.
B 350–440 The minimum most regulators ask for in each sub-test.
C+ 300–340 Accepted for Writing by the NMC, NMBI, ECFMG and both New Zealand councils; below the GMC and Ahpra minimums.
C 200–290 Below the usual registration minimums.
D 100–190 Below the usual registration minimums.
E 0–90 Below the usual registration minimums.
What OET score do you need?
The four most common targets are below; the calculator checks eleven. Requirements change, so always confirm on the regulator's own page before you book.
Regulator Listening Reading Writing Speaking Sittings
NMC (UK nurses, midwives) 350 350 300 350 Two sittings can be combined under NMC rules
GMC (UK doctors) 350 350 350 350 One sitting, Medicine version
Ahpra (Australia, tests from 23 Apr 2026) 350 360 350 360 One sitting, or two within 12 months with floors of 320/340/350/350
ECFMG (USA, 2027 Pathways) 350 350 300 350 One sitting, on or after 1 January 2025
Registering in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand or the Gulf? See the full OET score requirements by regulator .
How are Listening and Reading raw scores converted?
Listening and Reading each have 42 questions worth one mark. OET converts your raw mark to the 0–500 scale, and according to OET, candidates awarded Grade B (350) typically score at least 30 out of 42. The exact boundary moves slightly with each test version, and OET does not publish a fixed raw mark for C+ (300).
Source: OET results and scoring . Treat any online chart that gives an exact raw mark for every score as an estimate.
How does an OET score compare with IELTS and CEFR?
OET publishes its own benchmarking tables. Grade B sits at CEFR C1 and is benchmarked to IELTS 7.0 (350–390) or 7.5 (400–440).
OET score IELTS band CEFR
A (450–500) 8.0–9.0 C2
B (400–440) 7.5 C1
B (350–390) 7.0 C1
C+ (300–340) 6.5 B2
C (250–290) 6.0 B2
C (200–240) 5.5 B2
Source: OET benchmarking tables . Choosing between the two tests? Read OET vs IELTS .

OET score calculator FAQ
What is a passing score in OET?
OET has no single pass mark. Each regulator sets its own minimum. Many ask for Grade B (350) in each sub-test; the NMC, NMBI and ECFMG accept 300 in Writing, and Ahpra asks for 350, 360, 350 and 360 for tests taken from 23 April 2026.
What grade is 350 in OET?
350 is Grade B. Grade B covers scores from 350 to 440 on the 0 to 500 scale.
Does this calculator replace my official result?
No. It applies the published grade bands and regulator minimums to the scores you enter. Your official OET result and your regulator's current rules always take priority.
Which regulators does the calculator check?
It checks the NMC, GMC and GPhC in the UK, Ahpra in Australia, NMBI and the Medical Council of Ireland, both New Zealand councils, ECFMG and CGFNS VisaScreen in the USA, and the Singapore Medical Council. It checks one-sitting minimums; combined-sitting rules are explained in the OET score requirements guide.

## OET Score Requirements 2026: NMC, GMC, Ahpra, NMBI & More

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-score-requirements.html

OET score requirements for 2026: minimum scores, sittings, OET@Home rules and validity for the NMC, GMC, Ahpra, NMBI, New Zealand, ECFMG and more.

OET Exam Guide
OET Score Requirements by Regulator (2026)
There is no single OET pass mark. Each regulator sets its own minimum score for each sub-test: most ask for grade B (350), several accept C+ (300) in Writing, and Ahpra raised its minimums for tests taken from 23 April 2026. This guide lists the scores, sitting rules, OET@Home acceptance and validity for each major regulator.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026
Checked against official regulator pages on 24 October 2026. Rules change — confirm before you book.
Check your scores Ask on WhatsApp
At a glance
The rules most candidates miss
01 Most want B (350) In every sub-test, but the NMC, NMBI, NCNZ, MCNZ and ECFMG accept 300 in Writing.
02 Ahpra changed in 2026 From 23 April 2026: 350 Listening, 360 Reading, 350 Writing, 360 Speaking.
03 OET@Home is limited Accepted by the NMC and GMC; not by Ahpra, NMBI, HCPC or GPhC.
OET score requirements at a glance
Minimum scores by regulator for the test dates shown. Each regulator name links to its official page.
Regulator Who Listening Reading Writing Speaking Sittings OET@Home Validity
NMC UK nurses, midwives 350 350 300 350 1, or 2 within 12 months Accepted 2 years

* GPhC may accept older results with evidence of maintained English; Ahpra has limited exceptions for continuous work or study.
What OET score do you need in the UK?
The UK has four regulators that matter for OET candidates, and each has its own rules.
NMC (nurses and midwives): OET Nursing with B (350) in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ (300) in Writing. Paper, computer and OET@Home are all accepted, and OET@Home results can be combined with paper or computer results. NMC: OET requirements .
GMC (doctors): OET Medicine with at least B in all four sub-tests, in the same test and your most recent sitting. Paper, computer and OET@Home are accepted. Results are valid for 2 years, with a possible extension to under 3 years if you passed PLAB 2 less than 3 months before applying (not on the sponsorship route). GMC: using your OET certificate .
GPhC (pharmacists and pharmacy technicians): OET Pharmacy with at least B in each of the four areas in one sitting, on paper or computer only. The GPhC does not accept OET@Home. Results should be under 2 years old; older results may be considered with evidence that you have maintained your English. GPhC guidance (PDF) .
GDC (dentists): the GDC’s current list of accepted evidence does not include OET, and the GDC says its guidance is under review. GDC: English language controls .
HCPC uses a total-score rule instead of per-skill minimums. You need the profession-specific OET, taken at an official test centre rather than at home, and the certificate must be no more than 2 years old when HCPC receives your application. HCPC: English language proficiency .
HCPC profession OET version Minimum
Chiropodists and podiatrists Podiatry 1400 total, no element below 300
Dietitians Dietetics 1400 total, no element below 300
Occupational therapists Occupational Therapy 1400 total, no element below 300
Physiotherapists Physiotherapy 1400 total, no element below 300
Radiographers Radiography 1400 total, no element below 300
Speech and language therapists Speech Pathology 1800 total, no element below 400
For the full registration route, see the UK pathway guide .
What OET score do you need in Ireland?
Both Irish regulators want a single sitting and do not accept OET@Home.
NMBI (nurses and midwives): OET Nursing with B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing. NMBI accepts one test result only, does not accept combined results and does not accept OET at home. Results must be under 2 years old. NMBI: English language requirements .
Medical Council of Ireland (doctors): for applications from 1 March 2025, OET Medicine with at least B in each module in a single sitting. OET@Home is not accepted, and the certificate must be dated within 2 years of both your application and your registration. Graduates of Irish, EU/EEA, UK, Australian, New Zealand and US medical schools, among others, are exempt. Medical Council: English language .
What OET score does Ahpra need from 23 April 2026?
From 23 April 2026 the National Boards raised the published OET minimums. Ahpra says this aligns with migration scores and does not change the level of English required.
Ahpra and all National Boards (except the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Practice Board) use the same English test list and minimums, so the rules below apply to nurses, midwives, doctors, pharmacists, physiotherapists and the other regulated professions. Any profession-specific OET is accepted. Ahpra: accepted English language tests .
OET test taken Listening Reading Writing Speaking
On or after 23 April 2026 350 360 350 360
Two sittings: no score in either below 320 340 350 350
On or before 22 April 2026 B (350) B (350) C+ (300) B (350)
Sittings: one sitting, or at most two sittings within 12 months, with all four components tested each time. Results from different test providers cannot be combined.
Mixed dates: if your first sitting was on or before 22 April 2026 and your second on or after 23 April 2026, each sitting must meet the minimums that applied on its date.
Test mode: OET on paper or on computer at a test centre. OET@Home is not accepted; the computer test’s remotely delivered Speaking component has been assessed as acceptable.
Validity: results must be no more than 2 years old when you lodge your application, with limited exceptions for continuous work or study in a recognised country. The NMBA also links its English language skills standard to these minimums.
For the full process, see the Australia pathway guide .
What OET score do you need in New Zealand?
Nurses and doctors in New Zealand need 300 in Writing and 350 in the other sub-tests.
Nursing Council of New Zealand: 350 in Reading, Listening and Speaking and 300 in Writing. Scores can come from more than one sitting, within 12 months of the first, and all sittings must be within the 3 years before you apply. Online tests, including OET@Home, are not accepted; OET on computer at an approved venue is. Nursing Council: English language .
Medical Council of New Zealand: OET Medicine with 350 in Speaking, Listening and Reading and 300 in Writing, in one sitting or at most two within 12 months, with all four components tested each time and no component below 300 in either sitting. Results must be within 2 years of your registration application. MCNZ English language policy (PDF) .
What OET score do you need in the USA?
Doctors use OET for ECFMG certification; nurses use it for the VisaScreen certificate.
ECFMG (2027 Pathways): OET Medicine with 350 in Listening, Reading and Speaking and 300 in Writing in one test administration, taken on or after 1 January 2025. OET@Home is available only if there is no test venue in your country, and results released from 14 May 2026 need your MyIntealth ID. Read the full OET for ECFMG guide for deadlines.
CGFNS / TruMerit VisaScreen: OET is accepted, but at-home versions of English tests are not. For exams taken on or after 12 May 2026 the minimums are:
VisaScreen group Speaking Reading Writing Listening
Registered nurses and other degree-level workers 360 340 350 320
Occupational therapists and physical therapists 360 340 350 320
Below-degree-level workers (e.g. LPN/LVN) 360 310 290 290
Exams taken before 12 May 2026 are certified under the previous minimums (registered nurses: 300 in Reading, Listening and Writing and 350 in Speaking). Sources: TruMerit VisaScreen , pre-12 May 2026 scores and CGFNS FAQ . US state boards of nursing set their own English rules, so check your board directly. See the USA pathway guide .
What OET score do you need in Singapore?
The Singapore Medical Council publishes OET minimums for doctors.
Singapore Medical Council: international medical graduates whose basic medical degree was not taught in English need at least B in each of the four OET components in a single sitting, accepted within 2 years of the test date. SMC: documents for registration . We could not find an official Singapore Nursing Board statement on OET scores, so check with the board directly.
What about the Gulf?
Requirements differ by country and licensing route.
Gulf regulators publish their English requirements on their own portals and they change often. We could not confirm current official OET minimums for Qatar or Dubai, so check with the regulator before you book. The Gulf pathway guide walks through the licensing steps.
How do OET scores and grades work?
Knowing the scale helps you read any regulator's table.
Each sub-test is reported from 0 to 500 in steps of 10, with a letter grade: A (450–500), B (350–440), C+ (300–340), C (200–290), D (100–190) and E (0–90). OET does not issue an overall score or grade, so regulators look at each sub-test separately. OET: results and scoring .
Listening and Reading each have 42 questions. OET says candidates awarded grade B typically score at least 30 out of 42, but the exact number changes with each test version. Writing and Speaking are marked against published criteria by two assessors. Check your own result against these minimums with the OET score calculator .
Can you combine two OET sittings?
Combining is the exception, not the rule.
NMC: up to two sittings within 12 months, both no more than 2 years old. Each required score must be met once, with no Listening, Reading or Speaking score below 300 and no Writing score below 250 in either sitting. You cannot retake single sub-tests, and OET and IELTS cannot be combined.
Ahpra: up to two sittings within 12 months, with the floor scores in the Australia table above.
Nursing Council of NZ and Medical Council of NZ: allowed under the rules in the New Zealand section.
One sitting only: GMC, GPhC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, ECFMG and the Singapore Medical Council.
OET itself only sells single sub-test resits for paper tests, after a full test, and not in the USA. Many regulators will not accept a result built from sub-test resits, so check before you book one.
Is OET@Home accepted?
Check this before you book, because most regulators outside the UK do not accept it.
OET@Home is offered in countries where taking the test at a venue is not yet available, and OET warns it may not be accepted by all recognising organisations. OET@Home .
Accepted: NMC and GMC.
Only without a venue in your country: ECFMG.
Not accepted: Ahpra, HCPC, GPhC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, the Nursing Council of New Zealand and CGFNS VisaScreen.
How long are OET results valid?
Validity is set by the regulator, not by OET.
OET does not set a validity period for results. Each organisation decides how long it accepts them:
Regulator How recent your result must be
NMC 2 years before the complete application is assessed
GMC 2 years (on the day of PLAB 1, or when registration is approved)
HCPC No more than 2 years old when the application is received
GPhC Under 2 years; older accepted with evidence
NMBI Under 2 years
Medical Council of Ireland Within 2 years of both application and registration
Ahpra 2 years before the application is lodged, with exceptions
Nursing Council of NZ All sittings within 3 years before the application
Medical Council of NZ Within 2 years of the application
Singapore Medical Council Within 2 years of the test date
ECFMG Test taken on or after 1 January 2025 (2027 Pathways)
FAQ
Is there a single OET passing score?
No. OET reports each sub-test from 0 to 500 with a grade, and each regulator sets its own minimums. Many ask for grade B (350) in every sub-test, while some, such as the NMC and NMBI, accept C+ (300) in Writing.
What OET score does Ahpra need in 2026?
For tests taken on or after 23 April 2026, Ahpra and the National Boards ask for at least 350 in Listening, 360 in Reading, 350 in Writing and 360 in Speaking. Tests taken on or before 22 April 2026 are assessed against the previous minimums of B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing.
Which regulators accept OET@Home?
The NMC and the GMC accept OET@Home. ECFMG accepts it only if there is no test venue in your country. Ahpra, HCPC, GPhC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, the Nursing Council of New Zealand and CGFNS VisaScreen do not accept it.
Can I combine OET results from two sittings?
Some regulators allow it under strict rules, including the NMC, Ahpra, the Nursing Council of New Zealand and the Medical Council of New Zealand. The GMC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, GPhC, ECFMG and the Singapore Medical Council need all scores from one sitting.
How long are OET results valid?
OET does not set a validity period; each regulator does. Most, including the NMC, GMC, Ahpra and NMBI, accept results up to two years old under their own rules, while the Nursing Council of New Zealand allows sittings within the three years before you apply.
Know your target? Now close the gap.
Most candidates miss their target in one sub-test, usually Writing or Speaking. Start with the free placement test , then choose the OET course for nurses , the OET course for doctors or OET writing correction .

OET exam guide
OET Test Dates 2026, Fees and Results
OET on paper runs on fixed Saturdays roughly every two weeks in 2026, with Americas sessions on the Friday before, and the last paper sessions are on 18 and 19 December. The full test costs AU$587 (US$455 for computer and OET@Home tests in the USA). Computer results can arrive in 48 hours; paper results take from 13 days.

Which OET test mode should you book?
OET is delivered in three ways. The mode changes which professions you can book, how Speaking works, when bookings close and how fast results arrive. For a side-by-side guide to the two venue formats, read OET on computer vs paper .

Before you book OET@Home, check that your regulator accepts it. The NMC and the GMC accept OET@Home. Ahpra , the HCPC , the GPhC , NMBI , the Medical Council of Ireland , the Nursing Council of New Zealand and CGFNS VisaScreen do not. ECFMG allows OET@Home only if there is no physical test venue in your country.

OET paper test dates 2026
OET on paper runs on fixed dates. Global sessions are on Saturdays, about two a month, and Americas sessions are on the Friday before each Global date. Paper bookings close 24 days before the test, which falls on a Wednesday for Global sessions and a Tuesday for Americas sessions.

The matching Americas session is the day before each date. The last one is Friday 18 December 2026: bookings close on Tuesday 24 November and results are due on 5 January 2027. Both December sessions are the final chance in 2026 to sit OET on paper.
OET on Computer and OET@Home dates
OET on Computer does not follow the paper calendar. In the computer dates we checked on OET's booking page (March to July 2026), Global computer sessions ran from Monday to Saturday in most weeks, with a few weeks that had none. All 12 professions were available, and each date showed a results date, usually the Friday of the following week.
Computer and OET@Home bookings close 7 days before the test at 11:59 pm UTC, so you can book much closer to your exam than on paper. Dates and venues vary by country. Use the official OET date finder to see what is available where you live.
OET test dates 2027
As of 2 November 2026, OET has not published any 2027 test dates or a 2027 date pattern. We will not guess them. When OET releases them, they will appear on the official booking page with their booking deadlines and results dates. If you are applying for the 2027 Match, see OET for ECFMG : ECFMG asks candidates to sit OET Medicine on or before the last scheduled date in December 2026.
How much does OET cost in 2026?
The full OET test costs AU$587 in every mode. Candidates in the USA pay US$455 for OET on Computer at a venue or OET@Home.

Changing your booking costs less the earlier you do it. These are the fees in OET's test regulations.

When do OET results come out?
OET reports each sub-test separately on a scale from 0 to 500. There is no overall OET score or grade.
Computer and OET@Home: results in as little as 48 hours after you finish all four sub-tests. For OET on Computer, OET says 95% are released within 6 calendar days.
Paper: from 13 days after the test date, or from 5 days in India and the Philippines.
Doctors applying to ECFMG: ECFMG says OET Medicine results are typically released 10 business days after the test.
OET describes all timeframes as indicative. OET itself sets no validity period for results: each regulator decides how long it accepts them, so check the OET score requirements for your destination. To see which grade each score gives, use the OET score calculator .
How to choose your OET test date
Work backwards from the date your regulator or employer needs your result, then add time for preparation and a possible re-sit.
Start from your deadline
Find the date your regulator, employer or ECFMG must receive your scores, then count back the results time for your mode.
Book 6 to 10 weeks ahead
Our advice: this gives you a firm target for preparation and protects you from paper booking closing 24 days before the test.
Need results fast?
OET on Computer gives the quickest results and closes bookings only 7 days before, which helps when a deadline is close.
Check the mode is accepted
Do not book OET@Home unless your regulator accepts it. Ahpra, NMBI, the GPhC and the HCPC do not.
Leave room for a re-sit
If your regulator needs all four sub-tests in one sitting, plan a second full test date in case one sub-test falls short.
Applying for the 2027 Match?
Sit OET Medicine by the last December 2026 date. ECFMG must receive your scores by 31 January 2027. OET for ECFMG .
Not sure you are ready for the date you want? Take the free placement test , then follow the OET course for nurses or the OET course for doctors .
OET test dates and fees FAQ

When are the OET test dates in 2026?
OET on paper runs on fixed Saturdays roughly every two weeks, with an Americas session on the Friday before each one. OET on Computer runs on many more dates, often Monday to Saturday in most weeks, depending on your country. The last 2026 paper sessions are Friday 18 December (Americas) and Saturday 19 December (Global).
How much does the OET exam cost?
The full OET test costs AU$587 in every mode. In the USA, OET on Computer and OET@Home cost US$455. A paper re-sit of one, two or three sub-tests costs AU$315, AU$415 or AU$515 after a full test, but not in the USA.
How long do OET results take?
Computer and OET@Home results can arrive in as little as 48 hours, and 95% of OET on Computer results are released within 6 calendar days. Paper results arrive from 13 days after the test, or from 5 days in India and the Philippines. OET describes these timeframes as indicative.
Are the 2027 OET test dates available?
Not yet. As of 2 November 2026, OET has not published any 2027 test dates. Check the official booking page, which lists each date with its booking deadline and results date.
Can I retake only one OET sub-test?
Only on paper, only after a full OET test, and not in the USA. Many regulators will not accept it: the NMC, Ahpra, the Medical Council of New Zealand and ECFMG all need all four sub-tests in each sitting.

## OET vs IELTS 2026 for Nurses and Doctors: Which Is Easier?

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-vs-ielts.html

OET vs IELTS for nurses and doctors: OET's official IELTS score comparison, format differences, which regulators accept each test and how to choose.

Test comparison
OET vs IELTS: Which Test Should Nurses and Doctors Take?
For nurses and doctors registering with a healthcare regulator, OET is usually the better fit: its Writing and Speaking tasks are written for your profession, and regulators such as the NMC, GMC and Ahpra accept it. IELTS tests general or academic English and is also used outside healthcare. In OET's own benchmarking, grade B (350–390) compares with IELTS 7.0.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026
Start the free placement test Check score requirements Ask on WhatsApp
At a glance OET grade B and IELTS
From OET's published benchmarking tables.
7.0 OET 350–390 (B) Compares with IELTS 7.0 and CEFR C1.
7.5 OET 400–440 (B) Compares with IELTS 7.5 and CEFR C1.
6.5 OET 300–340 (C+) Compares with IELTS 6.5 and CEFR B2.
OET or IELTS: the short answer
If you are a nurse, doctor or other health professional registering with a regulator that accepts OET, OET is usually the better fit. If you need a test outside healthcare, or your regulator does not list OET, IELTS may be the right choice.
Choose OET if…
you are registering as a health professional, your regulator accepts OET, and you would rather write a referral letter and role-play a patient conversation than discuss general academic topics.
Choose IELTS if…
you also need the score for purposes outside healthcare, your regulator does not list OET (for example the GDC for UK dentists), or you want a one-skill retake your regulator accepts.
Check first
the exact scores, sitting rules and test modes your regulator accepts. These differ more between regulators than between the two tests.
OET to IELTS score conversion
OET publishes its own benchmarking against IELTS and the CEFR. Grade B, the score most regulators ask for, sits at IELTS 7.0 to 7.5 and CEFR C1.
OET score (grade) IELTS band CEFR level
450–500 (A) 8.0–9.0 C2
400–440 (B) 7.5 C1
350–390 (B) 7.0 C1
300–340 (C+) 6.5 B2
250–290 (C) 6.0 B2
200–240 (C) 5.5 B2
0–190 (D and E) Below 5.5 Not shown in OET's table
Source: OET's published IELTS benchmarking and CEFR benchmarking , linked from OET results and scoring . Regulators set their own equivalences, and the NMC, for example, treats OET B with Writing C+ as equivalent to IELTS 7 with Writing 6.5. To check your own scores, use the OET score calculator .
How OET and IELTS differ
The biggest difference is content. OET tests the English you use at work in healthcare; IELTS tests general or academic English.
OET IELTS
Content Healthcare scenarios. Writing and Speaking are specific to your profession (12 professions); Listening and Reading are the same for all General or academic topics, not specific to healthcare
Writing One letter from case notes, such as a referral or discharge letter: 5 minutes reading time plus 40 minutes writing, 180–200 words Not profession-specific; check the official IELTS website for the current format
Speaking About 20 minutes: two role-plays with an interlocutor playing your patient, a relative or a carer Not profession-specific; check the official IELTS website
Listening and Reading Each has 42 questions in 3 parts; Reading takes 60 minutes, Listening about 40 minutes, using healthcare texts and recordings General or academic texts and recordings
Scores Each sub-test from 0 to 500 with grades A to E; no overall score Band scores
Delivery Paper, computer at a venue, OET@Home (OET@Home accepted by the NMC and GMC, not by Ahpra, NMBI, the GPhC or the HCPC) Check your regulator: the GDC accepts IELTS Online; NMBI does not accept IELTS online
Re-taking one skill Paper re-sit of single sub-tests after a full test, not in the USA; not accepted by the NMC, Ahpra, MCNZ or ECFMG IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted by Ahpra and the GDC
OET details from the OET Test Handbook 2026 and oet.com . For IELTS, always check the official IELTS website for the current format, fees and dates.
Which regulators accept OET and IELTS?
Both tests are widely accepted for healthcare registration, but the rules differ by regulator. These are the verified OET requirements for the most common destinations.
Regulator OET requirement IELTS
NMC (UK nurses and midwives) OET Nursing: B in Listening, Reading and Speaking; C+ in Writing Accepted; the NMC treats IELTS 7 with Writing 6.5 as equivalent. OET and IELTS cannot be combined
GMC (UK doctors) OET Medicine: B in all four sub-tests from the same, most recent sitting See the GMC's English language page
GPhC (UK pharmacists) OET Pharmacy: B in all four, one sitting; paper or computer only The GPhC calls OET B in all four equivalent to its IELTS requirement
GDC (UK dentists) Not on the GDC's routinely accepted list Accepted, including IELTS One Skill Retake and IELTS Online
Ahpra (Australia, all National Boards) Tests from 23 April 2026: Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350, Speaking 360 Accepted, including IELTS One Skill Retake; different providers cannot be combined
NMBI (Ireland nurses) OET Nursing: B in Listening, Reading and Speaking; C+ in Writing; one sitting Accepted test list on the NMBI page; NMBI does not accept IELTS online
ECFMG (USA, 2027 Pathways) OET Medicine: 350 in Listening, Reading and Speaking; 300 in Writing; one sitting on or after 1 January 2025 OET Medicine is the test named on ECFMG's Pathways page
For every regulator, the minimum scores, validity rules and accepted test modes are in the OET score requirements guide . Always confirm on the official page before you book.
Is OET easier than IELTS?
Neither test is easier for everyone, and we do not publish pass-rate comparisons we cannot verify. What matters is which test plays to your strengths.
Writing: OET asks for one letter from case notes, with a clear reader and purpose. Many clinicians find selecting and organising patient information more natural than writing an essay on a general topic. Our OET Writing tips explain how the letter is marked.
Speaking: OET Speaking is two role-plays with a patient, relative or carer. If you talk to patients every day, the scenarios feel familiar; the challenge is structure and patient-friendly language. See our OET Speaking tips .
Listening and Reading: OET uses healthcare recordings and texts. Medical vocabulary helps, but Reading Part A is a strict 15-minute scanning task that needs practice.
Re-sits: if your regulator accepts a single-skill retake, IELTS One Skill Retake can be an advantage. OET single sub-test re-sits are not accepted by the NMC, Ahpra, MCNZ or ECFMG.
Not sure where you stand? The free placement test gives an indicative CEFR level for each skill before you choose.
Can you combine OET and IELTS results?
Usually not. The NMC states that OET and IELTS cannot be combined, and Ahpra does not accept results from different test providers in one application. Some regulators let you combine two sittings of the same test, but the rules are strict. The NMC, for example, allows two OET sittings within 12 months, with no score below C+ (Writing C) in either.
Pick one test and plan to meet your requirement with it.
What does each test cost?
The full OET test costs AU$587 in every mode, or US$455 for OET on Computer and OET@Home in the USA. A paper re-sit of one, two or three OET sub-tests costs AU$315, AU$415 or AU$515 after a full test. See OET test dates and fees for rescheduling and re-marking costs.
IELTS fees vary by country and test centre, so check the official IELTS provider where you will sit the test. Remember to compare the cost of a possible re-sit as well as the first attempt.
OET vs IELTS FAQ
Quick answers for healthcare professionals choosing a test. More exam questions are on the full OET FAQ page .
Is OET easier than IELTS?
Neither test is easier for everyone. Many nurses and doctors find OET more familiar because the Writing and Speaking tasks use their own profession, such as a referral letter or a patient role-play. IELTS uses general or academic topics. The right choice is the test your regulator accepts that best matches your strengths.
What IELTS score is equal to OET grade B?
In OET's published benchmarking, an OET score of 350 to 390 (grade B) compares with IELTS 7.0, and 400 to 440 (also grade B) compares with IELTS 7.5. OET C+ (300 to 340) compares with IELTS 6.5.
Does the NMC accept both OET and IELTS?
Yes. The NMC accepts OET Nursing with B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing, which it treats as equivalent to IELTS 7 with 6.5 in Writing. You cannot combine an OET result with an IELTS result.
Can I combine OET and IELTS results?
Usually not. The NMC does not allow OET and IELTS to be combined, and Ahpra does not accept results from different test providers in one application. Plan to meet your requirement with one test.
Which test should dentists take for the UK?
Check the GDC first. OET is not on the GDC's list of routinely accepted English evidence, while IELTS is, including IELTS One Skill Retake and IELTS Online.

Take the free placement test, then choose profession-specific OET preparation with feedback on your letters and role-plays.

## OET for ECFMG 2027 Pathways: Scores, Deadlines & MyIntealth

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-for-ecfmg.html

OET for ECFMG 2027 Pathways: required OET Medicine scores, one-sitting rule, MyIntealth ID, OET@Home limits and the deadlines for the 2027 Match.

OET for ECFMG
OET for ECFMG Certification: 2027 Pathways Guide
For the 2027 Pathways, ECFMG asks for OET Medicine with at least 350 in Listening, Reading and Speaking and 300 in Writing, all in one sitting taken on or after 1 January 2025. Results released from 14 May 2026 reach ECFMG through your MyIntealth ID, and ECFMG must receive them by 31 January 2027.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026
Checked against official regulator pages on 24 October 2026. Rules change — confirm before you book.
OET course for doctors Ask on WhatsApp
Deadlines
Key dates for the 2027 Match
01 25 Nov 2026 Booking closes for the last Global paper session.
02 19 Dec 2026 Last Global paper session; results scheduled for 5 January 2027.
03 31 Jan 2027 ECFMG must receive your scores from OET.
Who needs OET for ECFMG?
International medical graduates on the 2027 Pathways need OET Medicine.
The OET Medicine requirement applies to international medical graduates applying through the ECFMG Certification Pathways for the 2027 Match. The test checks the clinical communication skills you will use with patients and colleagues in US residency, so ECFMG treats it as part of the communication requirement. Use the USA pathway guide for the wider route from ECFMG Certification to residency and state licensure.
Only OET Medicine counts for this purpose. The Nursing, Pharmacy and other profession versions are not accepted for ECFMG.
What OET score does ECFMG require?
Three sub-tests at 350 and Writing at 300, all from one sitting.
Sub-test Minimum score Grade
Listening 350 B
Reading 350 B
Writing 300 C+
Speaking 350 B
One test administration: all four scores must come from the same sitting. If you miss the minimum in any sub-test, you retake all four.
Date: the passing result must be from a test taken on or after 1 January 2025.
Retakes: ECFMG sets no limit on the number of attempts.
Source: ECFMG: OET Medicine for the 2027 Pathways (last updated 14 May 2026).
Enter your own scores in the OET score calculator to see whether they meet the ECFMG minimums.
Which OET test mode can you use?
Paper and computer at a venue are the default; OET@Home is the exception.
OET on paper: all four sub-tests on one day at a test centre. Paper bookings close 24 days before the test date.
OET on computer: Listening, Reading and Writing at a venue, with Speaking usually taken online on a different day. Bookings close 7 days before the test, and results can arrive in as little as 48 hours, with 95% released within 6 calendar days.
OET@Home: accepted by ECFMG only if there is no physical test venue in your country. You must sit it in the country you booked and show proof of presence at check-in.
OET lists the full test at AU$587, or US$455 for the computer and at-home tests in the USA. See OET test dates and fees for booking details.
How do OET scores reach ECFMG?
Your MyIntealth ID links your OET result to your ECFMG record.
From 14 May 2026, OET sends Medicine results to ECFMG using your MyIntealth ID. If your results are released on or after that date, make sure OET has your MyIntealth ID, not your USMLE ID.
If your MyIntealth ID or date of birth does not match, your results are not released to ECFMG.
Results released before 14 May 2026 under a USMLE ID are matched within 3 business days.
Allow 3 business days for a passing result to update in your Pathways application.
Source: ECFMG OET page .
What are the deadlines for the 2027 Match?
Work back from 31 January 2027 and leave room for one retake.
Date What happens
Tue 24 Nov 2026 Booking closes for the last Americas paper session
Wed 25 Nov 2026 Booking closes for the last Global paper session
Fri 18 Dec 2026 Last Americas paper session (Nursing and Medicine)
Sat 19 Dec 2026 Last Global paper session (Nursing and Medicine)
Tue 5 Jan 2027 Scheduled results for the 18 and 19 December paper sessions
31 Jan 2027 ECFMG must have received your scores from OET; Pathways application and documents due (US Eastern Time)
ECFMG advises taking OET Medicine on or before the last scheduled test date in December 2026. Results that arrive later are still processed but may be too late for the 2027 Match. ECFMG says results are typically released about 10 business days after the test. Computer dates vary by country, so check the official OET date finder for sessions near you.
Step-by-step checklist
Follow this order to avoid a result that arrives too late or never reaches ECFMG.
01 Get your MyIntealth ID Create or confirm your MyIntealth account and check your name and date of birth.
02 Choose the test mode Paper or computer at a venue; OET@Home only if your country has no venue.
03 Book early Paper closes 24 days before the test, computer 7 days before. Make sure OET has your MyIntealth ID.
04 Prepare Medicine Writing and Speaking These two sub-tests decide most retakes for doctors.
05 Sit all four sub-tests One administration; all four scores must meet the minimums together.
06 Track the result Check that your passing scores appear in your Pathways application.
Which mistakes delay ECFMG results?
Most problems are administrative, not linguistic, and each one can cost you the 2027 Match.
Using your USMLE ID: results released from 14 May 2026 need your MyIntealth ID; the wrong ID means the scores do not reach ECFMG.
A mismatched date of birth: if your details do not match, OET cannot release your results to ECFMG.
Booking OET@Home with a venue nearby: ECFMG accepts OET@Home only when your country has no test venue.
Counting on two sittings: ECFMG needs all four minimums in one test administration; a strong Writing score from an earlier sitting cannot be carried over.
Using an old result: the passing test must be taken on or after 1 January 2025.
Leaving no time for a retake: paper bookings close 24 days before the test and results can take around two weeks, so the last December dates leave no room to try again before 31 January 2027.
How should doctors prepare for OET Medicine?
Listening and Reading are the same for every profession; Writing and Speaking are where doctors usually need targeted work.
Writing: referral letters
Medicine Writing is usually a letter to a specialist or GP who will take over care. Select only the case notes the reader needs, state the purpose early and make the request clear. Practise with the OET Medicine writing sample .
Speaking: patient conversations
Role-plays include explaining a diagnosis, discussing treatment options and responding to a worried patient. Structure, empathy and checking understanding are marked alongside language.
Get feedback before you book
A retake means all four sub-tests again, so check Writing with OET writing correction and follow the OET course for doctors .
FAQ
What OET score do I need for ECFMG?
For the 2027 Pathways, ECFMG asks for OET Medicine with at least 350 in Listening, Reading and Speaking and 300 in Writing, all in one test administration taken on or after 1 January 2025.
Can I use OET@Home for ECFMG?
Only if there is no physical OET test venue in your country. Otherwise you need to take OET Medicine on paper or on computer at a venue.
What is the MyIntealth ID used for?
If your OET Medicine results are released on or after 14 May 2026, you must give OET your MyIntealth ID, not your USMLE ID, so your scores reach ECFMG. If the ID or date of birth does not match, the results are not released to ECFMG.
When should I take OET for the 2027 Match?
ECFMG advises taking OET Medicine on or before the last scheduled test date in December 2026. ECFMG must receive your scores directly from OET by 31 January 2027.
What happens if I miss the score in one sub-test?
You must retake all four sub-tests in a new test administration. ECFMG does not limit the number of retakes, and OET does not offer single sub-test resits in the USA.
Aiming for the 2027 Match?
There is little room for a retake before 31 January 2027. Check your level with the free placement test , then prepare Writing and Speaking with the OET course for doctors .

## OET Writing Sample for Nurses: Model Discharge Letter

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-writing-sample-nursing.html

Free OET writing sample for nurses: realistic discharge case notes, a model letter to the district nurse and a criterion-by-criterion explanation.

OET Nursing Writing
OET Writing Sample for Nurses: Discharge Letter
This OET writing sample for nurses gives you a complete practice task: realistic discharge case notes, the writing instructions, a model letter to a district nurse and a criterion-by-criterion explanation of why it works. Write your own letter first, then compare.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026
Get your letter marked
Read the case notes
Ask on WhatsApp
45 min 5 minutes reading plus 40 minutes writing
180–200 Words in the body of the letter
6 Writing criteria the examiner uses
How to use this sample
Write first, compare second.
Reading a model letter teaches far less than writing your own and then comparing. Use the timings below and treat it like the real test.
01 Read the case notes Five minutes, no writing, just planning.
02 Write your letter Forty minutes, about 180–200 words in the body.
03 Compare and get marked Check the model answer, then send your letter for correction.
What is the OET Writing task for nurses?
OET Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. For nurses, the letter is usually a discharge, transfer or referral letter to the health professional who will continue the patient's care. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
What the examiner checks Six criteria: Purpose, Content, Conciseness & Clarity, Genre & Style, Organisation & Layout, and Language.
Case notes: discharge of Mrs Joan Whitfield
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the district nurse needs before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mrs Joan Whitfield
DOB: 14/03/1952 (74 y.o.)
Address: 27 Elm Grove, Westbridge
Admitted: 12/10/2026; discharge: 19/10/2026
Ward 6, Westbridge General Hospital
Diagnosis: cellulitis L lower leg; venous leg ulcer (2 cm) L medial ankle
Social background Widowed, lives alone in ground-floor flat
Daughter lives 20 mins away, visits twice weekly; aware of discharge
Retired teacher; enjoys gardening (scratched leg while gardening 2/52 before admission)
Non-smoker; occasional glass of wine
Medical history T2DM (2015): metformin 500 mg BD
Hypertension (2018): amlodipine 5 mg OD
Osteoarthritis both knees
Appendicectomy (1980)
NKDA
Nursing notes 12/10: admitted via ED, L lower leg red, hot, swollen; temp 38.4°C; BGL 14.2 mmol/L; IV antibiotics commenced
14/10: temp within normal limits; redness reducing; pain 3/10 (from 6/10) with regular paracetamol
15/10: changed to oral flucloxacillin
16/10: tissue viability nurse review: ulcer cleaned, non-adherent dressing applied; change every 2 days
17/10: BGL 6–9 mmol/L; diabetes nurse: pt understands self-monitoring but occasionally forgets evening metformin
18/10: mobilising with walking frame; physio: mild unsteadiness, falls risk
Pt anxious about managing dressing alone; keen to go home
Discharge plan Flucloxacillin 500 mg PO QID until 24/10
Continue metformin 500 mg BD, amlodipine 5 mg OD
Paracetamol 1 g PO QID PRN for pain
District nurse: dressing change every 2 days; monitor ulcer and signs of infection; check BGL diary; reinforce medication adherence
Walking frame supplied; OT home assessment 22/10
GP review in 1/52
Writing task
You are the charge nurse on Ward 6, Westbridge General Hospital. Mrs Whitfield is being discharged home today. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Ms Sarah Patel, District Nurse, Westbridge Community Nursing Team, 4 Mill Lane, Westbridge, who will continue Mrs Whitfield's care at home.
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences.
Do not use note form.
Use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task.
Model answer: discharge letter to the district nurse
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Ms Sarah Patel
District Nurse
Westbridge Community Nursing Team
4 Mill Lane
Westbridge
19 October 2026
Dear Ms Patel,
Re: Mrs Joan Whitfield, DOB 14/03/1952
I am writing to request your continued care of Mrs Whitfield, aged 74, who is being discharged home today after treatment for cellulitis of her left lower leg. She will need regular dressing changes for a small leg ulcer and support with her diabetes management.
Mrs Whitfield was admitted on 12 October with a red, swollen left leg and a fever. Her condition improved with intravenous antibiotics, and she is now taking oral flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily until 24 October. A 2 cm venous ulcer on her left medial ankle has been cleaned and covered with a non-adherent dressing.
Could you please change this dressing every two days and monitor for signs of recurrent infection, such as spreading redness or fever? In addition, she has type 2 diabetes and occasionally forgets her evening metformin, so I would be grateful if you could review her glucose diary and encourage adherence.
Please note that she lives alone, mobilises with a walking frame and is at risk of falls. An occupational therapy home assessment is booked for 22 October. She is anxious about managing her dressing, so reassurance would be appreciated.
Please contact me if you require further information.
Yours sincerely,
Charge Nurse
Ward 6, Westbridge General Hospital
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 198 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The purpose is stated in the first paragraph: continued care at home, with the two needs (dressing changes and diabetes support) named straight away. The reader knows within two sentences why the letter exists and what will be asked.
Content
Every included note changes what the district nurse does: the antibiotic end date, the ulcer and dressing plan, the missed evening metformin, the falls risk and the occupational therapy visit. Background that does not affect home care, such as the old appendicectomy, is left out.
Conciseness & Clarity
The hospital stay is summarised in two sentences instead of a day-by-day diary. Daily temperatures and pain scores were useful on the ward but do not help the reader, so they become “improved with intravenous antibiotics”.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional and polite, written nurse to nurse. Requests use “Could you please” and “I would be grateful if”, and note-form abbreviations such as BGL, QID and BD are written out in full.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose first, then a brief admission summary, then the actions requested, then social and safety information. Each paragraph has one job, and the recipient's details, date and Re: line follow standard letter layout.
Language
Short, accurate sentences with controlled tenses: past for the admission, present for her current condition and future for the plan. Medicine names and doses are copied exactly from the notes.
Included because the reader needs it Diagnosis and the reason for discharge
Antibiotic, dose and end date (24 October)
Ulcer size, site and dressing frequency
Missed evening metformin and the glucose diary
Lives alone, walking frame and falls risk
Occupational therapy home assessment on 22 October
Her anxiety about managing the dressing
Left out because it does not change the next step Retired teacher and the gardening history
Appendicectomy (1980) and knee osteoarthritis
Daily temperatures, pain scores and the admission glucose of 14.2 mmol/L
Wine intake and non-smoking status
Unchanged regular medicines and paracetamol as required
Daughter's visits (a short mention is acceptable if you have words left)
Common mistakes in OET discharge letters
These errors cost marks in discharge letters again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Starting with the patient's life story instead of the reason for writing.
Copying the day-by-day ward notes in date order.
Listing every regular medicine, including unchanged ones, without saying what the nurse should do.
Forgetting the antibiotic end date or the dressing frequency, the two details the district nurse acts on first.
Writing requests as statements, such as “The dressing will be changed”, so the reader is unsure who is responsible.
Using note-form abbreviations such as BD, QID or BGL in the letter.
Going well beyond 200 words because irrelevant social details were included.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips , see how the OET course for nurses trains letter selection, or try the OET writing sample for doctors . Results from candidates who prepared with this method are on the success stories page.
Write your own version and get it marked
Write your own letter for this task in 40 minutes, then send it for OET writing correction . Each corrected letter comes back with an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp. If you are not sure your English is ready for OET yet, start with the free placement test .
Get your letter marked Writing assessment packages Free placement test
OET nursing writing sample FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET nursing letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
Who do nurses write to in OET Writing?
Usually another health professional who will continue the patient's care, such as a district or community nurse, a GP, a care home nurse or a rehabilitation team. Sometimes the reader is a carer or family member, which changes the tone and the amount of medical language.
Should I include every medication in a discharge letter?
No. Include new medicines, changed doses and anything the reader must give, monitor or stop. Long-standing medicines that have not changed can usually be left out or mentioned briefly if they matter to the care plan.
Can I get my OET nursing letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.

Write this task under time, send it for correction and get an estimated score with voice-note feedback on exactly what to change.
Get your letter marked Message on WhatsApp

01 Write under time Five minutes reading, forty minutes writing.
02 Compare with the model Check purpose, selection and your final request.
03 Get it marked An estimated score and voice-note feedback on what to fix.

What is the OET Writing task for doctors?
OET Medicine Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. The letter is usually a referral to a specialist or a discharge or transfer letter to a GP or colleague. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
