Case notes: referral of Mr David Hartley
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the cardiologist needs before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mr David Hartley
DOB: 02/07/1968 (58 y.o.)
Address: 15 Station Road, Westbridge
Occupation: warehouse supervisor (on feet most of day, climbs stairs between floors)
Consultation: 20/10/2026, Westbridge Medical Centre
Social background Married, 2 adult children (left home)
Smoker for 30 yrs, currently 10 cigs/day (previously 20/day)
Alcohol approx. 14 units/week
Watches football; little regular exercise
Medical history Hypertension (2019): ramipril 5 mg OD
Hypercholesterolaemia (2021): atorvastatin 20 mg nocte
GORD (2017): omeprazole 20 mg OD, symptoms well controlled
R knee arthroscopy (2010)
Family hx: father MI aged 61; mother T2DM
NKDA
Presenting complaint 3/52 central chest tightness on exertion (stairs at work, walking uphill)
Lasts 3–5 min, relieved by rest; occasionally radiates to L arm
Frequency increasing: now 3–4 times/week
No pain at rest, no SOB at rest, no palpitations, no syncope
Pt anxious: “worried it's my heart like Dad”; keen to keep working
Examination and investigations BP 148/92 mmHg, HR 78 bpm regular, BMI 31
Heart sounds normal, chest clear, no peripheral oedema
Resting ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute changes
Bloods: FBC NAD, HbA1c 41 mmol/mol, total cholesterol 5.8 mmol/L, renal function normal
Assessment and plan Suspected stable angina
Started aspirin 75 mg OD and GTN spray PRN; explained use and emergency action if pain at rest or not relieved
Smoking cessation advice; referred to stop-smoking service
Refer: Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic for urgent assessment and further investigation
GP review in 2/52
Writing task
You are a GP at Westbridge Medical Centre. You saw Mr Hartley today. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter of referral to Dr Helen Morris, Consultant Cardiologist, Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic, Westbridge General Hospital, Hospital Road, Westbridge, requesting urgent assessment.
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences.
Do not use note form.
Use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task.
Model answer: referral letter to the cardiologist
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Dr Helen Morris
Consultant Cardiologist
Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic
Westbridge General Hospital
Hospital Road
Westbridge
20 October 2026
Dear Dr Morris,
Re: Mr David Hartley, DOB 02/07/1968
I am writing to refer Mr Hartley, a 58-year-old warehouse supervisor, for urgent assessment of suspected stable angina.
Mr Hartley presented with a three-week history of central chest tightness on exertion, such as when climbing stairs at work. The episodes last three to five minutes, are relieved by rest and occasionally radiate to his left arm. They have become more frequent and now occur three to four times a week, although he has had no pain at rest.
His cardiovascular risk factors include hypertension, treated with ramipril 5 mg daily, and hypercholesterolaemia, for which he takes atorvastatin 20 mg nightly. He has smoked for 30 years, and his father had a myocardial infarction at 61. On examination, his blood pressure was 148/92 mmHg and his BMI was 31. A resting ECG showed sinus rhythm with no acute changes. His full blood count and HbA1c were normal, but his total cholesterol was 5.8 mmol/L.
I have started aspirin 75 mg daily and a GTN spray as required, and referred him to the stop-smoking service. He is anxious given his father's history.
I would be grateful if you could assess him and arrange further investigations as appropriate.
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
General Practitioner, Westbridge Medical Centre
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 195 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The first sentence names the request (urgent assessment) and the working diagnosis (suspected stable angina), so the cardiologist knows the priority before reading any history.
Content
The letter keeps the features that make angina likely and that a cardiologist needs to plan tests: the exertional pattern, relief by rest, radiation, increasing frequency, risk factors, examination findings, the ECG and the treatment already started.
Conciseness & Clarity
Risk factors are grouped into one paragraph instead of being scattered through the letter. Negative findings are summarised as “no pain at rest” rather than listing every symptom he does not have.
Genre & Style
Written doctor to doctor, so medical terms such as myocardial infarction and sinus rhythm are appropriate, but note-form abbreviations such as SOB, NAD and OD are written out or avoided.
Organisation & Layout
Reason for referral, presenting complaint, background and findings, management so far, then the request. This is the order a specialist reads a referral in, and each paragraph has a single focus.
Language
Precise verbs (presented, relieved, radiate, started) and controlled tenses keep the timeline clear: past for the history, present perfect for what has been done and a polite conditional for the request.
Included because the reader needs it Age, occupation, suspected diagnosis and urgency
Exertional pattern, duration, relief by rest, radiation and frequency
Hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia and their treatment
Smoking history and father's MI at 61
Blood pressure, BMI, ECG and the relevant blood results
Aspirin, GTN spray and the stop-smoking referral
His anxiety about his father's history
Left out because it does not change the next step GORD and omeprazole (well controlled and not part of the request)
Knee arthroscopy (2010) and his mother's diabetes
Alcohol intake, family details and leisure activities
Address and the full list of negative symptoms
Normal heart sounds, clear chest and no oedema (a short phrase is acceptable if you have words left)
The two-week GP review, which is not the cardiologist's concern
Common mistakes in OET referral letters
These errors cost marks in Medicine referral letters again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Hiding the request in the last paragraph, so the specialist does not see the urgency.
Listing every negative symptom instead of the pattern that suggests angina.
Writing the history in the same order as the notes instead of grouping the risk factors.
Leaving out the medicines already started, which the cardiologist needs to know before testing.
Including the GP's own follow-up plan, which does not help the specialist.
Using abbreviations from the notes, such as SOB, NAD, OD or PRN.
Using casual or dramatic language, such as “very worried” or “please see ASAP”.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips , see how the OET course for doctors trains referral letters, or try the OET writing sample for nurses . Results from candidates who prepared with this method are on the success stories page.
Write your own version and get it marked
Write your own referral letter for this task in 40 minutes, then send it for OET writing correction . Each corrected letter comes back with an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp. If you are not sure your English is ready for OET yet, start with the free placement test .
Get your letter marked Writing assessment packages Free placement test
OET medicine writing sample FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET referral letter be?
Aim for about 180–200 words in the body of the letter. Specialists want a clear reason for referral and the findings that support it, so a focused letter usually scores better than a longer one.
What should the first paragraph of an OET referral letter say?
It should state who the patient is, why you are referring them and how urgently, in one or two sentences. The reader should know the request before reading any history.
Do I need to include normal test results?
Include normal results only when they help the reader, such as a normal resting ECG in suspected angina. Leave out normal findings that do not change the specialist's assessment.
Can I get my OET referral letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.

Case notes: medication review for Mr Peter Lawson
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the GP needs to know and do before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mr Peter Lawson
DOB: 02/06/1955 (71 y.o.)
Address: 8 Willow Close, Northfield
GP: Dr Helen Carter, Northfield Medical Centre
Seen at Riverside Pharmacy for medication review (pt request): 20/10/2026
Social background Lives with wife; wife willing to help with medicines
Retired bus driver; walks dog daily
Poor eyesight: difficulty reading small print on labels
Non-smoker; occasional alcohol
Medical history and medicines Hypertension (2014): amlodipine 10 mg OD (increased from 5 mg, 08/2026); ramipril 5 mg OD

NKDA
Pharmacy notes 20/10 Bilateral ankle swelling since amlodipine dose increase (approx. 6 wks); shoes tight by evening
No breathlessness or chest pain reported
Home BP (own monitor): 128–135/80–84 mmHg
Medicines kept in original boxes; confused by different dose times; 'too many boxes'
Admits missing evening atorvastatin 2–3 times/week
Has occasionally taken ramipril twice in one day
Explained amlodipine can cause ankle swelling; advised not to stop any medicine without GP advice
Large-print medication chart provided
Plan Letter to GP: review of antihypertensive treatment; consider simplifying regimen (e.g. atorvastatin in the morning)
Pt consented to GP being contacted
Pt to book GP appointment within 2/52
Pharmacy follow-up phone call in 1/12
Writing task
You are the pharmacist at Riverside Pharmacy, 12 High Street, Northfield. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Dr Helen Carter, Mr Lawson's GP, at Northfield Medical Centre, 3 Station Road, Northfield, outlining your concerns and requesting a review of his medication.

Northfield
20 October 2026
Dear Dr Carter,
Re: Mr Peter Lawson, DOB 02/06/1955
I am writing to request a review of the medication of Mr Lawson, aged 71, whom I saw today for a medication review. He has developed ankle swelling and is having difficulty following his regimen.
Since his amlodipine was increased from 5 mg to 10 mg daily in August, Mr Lawson has noticed swelling of both ankles, which is worse in the evenings. He denies breathlessness or chest pain, and his home blood pressure readings have been 128–135/80–84 mmHg.
In addition, he finds his medicines confusing, as they are taken at different times of the day. He admits missing his evening atorvastatin two or three times a week and has occasionally taken his ramipril twice in one day.
I would be grateful if you could review his antihypertensive treatment in view of the ankle swelling and consider simplifying his regimen, for example by moving atorvastatin to the morning. I have advised him not to stop any medicine before seeing you and have given him a large-print medication chart, as his eyesight is poor.
Mr Lawson has agreed to this referral and will book an appointment within two weeks. Please contact me if you require further information.
Yours sincerely,
Pharmacist
Riverside Pharmacy
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 196 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The opening paragraph asks for a medication review and names both problems: ankle swelling and difficulty following the regimen. The GP knows straight away what the letter wants and why it matters.
Content
Every included note supports the request: the dose increase and timing of the swelling, the relevant negatives (no breathlessness or chest pain), the home blood pressure, the missed and doubled doses, and what the pharmacist has already done. Medicines that are stable and unrelated, such as allopurinol, are left out.
Conciseness & Clarity
The review is summarised in four short paragraphs. Patient quotes and storage details become one clear point: the regimen is confusing because doses are taken at different times.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional, pharmacist to prescriber. Recommendations are offered for the GP to consider, using “I would be grateful if” and “for example”, so the prescribing decision stays with the doctor.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose first, then the side effect, then the adherence problem, then the request and the actions already taken, then consent and follow-up. Standard letter layout with the recipient, date and Re: line.
Language
Accurate tenses (present perfect for the swelling that started after the dose change, past for what he admitted), precise doses and units copied from the notes, and no note-form abbreviations such as OD or ON.
Included because the reader needs it Reason for writing: review of medication
Amlodipine increase from 5 mg to 10 mg in August and the ankle swelling since then
No breathlessness or chest pain
Home blood pressure readings
Missed evening atorvastatin and the doubled ramipril doses
Suggested review and simplification for the GP to consider
Advice given, large-print chart and poor eyesight
Consent and appointment within two weeks
Left out because it does not change the next step Retired bus driver and dog walking
Gout history and allopurinol (stable, unrelated)
Hip osteoarthritis and paracetamol as required
Alcohol and smoking status
Exact wording of the patient's comments
Pharmacy follow-up phone call (useful but not something the GP must act on)
Common mistakes in OET pharmacy letters
These errors cost marks in pharmacy letters to prescribers again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Telling the GP what to prescribe instead of suggesting a review for the GP to decide.
Listing every medicine and dose, including stable ones that have nothing to do with the problem.
Leaving out relevant negatives, such as no breathlessness, that help the GP judge how urgent the swelling is.
Forgetting to say what the pharmacist has already done and advised.
Missing the safety point: the occasional double dose of ramipril.
Using note-form abbreviations such as OD, ON and PRN in the letter.
Forgetting to mention that the patient has consented to the GP being contacted.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips or see the OET courses , including the pharmacy course. Try the other practice letters too: the nursing discharge letter , the nursing transfer letter , the medicine referral letter , the pharmacy letter to a GP and the physiotherapy discharge letter .

OET pharmacy writing sample FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET pharmacy letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
Who do pharmacists write to in OET Writing?
Usually a GP or another prescriber about a medication problem, such as a side effect, an interaction, poor adherence or a dosing concern. Some tasks ask you to write to a patient, a carer or a manufacturer, which changes the reader and the tone.
Can a pharmacist recommend changes to a GP in the letter?
Yes, but as a suggestion for the prescriber to consider, not as an instruction. Phrases such as “I would be grateful if you could review” keep the tone professional and leave the prescribing decision with the GP.
Can I get my OET pharmacy letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.

OET Writing Sample for Physiotherapists: Discharge Letter

What is the OET Writing task for physiotherapists?
OET Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. For physiotherapists, the letter is usually a referral or discharge letter to another physiotherapist, a GP or a specialist who will continue the patient's rehabilitation. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
What the examiner checks Six criteria: Purpose, Content, Conciseness & Clarity, Genre & Style, Organisation & Layout, and Language.
Case notes: discharge of Mrs Linda Hughes
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the community physiotherapist needs before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mrs Linda Hughes
DOB: 11/09/1958 (68 y.o.)
Address: 15 Orchard Way, Eastfield
Admitted: 01/10/2026 for elective R total knee replacement (osteoarthritis)
Discharge: 06/10/2026; Orthopaedic Ward 3, Eastfield Hospital
Social background Lives with husband in two-storey house; bedroom upstairs; rail on one side of stairs
Husband supportive, drives
Retired librarian; enjoys swimming
Goals: walk to local shops (approx. 500 m) and return to swimming
Medical history Osteoarthritis both knees (L knee mild symptoms)
Hypertension: amlodipine 5 mg OD
BMI 31
NKDA
Physiotherapy notes 02/10 (day 1): mobilised with walking frame; R knee flexion 45°, lacks 15° extension; pain 6/10 on movement
03/10: progressed to 2 elbow crutches; flexion 65°
05/10: stairs practised with 1 rail + 1 crutch, safe and independent; flexion 85°, lacks 5° extension; pain 3/10 with analgesia
06/10: independent indoors and outdoors (short distances) with 2 crutches
Home exercise programme taught: straight leg raises, heel slides, knee bends; completing 3 times daily; ice 15 mins after exercise for swelling
Pt anxious about falling when going to the toilet at night
OT: raised toilet seat and bed lever supplied
Discharge plan Continue 2 elbow crutches
Community physiotherapy: progress range of movement (target flexion 110°+), strengthening and gait; reduce walking aid when appropriate
Orthopaedic outpatient review 12/11/2026
Wound care and staple removal arranged with practice nurse
Writing task
You are the physiotherapist on Orthopaedic Ward 3, Eastfield Hospital. Mrs Hughes is being discharged home today. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Mr James Ward, Community Physiotherapist, Eastfield Health Centre, 10 Park Road, Eastfield, who will continue her rehabilitation.

Model answer: physiotherapy discharge letter
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Mr James Ward
Community Physiotherapist
Eastfield Health Centre
10 Park Road
Eastfield
6 October 2026
Dear Mr Ward,
Re: Mrs Linda Hughes, DOB 11/09/1958
I am writing to refer Mrs Hughes, aged 68, for continued physiotherapy following her right total knee replacement on 1 October. She is being discharged home today and requires ongoing rehabilitation to regain movement, strength and walking ability.
Mrs Hughes has made good progress. Her knee flexion has improved from 45 to 85 degrees, although she still lacks 5 degrees of full extension, and her pain has reduced to 3/10 with analgesia. She walks independently over short distances with two elbow crutches and can manage stairs using one rail and one crutch.
She has been taught a home exercise programme, including straight leg raises, heel slides and knee bends, which she completes three times a day, followed by ice to control swelling.
Could you please progress her range of movement and strengthening and reduce her walking aid when appropriate? Her goals are to walk to her local shops, about 500 metres away, and to return to swimming. She is anxious about falling at night, so advice on safe mobility would be appreciated. Her orthopaedic review is on 12 November.
Please contact me if you require further information.
Yours sincerely,
Physiotherapist
Orthopaedic Ward 3, Eastfield Hospital
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 187 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The first paragraph states the referral, the operation and date, and the three rehabilitation aims. The community physiotherapist knows immediately why the patient is being referred.
Content
The letter gives the reader a clear baseline: current range of movement, pain, walking aid, stairs and the home exercise programme. The goals and the night-time anxiety help plan treatment. Day-by-day measurements are reduced to the starting and current figures.
Conciseness & Clarity
Five days of ward notes become one progress paragraph. Information that belongs to other professionals, such as wound care, is left out because the physiotherapist does not act on it.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional and collegial, physiotherapist to physiotherapist. The request is a polite question, and clinical measurements are written in full sentences rather than notes.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose, then progress, then the exercise programme, then the requested treatment with goals and follow-up. Each paragraph has one job, and the letter follows standard layout.
Language
Comparatives show progress clearly (“has improved from 45 to 85 degrees”), and the present tense describes her current function. Units and numbers match the case notes exactly.
Included because the reader needs it Right total knee replacement on 1 October and discharge today
Knee flexion 45 to 85 degrees and the 5-degree extension lag
Pain 3/10 with analgesia
Two elbow crutches and safe on stairs with one rail and one crutch
Home exercise programme and ice for swelling
Goals: shops about 500 metres away and swimming
Anxiety about falling at night
Orthopaedic review on 12 November
Left out because it does not change the next step Retired librarian
Mild symptoms in the left knee
Hypertension and amlodipine
BMI
Each day's separate measurements
Wound care and staple removal (arranged with the practice nurse)
Raised toilet seat and bed lever (a short mention is acceptable if you have words left)
Common mistakes in OET physiotherapy letters
These errors cost marks in physiotherapy discharge letters again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Copying every day's range-of-movement figures instead of giving the starting and current values.
Forgetting the patient's functional goals, which the next physiotherapist needs to plan treatment.
Including wound care, blood pressure or other details the reader will not act on.
Describing the exercise programme without saying how often it is done.
Writing the request as a vague statement instead of a clear question to the reader.
Leaving out the follow-up appointment date.
Using note-form shorthand such as “2 x crutches” or “ROM” in the letter.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips or see the OET courses , including the physiotherapy course. Try the other practice letters too: the nursing discharge letter , the nursing transfer letter , the medicine referral letter , the pharmacy letter to a GP and the physiotherapy discharge letter .

OET physiotherapy writing sample FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET physiotherapy letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
Who do physiotherapists write to in OET Writing?
Usually another physiotherapist, a GP, a specialist or a rehabilitation team who will continue the patient's care. Some tasks ask you to write to a patient or carer, which changes the tone and the amount of technical language.
Should I include every measurement in a physiotherapy letter?
No. Give the starting and current figures that show progress, plus anything the reader needs to plan treatment. Copying every day's measurements makes the letter long without helping the reader.

What is an OET nursing transfer letter?
OET Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. A transfer letter hands over a patient's ongoing care to nurses in another setting, such as a care home, rehabilitation unit or another ward, so it focuses on the care the receiving team must provide from day one. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
What the examiner checks Six criteria: Purpose, Content, Conciseness & Clarity, Genre & Style, Organisation & Layout, and Language.
Case notes: transfer of Mr Arthur Bennett
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the care home nurse needs before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mr Arthur Bennett
DOB: 17/04/1944 (82 y.o.)
Admitted: 03/10/2026; transfer: 24/10/2026
Stroke Unit, Hillcrest General Hospital
Diagnosis: L ischaemic stroke: R-sided weakness, mild expressive dysphasia
Social background Widower (wife died 2023); previously lived alone in a bungalow, independent
Son, Michael, lives 2 hrs away; next of kin; plans to visit at weekends
Retired engineer; enjoys radio news
Medical history Hypertension (2010): amlodipine 5 mg OD (continued)
Osteoarthritis
Cataract surgery (2018)
NKDA
Nursing notes 04/10: SLT assessment: dysphagia; soft & bite-sized diet (IDDSI level 6) and mildly thick fluids (IDDSI level 2); sit fully upright for meals and 30 mins after; supervise at meals
10/10: walks short distances with walking frame + assistance of 1; transfers with assistance of 1
R arm weakness: needs help cutting food and with buttons
12/10: grade 1 pressure area on sacrum; resolved 18/10 with 3-hourly repositioning and pressure-relieving mattress
Mild expressive dysphasia: word-finding difficulty; understanding good; responds well to short questions and extra time
Continent with prompting every 2–3 hrs
Mood low at times
Transfer plan New medicines: clopidogrel 75 mg OD, atorvastatin 80 mg ON; medication chart and 7-day supply sent
Continue 3-hourly repositioning and pressure-relieving mattress
Community stroke team (physio and OT) to visit weekly
SLT review 2/52; stroke clinic 6/52 (appointments in discharge summary)
Writing task
You are the nurse in charge of the Stroke Unit at Hillcrest General Hospital. Mr Bennett is being transferred to a nursing home today. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Ms Grace Miller, Nurse in Charge, Oakwood Nursing Home, 22 Beech Road, Hillcrest, who will take over his care.
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences.
Do not use note form.
Use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task.
Model answer: transfer letter to the care home nurse
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Ms Grace Miller
Nurse in Charge
Oakwood Nursing Home
22 Beech Road
Hillcrest
24 October 2026
Dear Ms Miller,
Re: Mr Arthur Bennett, DOB 17/04/1944
I am writing to hand over the care of Mr Bennett, aged 82, who is being transferred to your nursing home today following a left-sided ischaemic stroke on 3 October. He requires support with eating, mobility and pressure-area care.
Mr Bennett has right-sided weakness and mild expressive dysphasia, although his understanding is good. Please use short questions and allow him time to respond.
Following a speech and language therapy assessment, he requires a soft and bite-sized diet (IDDSI level 6) and mildly thick fluids (IDDSI level 2). Please ensure he sits fully upright for meals and for 30 minutes afterwards, and supervise him while eating. He also needs help to cut food and fasten buttons.
He walks short distances and transfers with a walking frame and the assistance of one person. A grade 1 sacral pressure area resolved with three-hourly repositioning and a pressure-relieving mattress, which should continue.
He has been started on clopidogrel and atorvastatin, and his medication chart and a seven-day supply are enclosed. His son, Michael, is his next of kin.
Please contact me if you require further information.
Yours sincerely,
Nurse in Charge
Stroke Unit, Hillcrest General Hospital
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 182 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The opening paragraph explains the transfer, the diagnosis and date, and the three areas of care the nursing home must provide. The reader knows immediately what the letter is for.
Content
The letter prioritises safety: the swallowing plan with exact diet and fluid levels, supervision at meals, the level of help needed to move, and pressure-area care. These are the details the care home acts on from the first meal.
Conciseness & Clarity
Three weeks on a stroke unit are summarised in a few sentences. Dated ward entries become current needs, and the resolved pressure area is mentioned only to explain why repositioning should continue.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional, nurse to nurse, with clear polite requests (“Please ensure”, “Please use”). Abbreviations such as SLT and OD are written out in full.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose, then communication, then eating and drinking, then mobility and skin, then medicines and family. Grouping by care need, rather than by date, makes the letter easy to act on.
Language
Accurate, specific language for the diet and fluid levels, and controlled tenses: past for the stroke and the resolved pressure area, present for his current needs.
Included because the reader needs it Transfer today after a left-sided ischaemic stroke on 3 October
Right-sided weakness and mild expressive dysphasia, with communication advice
Soft and bite-sized diet, mildly thick fluids, upright positioning and supervision
Help needed to cut food and fasten buttons
Walking frame and assistance of one person
Resolved sacral pressure area and continued repositioning
New medicines, medication chart and supply
Son as next of kin
Left out because it does not change the next step Retired engineer and late wife
Cataract surgery and osteoarthritis
Amlodipine (unchanged and on the medication chart)
Exact medicine doses (on the enclosed chart)
Dates of each ward entry
Follow-up appointments and community stroke team visits (in the discharge summary; a short mention is acceptable if you have words left)
Common mistakes in OET nursing transfer letters
These errors cost marks in transfer letters again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Writing the hospital stay day by day instead of describing current care needs.
Leaving out the exact diet and fluid levels, which is a safety risk for a patient with dysphagia.
Forgetting to say how much help the patient needs to walk and transfer.
Mentioning the pressure area without saying what care must continue.
Listing every medicine and dose when a chart is already being sent.
Using abbreviations such as SLT, OD or ON in the letter.
Ending without a clear closing line or contact offer.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips or see how the OET course for nurses trains letter selection. Try the other practice letters too: the nursing discharge letter , the nursing transfer letter , the medicine referral letter , the pharmacy letter to a GP and the physiotherapy discharge letter .

OET nursing transfer letter FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET nursing transfer letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
What is the difference between a transfer letter and a discharge letter?
A transfer letter hands care over to nurses in another setting, such as a care home or rehabilitation unit, so it focuses on the daily care they must provide. A discharge letter usually goes to a community professional who will support a patient returning home.
Should I list every medicine in a transfer letter?
No. Mention new or changed medicines and anything the reader must give or monitor. If the case notes say a medication chart is being sent, refer to it instead of copying every dose.
Can I get my OET nursing letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.

## OET Speaking Role-Play Cards for Nurses With Model Answers

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-speaking-role-play-nursing.html

Free OET Speaking role-play cards for nurses: two practice cards, a model role-play with marking notes, useful phrases and common mistakes.

OET Nursing Speaking
OET Speaking Role-Play Cards for Nurses (With Model Answers)
These OET Speaking role-play cards for nurses give you two realistic practice cards, a model role-play with notes on what earns marks, useful phrases for each stage and the mistakes that cost nurses a B. Prepare for 3 minutes, speak for 5, then compare.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026
Book a 1:1 Speaking session
Read the cards
Ask on WhatsApp
20 min Approximate length of the Speaking sub-test
3 min Preparation time for each role-play card
2 Profession-specific role-plays, about 5 minutes each
How to use these cards
Perform first, read the model second.
Reading a model role-play teaches far less than performing your own under time. Ask a partner to read the interlocutor card and record yourself.
01 Prepare for 3 minutes Read the candidate card and plan your structure.
02 Speak for 5 minutes Respond to the patient, not to a script.
03 Compare and get feedback Check the model, then book a live 1:1 session.
How does OET Speaking work for nurses?
The Speaking sub-test is the same format for every profession, but the role-plays are written for your profession. As a nurse you play yourself, talking to a patient, relative or carer in a realistic nursing situation.
Timing: about 20 minutes The Speaking sub-test takes about 20 minutes in total. It opens with a short warm-up conversation, which is not assessed.
Two role-plays You complete two profession-specific role-plays. For each one you get 3 minutes to prepare from your card, and the role-play itself lasts about 5 minutes.
The interlocutor The interlocutor plays the patient, a relative or a carer from their own card. They may be anxious, reluctant or upset, so you have to respond to them, not recite a script.
Two assessors Your performance is recorded and assessed by two assessors against four linguistic criteria and five clinical communication criteria.
How is OET Speaking marked?
Two sets of criteria are used. The linguistic criteria look at how you speak; the clinical communication criteria look at how you manage the conversation with the patient.
Linguistic criteria (each out of 6)
Intelligibility
Fluency
Appropriateness of Language
Resources of Grammar and Expression
Clinical communication criteria (each out of 3)
Relationship-building
Understanding and incorporating the patient's perspective
Providing structure
Information-gathering
Information-giving
What Grade B looks like OET states that Grade B means predominantly scores of 5 out of 6 on each linguistic criterion and 2 out of 3 on the clinical communication criteria. Source: OET Speaking guide .
Two OET Nursing role-play cards to practise
Each card has two halves: the candidate card you would see in the test and the interlocutor card the examiner uses. Read only the candidate card first, prepare for 3 minutes and ask a partner to play the patient.
Card 1: Anxious patient going home after surgery
Candidate card Setting: Surgical ward, general hospital
Nurse. You are talking to a 58-year-old patient, Mrs Grace Owen, who had keyhole surgery to remove her gallbladder two days ago and is due to go home tomorrow. She seems anxious about leaving hospital.
Task:
Find out what is worrying the patient about going home.
Explain the pain relief plan and why the tablets should be taken regularly at first.
Explain how to look after the small wounds and when she can shower.
Describe the warning signs that mean she should seek medical advice.
Reassure her about the support available after discharge.
Interlocutor card Setting: Surgical ward, general hospital
Patient. You had keyhole gallbladder surgery two days ago and are going home tomorrow. Your husband works long hours, so you will be alone during the day. You are worried the pain will get worse at home.
Task:
When asked, explain that you are nervous about the pain and about being alone.
Say that you do not like taking tablets and would rather take them only when you need them.
Ask what you should do if something goes wrong when you are on your own.
Agree to the plan if the nurse explains it clearly and kindly.
Card 2: Parent worried about a child's asthma inhaler
Candidate card Setting: Children's clinic, community health centre
Practice nurse. You are seeing the parent of 7-year-old Leo, who was diagnosed with asthma last month. He has a blue reliever inhaler and a preventer inhaler, both used with a spacer. His parent says the inhalers "don't seem to work".
Task:
Find out how and when Leo is using each inhaler.
Explain the difference between the reliever and the preventer, and why the preventer is used every day.
Talk the parent through using the inhaler with a spacer.
Respond to the parent's concern about steroids.
Explain when to seek urgent help.
Interlocutor card Setting: Children's clinic, community health centre
Parent. Your son Leo, aged 7, was diagnosed with asthma last month. He uses the blue inhaler when he coughs but you stopped the other inhaler because you read it contains steroids. He finds the spacer awkward, so he often uses the inhaler without it.
Task:
Say that the inhalers do not seem to be working.
When asked, admit that you stopped the preventer because you are worried about steroids.
Ask whether the steroids will affect his growth.
Agree to restart the preventer if the nurse reassures you and explains why it matters.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test card.
Model role-play: anxious patient going home after surgery
This is a condensed model performance for Card 1. Notice how the nurse finds out the concern first, organises the information and checks understanding before closing.
Nurse: Good morning, Mrs Owen. My name is Sam and I'm one of the nurses on the ward today. Is it all right if we have a chat about going home tomorrow?
Relationship-building
Patient: Yes, I suppose so. To be honest, I'm a bit nervous about it.
Nurse: That's completely understandable; a lot of people feel that way after an operation. What's worrying you most?
Relationship-building Patient's perspective Information-gathering
Patient: The pain, mainly. It's fine here because you bring the tablets, but what if it gets worse at home? And my husband works long hours, so I'll be on my own.
Nurse: So it's the pain, and being on your own during the day. Before I explain the plan, how is the pain at the moment, on a scale of nought to ten?
Patient's perspective Information-gathering
Patient: About three, I'd say. Worse when I get up.
Nurse: That's a good sign, and it's what we'd expect two days after keyhole surgery. I'd like to go through three things: your painkillers, looking after the wounds, and who to contact if you're worried. Is that OK?
Information-giving Providing structure
Patient: Yes, please.
Nurse: The doctor has prescribed paracetamol for you to take regularly, four times a day, for the first few days, rather than waiting for the pain to build up. That keeps the pain at a steady, low level. How do you feel about that?
Information-giving Patient's perspective
Patient: I don't really like taking tablets. I'd rather only take them when I need them.
Nurse: I can see why you'd prefer that. The thing is, pain is much easier to keep under control than to bring down once it's strong, and being comfortable helps you move around, which helps you recover. Most people only need them regularly for a few days. Would you be willing to try that?
Patient's perspective Information-giving
Patient: Well, if it's only for a few days, I can try.
Nurse: Thank you. Now, the small wounds on your tummy: you can shower from tomorrow, pat them dry and keep the dressings clean. The practice nurse at your surgery will check them in about a week.
Information-giving
Patient: And what if something goes wrong when I'm on my own?
Nurse: That's an important question. Please contact your GP or the ward straight away if you develop a fever, if the pain gets much worse rather than better, if a wound becomes red, swollen or starts leaking, or if your skin or eyes turn yellow. I'll write the ward number down for you.
Information-giving Patient's perspective
Patient: That makes me feel better, actually.
Nurse: I'm glad. Is there anyone who could pop in during the day for the first few days, for company and to help with lifting things?
Information-gathering Patient's perspective
Patient: My sister lives nearby. I could ask her.
Nurse: That would be ideal, because you should avoid heavy lifting for a couple of weeks. Just so I know I've explained things clearly, could you tell me how you'll take your painkillers when you get home?
Information-giving Providing structure
Patient: Paracetamol four times a day for the first few days, even if the pain is low.
Nurse: Exactly right. So, to sum up: regular painkillers, gentle movement, keep the wounds clean, and call us if you notice any of those warning signs. Do you have any other questions?
Providing structure
Patient: No, I think that covers it. Thank you.
Nurse: You're welcome, Mrs Owen. I'll bring you the written information and the phone number shortly.
Relationship-building
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test card. Each tag shows the clinical communication criterion a move supports.
Useful phrases for OET Nursing role-plays
Learn these as building blocks, not as a script. Adapt the wording to the patient in front of you.
Opening and rapport Hello, my name is … and I'm … . How would you like me to call you?
Is it all right if we talk about … today?
Before we start, is there anything you'd particularly like to cover?
Gathering information Could you tell me a bit more about …?
What do you already know about …?
How has this been affecting your day-to-day life?
Explaining in lay language In simple terms, this means …
Let me explain what that involves.
The main thing to remember is …
Responding to concerns That's completely understandable.
It sounds as though you're worried about … . Is that right?
I can see why you'd feel that way. Let's look at what we can do.
Checking understanding Just so I know I've explained it clearly, could you tell me how you'll …?
Does that make sense so far?
Is there anything you'd like me to go over again?
Closing So, to sum up: …
Do you have any other questions?
If you notice …, please contact … straight away.
Common mistakes nurses make in OET Speaking
These are the habits that most often pull a role-play below Grade B.
Giving information before finding out what the patient already knows or is worried about.
Using clinical terms such as "laparoscopic", "analgesia" or "bronchodilator" without explaining them.
Ignoring an emotional cue such as "I'm nervous" and carrying on with the task list.
Working through the card bullet by bullet instead of following the patient's concerns.
Talking for most of the 5 minutes, so the patient has little chance to respond.
Arguing with a reluctant patient instead of exploring the reason and negotiating.
Closing without checking understanding or summarising the plan.
How should you practise with these cards?
Use Card 1 to study the model and Card 2 to test yourself. The aim is to build a structure you can adapt, not a script you repeat.
Set a timer for 3 minutes and plan Card 2 before you read any model answer: decide how you will open, which questions you will ask and how you will close.
Ask a friend or colleague to read the interlocutor card and react naturally, including the emotional cue.
Record yourself for 5 minutes, then listen back against the two sets of criteria. Mark where you checked understanding and where you responded to a concern.
Repeat the same card a day later with a different reaction from your partner, so you practise responding rather than memorising.
Book a 1:1 Speaking session OET Speaking tips OET course for nurses Free placement test
OET Nursing Speaking FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long is each OET Speaking role-play for nurses?
Each role-play lasts about 5 minutes after 3 minutes of preparation. The whole Speaking sub-test takes about 20 minutes, including a short warm-up that is not assessed.
Are these official OET Nursing role-play cards?
No. They are practice cards written by OET with Dr Hesham in the style of the test. Official sample tests are available from OET.
Should I memorise model answers for OET Speaking?
No. The patient's reactions change in every role-play, so memorised scripts break down. Learn the structure and the phrases, then adapt them to the patient in front of you.
What Speaking score do nurses need?
It depends on the regulator. The NMC asks for B (350) in Speaking, and Ahpra asks for 360 for tests taken from 23 April 2026. Check the OET score requirements guide for your regulator.

## OET Speaking Role-Play Cards for Doctors With Model Answers

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-speaking-role-play-medicine.html

Free OET Speaking role-play cards for doctors: two practice cards, a model consultation with marking notes, useful phrases and common mistakes.

OET Medicine Speaking
OET Speaking Role-Play Cards for Doctors (With Model Answers)
These OET Speaking role-play cards for doctors give you two realistic practice consultations, a model role-play with notes on what earns marks, useful phrases for each stage and the mistakes that cost doctors a B. Prepare for 3 minutes, speak for 5, then compare.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026
Book a 1:1 Speaking session
Read the cards
Ask on WhatsApp
20 min Approximate length of the Speaking sub-test
3 min Preparation time for each role-play card
2 Profession-specific role-plays, about 5 minutes each
How to use these cards
Perform first, read the model second.
Reading a model role-play teaches far less than performing your own under time. Ask a partner to read the interlocutor card and record yourself.
01 Prepare for 3 minutes Read the candidate card and plan your structure.
02 Speak for 5 minutes Respond to the patient, not to a script.
03 Compare and get feedback Check the model, then book a live 1:1 session.
How does OET Speaking work for doctors?
The Speaking sub-test is the same format for every profession, but the role-plays are written for your profession. In OET Medicine you play yourself as a doctor, usually in a consultation with a patient or a relative.
Timing: about 20 minutes The Speaking sub-test takes about 20 minutes in total. It opens with a short warm-up conversation, which is not assessed.
Two role-plays You complete two profession-specific role-plays. For each one you get 3 minutes to prepare from your card, and the role-play itself lasts about 5 minutes.
The interlocutor The interlocutor plays the patient, a relative or a carer from their own card. They may be anxious, reluctant or upset, so you have to respond to them, not recite a script.
Two assessors Your performance is recorded and assessed by two assessors against four linguistic criteria and five clinical communication criteria.
How is OET Speaking marked?
Two sets of criteria are used. The linguistic criteria look at how you speak; the clinical communication criteria look at how you manage the conversation with the patient.
Linguistic criteria (each out of 6)
Intelligibility
Fluency
Appropriateness of Language
Resources of Grammar and Expression
Clinical communication criteria (each out of 3)
Relationship-building
Understanding and incorporating the patient's perspective
Providing structure
Information-gathering
Information-giving
What Grade B looks like OET states that Grade B means predominantly scores of 5 out of 6 on each linguistic criterion and 2 out of 3 on the clinical communication criteria. Source: OET Speaking guide .
Two OET Medicine role-play cards to practise
Each card has two halves: the candidate card you would see in the test and the interlocutor card the examiner uses. Read only the candidate card first, prepare for 3 minutes and ask a partner to play the patient.
Card 1: Explaining a new diagnosis of type 2 diabetes
Candidate card Setting: General practice
Doctor. Mr Daniel Price, aged 52, has come back to discuss his blood test results, which show type 2 diabetes. He seems worried.
Task:
Find out what the patient already knows and what is worrying him.
Explain the diagnosis in simple terms.
Outline the treatment plan: lifestyle changes, starting metformin and regular checks.
Respond to his fear about complications.
Arrange follow-up and refer him to a diabetes education course.
Interlocutor card Setting: General practice
Patient. You are 52 and came back for your blood test results. Your father had diabetes and lost part of his foot, so you are very worried. You eat out a lot for work.
Task:
Say that you have been worrying about the results.
When the diagnosis is explained, ask whether you will end up like your father.
Say that changing your diet will be hard because you eat out for work.
Accept the plan if the doctor explains it clearly and reassures you.
Card 2: Patient asking for antibiotics for a sore throat
Candidate card Setting: General practice
Doctor. Ms Laura Bennett, aged 29, a primary school teacher, has had a sore throat for three days. Your examination suggests a viral infection, and antibiotics are not indicated. She is asking for antibiotics.
Task:
Find out about her symptoms and what she is hoping for from the appointment.
Explain that the infection is most likely viral and why antibiotics will not help.
Suggest ways to relieve the symptoms at home.
Explain which symptoms mean she should come back or seek urgent help.
Respond to her concern about missing work.
Interlocutor card Setting: General practice
Patient. You are a 29-year-old teacher with a sore throat for three days. Last year a different doctor gave you antibiotics and you got better quickly. You have an important school event next week.
Task:
Ask directly for antibiotics so that you can get back to work.
Mention that antibiotics worked last time.
Show some frustration if you feel you are not being listened to.
Agree to the plan if the doctor explains the reasons and what to watch for.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test card.
Model role-play: explaining a new diagnosis of type 2 diabetes
This is a condensed model performance for Card 1. Notice how the doctor explores the patient's fear before explaining, signposts the plan in three parts and checks understanding before closing.
Doctor: Hello, Mr Price. I'm Dr Patel. Thank you for coming back to discuss your blood test results. How have you been since we last met?
Relationship-building
Patient: Fine, but I've been worrying about these results, to be honest.
Doctor: I can understand that. Before I go through them, could you tell me what you already know about why we did the tests?
Patient's perspective Information-gathering
Patient: You said my sugar might be high. My dad had diabetes. He ended up losing part of his foot, so I've been dreading this.
Doctor: I'm sorry to hear about your father; that must make this feel very frightening. I'll explain the results, and then we can talk about what we can do so that your experience is different. Is that all right?
Relationship-building Patient's perspective Providing structure
Patient: Yes, go on.
Doctor: The blood test measures your average sugar level over the past two to three months. Yours is in the range that means you have type 2 diabetes. In simple terms, your body isn't using insulin, the hormone that controls sugar, as well as it should, so sugar builds up in the blood.
Information-giving
Patient: So I'll end up like my dad?
Doctor: That's a very understandable fear. We usually find diabetes earlier now, and treatment has improved a lot. Keeping your sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol under control greatly lowers the risk of problems with the feet, eyes and kidneys. Can I ask how much you knew about your father's treatment?
Patient's perspective Information-giving Information-gathering
Patient: Not much. He didn't really go to his check-ups.
Doctor: That's helpful to know, because regular check-ups are one of the most important parts of the plan. There are three parts: lifestyle, medication and monitoring. Shall I go through each one?
Providing structure
Patient: Please.
Doctor: First, lifestyle: small changes to your diet, such as cutting down on sugary drinks and portion sizes, and being more active, for example a brisk walk most days. Losing even a little weight can make a real difference. How do you feel about those changes?
Information-giving Patient's perspective
Patient: I could probably walk more. Food is harder; I eat out a lot for work.
Doctor: That's very common. I'd like to refer you to a free diabetes education course, where you'll get practical tips, including on eating out. Second, medication: I'd suggest starting a tablet called metformin, which helps your body use insulin better. It can upset the stomach at first, so we start with a low dose taken with food.
Information-giving Patient's perspective
Patient: OK. And the monitoring?
Doctor: Every year you'll have checks of your eyes, feet and kidneys, as well as regular blood tests with the practice nurse. These catch problems early, before they become serious. Could you tell me in your own words what the plan is, so I know I've explained it clearly?
Information-giving Providing structure
Patient: Walk more, change my diet, start metformin with food, go on the course and come to every check-up.
Doctor: That's exactly it. I'll book you in with the practice nurse in two weeks to see how you're getting on with the tablets. Is there anything else you'd like to ask?
Providing structure Relationship-building
Patient: No, that's much clearer. Thank you, doctor.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test card. Each tag shows the clinical communication criterion a move supports.
Useful phrases for OET Medicine role-plays
Learn these as building blocks, not as a script. Adapt the wording to the patient in front of you.
Opening and rapport Hello, my name is … and I'm … . How would you like me to call you?
Is it all right if we talk about … today?
Before we start, is there anything you'd particularly like to cover?
Gathering information Could you tell me a bit more about …?
What do you already know about …?
How has this been affecting your day-to-day life?
Explaining in lay language In simple terms, this means …
Let me explain what that involves.
The main thing to remember is …
Responding to concerns That's completely understandable.
It sounds as though you're worried about … . Is that right?
I can see why you'd feel that way. Let's look at what we can do.
Checking understanding Just so I know I've explained it clearly, could you tell me how you'll …?
Does that make sense so far?
Is there anything you'd like me to go over again?
Closing So, to sum up: …
Do you have any other questions?
If you notice …, please contact … straight away.
Common mistakes doctors make in OET Speaking
These are the habits that most often pull a role-play below Grade B.
Explaining the diagnosis before finding out what the patient knows, fears or expects.
Using medical terms such as "HbA1c", "glycaemic control" or "self-limiting" without explaining them.
Responding to a request such as "Can I have antibiotics?" with a flat refusal instead of exploring the reason behind it.
Delivering a long monologue, so the patient has little chance to respond or ask questions.
Missing an emotional cue, such as a family history the patient is clearly worried about.
Running out of time before safety-netting or arranging follow-up.
Closing without checking understanding or summarising the plan.
How should you practise with these cards?
Use Card 1 to study the model and Card 2 to test yourself. Card 2 is a classic negotiation task: the aim is a shared plan, not winning the argument.
Set a timer for 3 minutes and plan Card 2 before you read any model answer: decide how you will open, which questions you will ask and how you will close.
Ask a friend or colleague to read the interlocutor card and react naturally, including the emotional cue.
Record yourself for 5 minutes, then listen back against the two sets of criteria. Mark where you checked understanding and where you responded to a concern.
Repeat the same card a day later with a different reaction from your partner, so you practise responding rather than memorising.

OET Medicine Speaking FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long is each OET Speaking role-play for doctors?
Each role-play lasts about 5 minutes after 3 minutes of preparation. The whole Speaking sub-test takes about 20 minutes, including a short warm-up that is not assessed.
Are these official OET Medicine role-play cards?
No. They are practice cards written by OET with Dr Hesham in the style of the test. Official sample tests are available from OET.
Do I need medical knowledge to pass OET Speaking?
OET Speaking assesses communication, not clinical knowledge. Your medical background helps you understand the scenario, but marks come from how you build rapport, structure the conversation, gather and give information and respond to the patient.
What Speaking score do doctors need?
It depends on the regulator. The GMC asks for B (350) in all four sub-tests, ECFMG asks for 350 in Speaking, and Ahpra asks for 360 for tests taken from 23 April 2026. Check the OET score requirements guide for your regulator.

## كورس OET أونلاين للأطباء والتمريض | د. أحمد هشام

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/ar/

كورس OET أونلاين للأطباء والتمريض والصيادلة مع د. أحمد هشام: دروس مسجلة وتصحيح كتابة شخصي ومحادثة فردية ودرجات OET المطلوبة لكل دولة.

OET بالعربي
كورس OET أونلاين للأطباء والتمريض مع د. أحمد هشام
كورس OET مع د. أحمد هشام هو تحضير أونلاين مسجل للأطباء والتمريض والصيادلة وأخصائيي العلاج الطبيعي، مع تصحيح شخصي لرسائل الكتابة وجلسات محادثة فردية. في هذه الصفحة تعرف ما هو امتحان OET، والدرجات المطلوبة في بريطانيا وأستراليا وأيرلندا وأمريكا، وكيف تبدأ التحضير بخطة واضحة.
بقلم د. أحمد هشام ، طبيب ومؤسس OET with Dr Hesham · تحديث 24 أكتوبر 2026 Read in English
ابدأ اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني
اسأل على واتساب
الباقات
12 مهنة يغطيها امتحان OET
4 أجزاء: استماع وقراءة وكتابة ومحادثة
+1,750 نتيجة OET موثقة 2021–2026
ما هو امتحان OET ولمن يناسب؟
OET (Occupational English Test) هو اختبار لغة إنجليزية مصمم للعاملين في المهن الصحية، وتقبله جهات الترخيص في بريطانيا وأيرلندا وأستراليا ونيوزيلندا وأمريكا وغيرها. الفرق الأساسي بينه وبين الاختبارات العامة أن مهام الكتابة والمحادثة مأخوذة من واقع عملك اليومي: رسالة تحويل أو خروج مريض، وحوار مع مريض أو أحد أقاربه.
أربعة أجزاء
الاستماع (Listening) حوالي 40 دقيقة و42 سؤالاً، والقراءة (Reading) 60 دقيقة و42 سؤالاً، والكتابة (Writing) 5 دقائق قراءة ثم 40 دقيقة لكتابة رسالة واحدة، والمحادثة (Speaking) حوالي 20 دقيقة فيها لعب أدوار مرتين.
12 مهنة
الطب والتمريض والصيدلة والعلاج الطبيعي وطب الأسنان والتغذية والعلاج الوظيفي والبصريات وطب القدم والأشعة وعلاج النطق والطب البيطري. الاستماع والقراءة موحدان للجميع، أما الكتابة والمحادثة فخاصتان بمهنتك.
لا توجد درجة كلية
كل جزء له درجة مستقلة من 0 إلى 500 بفواصل 10 درجات: A من 450 إلى 500، وB من 350 إلى 440، وC+ من 300 إلى 340، ثم C وD وE. جهات الترخيص تنظر إلى كل جزء على حدة.
ما درجات OET المطلوبة في كل دولة؟
هذه أشهر المتطلبات كما راجعناها على المواقع الرسمية في 24 أكتوبر 2026. القواعد تتغير، لذلك تأكد دائماً من صفحة الجهة نفسها قبل الحجز.
الجهة Listening Reading Writing Speaking عدد الجلسات
NMC (التمريض والقبالة، بريطانيا) 350 350 300 350 جلسة واحدة أو جلستان خلال 12 شهراً بشروط
GMC (الأطباء، بريطانيا) 350 350 350 350 جلسة واحدة (الأحدث)
Ahpra (أستراليا، للاختبارات من 23 أبريل 2026) 350 360 350 360 جلسة أو جلستان خلال 12 شهراً بحدود دنيا
NMBI (التمريض، أيرلندا) 350 350 300 350 جلسة واحدة فقط
ECFMG (الأطباء، أمريكا، مسارات 2027) 350 350 300 350 جلسة واحدة بعد 1 يناير 2025
في دول الخليج تختلف المتطلبات حسب الجهة والمهنة، راجع Gulf Pathway Guide . وللقائمة الكاملة بكل الجهات راجع OET Score Requirements ، أو احسب نتيجتك مباشرة عبر OET Score Calculator .
ماذا يشمل كورس OET مع د. أحمد هشام؟
الكورسات مسجلة ومقسمة حسب المهنة، ومعها تصحيح شخصي ومتابعة. الفكرة بسيطة: تتعلم الطريقة الصحيحة من الدروس، ثم تُصحَّح أخطاؤك الفعلية حتى تصل إلى درجتك المستهدفة.
كورس التمريض
أكثر من 30 ساعة مسجلة بأمثلة ورسائل وحالات تمريضية، مع خيار إضافة 5 تقييمات كتابة وجلسة محادثة فردية.
كورس OET للتمريض
كورس الأطباء
أكثر من 40 ساعة مسجلة لـ OET Medicine مع مكتبة تدريب كبيرة و5 تقييمات كتابة وجلسة محادثة فردية.
كورس OET للأطباء
الصيدلة والعلاج الطبيعي
كورسات خاصة بالصيدلة (أكثر من 25 ساعة) والعلاج الطبيعي (أكثر من 40 ساعة) ومهن الصحة المساندة، بحالات ومحادثات من نفس المهنة.
Full Recorded Courses
تصحيح الكتابة
تصحيح يدوي لكل رسالة مع درجة تقديرية وملاحظة صوتية على واتساب، خلال 48 إلى 72 ساعة عادةً (عدا الجمعة) في باقات الإضافة.
OET Writing Correction
محادثة فردية 1:1
جلسة مباشرة مع عدة بطاقات محادثة وتقييم تفصيلي للأداء، يمكن إضافتها لأي كورس.
Speaking sessions
امتحانات تجريبية وTutorBook
امتحانات كاملة بالأجزاء الأربعة يُقيَّم فيها الكتابة والمحادثة بالتفصيل، وكتاب TutorBook المبني على ريكولز 2026 بعشرة امتحانات كاملة.
Mock exams
النتائج متاحة للجميع: أكثر من 1,750 نتيجة OET موثقة من 2021 إلى 2026 في صفحة Success Stories .
كيف تبدأ التحضير لـ OET؟
أقصر طريق للدرجة المطلوبة هو أن تعرف مستواك الحقيقي أولاً، ثم تركز على الجزء الذي يخسرك الدرجات.
اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني. اختبار في المهارات الأربع يعطيك مستوى CEFR تقريبياً لكل مهارة. Free placement test .
اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك. إذا كان مستواك B1 أو أقل ابدأ بكورس الإنجليزي التأسيسي، وإذا كنت حول B2 أو أعلى ابدأ كورس OET لمهنتك مباشرة. للعلم، يربط OET الدرجة B بمستوى C1 في CEFR.
ذاكر الدروس المسجلة. تعلم طريقة تحليل الحالة واختيار المعلومات المهمة في الكتابة، وهيكل الحوار في المحادثة.
صحح رسائلك ومحادثتك. التصحيح الشخصي هو ما يرفع درجة الكتابة والمحادثة بسرعة، لأنهما الجزءان اللذان يخسر فيهما أغلب المتقدمين.
امتحان تجريبي ثم الحجز. احجز الامتحان الحقيقي عندما تصل إلى درجتك المستهدفة في الامتحانات التجريبية بشكل ثابت.
مواعيد ورسوم امتحان OET
رسوم الامتحان الكامل 587 دولاراً أسترالياً. يُغلق الحجز قبل 24 يوماً من امتحان الورق، وقبل 7 أيام من امتحان الكمبيوتر أو OET@Home. نتائج الكمبيوتر قد تظهر خلال 48 ساعة، و95% منها خلال 6 أيام، ونتائج الورق تبدأ من 13 يوماً.
انتبه: OET@Home لا تقبله Ahpra ولا NMBI ولا جهات نيوزيلندا، بينما تقبله NMC وGMC. كل المواعيد والتفاصيل في صفحة OET Test Dates and Fees .
أسئلة شائعة عن كورس OET
إجابات قصيرة على أكثر الأسئلة التي تصلنا.
ما هو امتحان OET؟
OET هو اختبار اللغة الإنجليزية المهنية للعاملين في القطاع الصحي. يتكون من أربعة أجزاء: الاستماع والقراءة وهما موحدان لكل المهن، والكتابة والمحادثة وهما خاصان بمهنتك، ويغطي 12 مهنة منها الطب والتمريض والصيدلة والعلاج الطبيعي.
كم الدرجة المطلوبة للنجاح في OET؟
لا توجد درجة نجاح واحدة، فكل جهة ترخيص تحدد حدها الأدنى. معظم الجهات تطلب الدرجة B أي 350 في كل جزء، وتقبل جهات مثل NMC وNMBI وECFMG درجة 300 في الكتابة، أما Ahpra في أستراليا فتطلب 350 و360 و350 و360 للاختبارات من 23 أبريل 2026.
هل الكورس مباشر أم مسجل؟
الكورسات مسجلة بالكامل ويمكنك إعادة أي درس طوال فترة الاشتراك، مع تصحيح شخصي للرسائل وجلسات محادثة فردية مباشرة 1:1 حسب الباقة التي تختارها.
كيف يتم تصحيح الكتابة؟
يصحح د. أحمد كل رسالة يدوياً، وتحصل على درجة تقديرية وتصحيح تفصيلي وملاحظة صوتية على واتساب، ويمكنك اختيار الرسالة بنفسك أو العمل على رسائل مقترحة من الريكولز.
من أين أبدأ إذا لم أعرف مستواي؟
ابدأ باختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني في المهارات الأربع، ثم اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك، وإذا كان مستواك B1 أو أقل فالأفضل أن تبدأ بكورس الإنجليزي التأسيسي قبل التحضير المكثف لـ OET.
ابدأ تحضيرك لـ OET اليوم
اعرف مستواك مجاناً، ثم اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك، أو راسل فريق د. أحمد هشام على واتساب بمهنتك وموعد امتحانك والدولة المستهدفة.
اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني واتساب

## كورس OET للتمريض أونلاين | د. أحمد هشام

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/ar/oet-course-for-nurses.html

كورس OET للتمريض أونلاين: أكثر من 30 ساعة مسجلة ورسائل تمريض وتصحيح كتابة شخصي ومحادثة فردية للوصول إلى درجة NMC وAhpra المطلوبة.

OET Nursing
كورس OET للتمريض أونلاين
كورس OET للتمريض مع د. أحمد هشام كورس مسجل خاص بالتمريض، يغطي الاستماع والقراءة والكتابة والمحادثة برسائل وحالات تمريضية، مع تصحيح شخصي للرسائل وجلسة محادثة فردية مباشرة، لتصل إلى درجة NMC: الدرجة B في الاستماع والقراءة والمحادثة وC+ في الكتابة.
بقلم د. أحمد هشام ، طبيب ومؤسس OET with Dr Hesham · تحديث 2 نوفمبر 2026 Read in English
ابدأ اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني
اسأل على واتساب
الباقات
+30 ساعة دروس تمريض مسجلة
6 أشهر صلاحية الكورس
5 تقييمات كتابة شخصية في الباقة المميزة
لمن يناسب كورس OET للتمريض؟
الكورس مصمم للممرضات والممرضين وأخصائيي القبالة الذين يحتاجون OET للتسجيل في بريطانيا أو أيرلندا أو أستراليا أو نيوزيلندا أو الخليج. كل الأمثلة والرسائل وبطاقات المحادثة مأخوذة من بيئة التمريض، فتتدرب على المواقف التي ستقابلها في الامتحان فعلاً.
ممرضون يبدؤون من الصفر
ابدأ باختبار تحديد المستوى، وإذا كان مستواك B1 أو أقل فالباقة المميزة تتضمن كورس الإنجليزي التأسيسي (أكثر من 11 ساعة) قبل التحضير المكثف.
من رسب في الكتابة أو المحادثة
الباقة المميزة للتمريض تمنحك 5 تقييمات شخصية للكتابة وجلسة محادثة فردية، وهما الجزءان اللذان يحددان النتيجة غالباً.
من يحتاج نتيجة قريبة
خطة واضحة: دروس مركزة، ثم تصحيح، ثم امتحان تجريبي قبل الحجز.
ما درجات OET المطلوبة للتمريض؟
راجعنا هذه المتطلبات على المواقع الرسمية في 24 أكتوبر 2026. تأكد من صفحة الجهة قبل الحجز لأن القواعد تتغير.
الجهة Listening Reading Writing Speaking ملاحظات
NMC (بريطانيا) 350 350 300 350 جلستان خلال 12 شهراً بحدود دنيا، ويقبل OET@Home
Ahpra / NMBA (أستراليا) 350 360 350 360 للاختبارات من 23 أبريل 2026، ولا يقبل OET@Home
NMBI (أيرلندا) 350 350 300 350 جلسة واحدة فقط، ولا يقبل OET@Home
Nursing Council NZ (نيوزيلندا) 350 350 300 350 أكثر من جلسة خلال 12 شهراً، ولا يقبل OET@Home
للخليج راجع دليل OET للترخيص الصحي في الخليج ، ولكل الجهات OET Score Requirements .
ماذا تشمل باقات التمريض؟
باقتان للتمريض، وكلتاهما بصلاحية 6 أشهر من تاريخ الشراء.
كورس التمريض الكلاسيكي
الكورس المسجل الكامل لمن يريد الدروس ومواد التدريب دون تقييمات شخصية مضمنة: أكثر من 30 ساعة مسجلة في المهارات الأربع، ورسائل تمريض مبنية على الريكولز مع إجابات نموذجية، وبطاقات محادثة تمريضية مع الأفكار المتوقعة، ومكتبة تدريب للاستماع والقراءة، و5 أرصدة تدريب، ودعم مستمر للأسئلة، ورفيق التعلّم SAMI على مدار الساعة.
Classic Nursing OET Course
الباقة المميزة للتمريض (الموصى بها)
كل ما في الكورس الكلاسيكي، مع 5 تقييمات شخصية لرسائل الكتابة بتصحيح تفصيلي وملاحظات صوتية على واتساب، وجلسة محادثة فردية مباشرة مع تقييم شخصي، وكورس الإنجليزي التأسيسي الكامل (أكثر من 11 ساعة)، وكتاب TutorBook المبني على ريكولز 2026 بعشرة امتحانات كاملة وإجابات نموذجية.
Nursing Premium Bundle
قارن الباقات في صفحة Pricing . ويمكنك إضافة تقييمات كتابة (3 أو 5 أو 7 أو 10 رسائل) أو جلسات محادثة لأي كورس نشط.
كيف تنجح في كتابة OET للتمريض؟
مهمة الكتابة 5 دقائق قراءة ثم 40 دقيقة لكتابة رسالة واحدة في حدود 180 إلى 200 كلمة. في التمريض غالباً تكون رسالة خروج مريض أو نقل أو تحويل لممرضة مجتمعية أو دار رعاية.
اختر ما يحتاجه القارئ
لا تنقل كل الملاحظات. اسأل نفسك: ماذا تحتاج الممرضة المجتمعية لتكمل الرعاية غداً؟ الأدوية والجروح والمتابعة والمخاطر أهم من التاريخ القديم.
الغرض في أول سطر
اكتب سبب الرسالة والمطلوب من القارئ بوضوح في الفقرة الأولى، فهذا يرفع درجة Purpose مباشرة.
رتب حسب الأولوية
ابدأ بالأهم للرعاية الحالية، ثم الخلفية المفيدة، واختم بطلب محدد وتاريخ المتابعة.
شاهد مثالاً كاملاً بحالة وإجابة نموذجية: OET Writing Sample for Nurses ، ثم أرسل رسالتك للتصحيح عبر OET Writing Correction .
كيف تتدرب على محادثة OET للتمريض؟
المحادثة حوالي 20 دقيقة، فيها لعب أدوار مرتين، لكل منهما 3 دقائق تحضير وحوالي 5 دقائق حوار، والممتحن يلعب دور المريض أو أحد أقاربه.
مواقف تمريضية متكررة
شرح إجراء أو العناية بجرح أو خطة الخروج، والالتزام بالأدوية وآثارها الجانبية، ونصائح نمط الحياة، وطمأنة مريض قلق.
ما الذي يُقيَّم؟
معايير لغوية (الوضوح والطلاقة ومناسبة اللغة والقواعد) ومعايير تواصل إكلينيكي (بناء العلاقة وفهم وجهة نظر المريض وتنظيم الحوار وجمع المعلومات وإعطاؤها).
تدرّب مع تصحيح
جلسة المحادثة الفردية 1:1 تكشف الأخطاء التي لا تراها بنفسك، مثل المصطلحات الطبية الصعبة على المريض أو إغلاق الحوار بلا خطة.
OET Speaking Tips
خطوات التحضير لـ OET للتمريض
خطة عملية من أول يوم حتى حجز الامتحان.
اعرف مستواك مجاناً. اختبار تحديد المستوى يقيس المهارات الأربع ويعطيك مستوى CEFR تقريبياً. Free placement test .
اختر الباقة. إذا كنت تريد تصحيحاً شخصياً للكتابة والمحادثة، أو كان مستواك B1 أو أقل، فالباقة المميزة بكورسها التأسيسي هي الأنسب. وإذا كنت حول B2 أو أعلى وتريد الدروس والمواد فقط فالكورس الكلاسيكي يكفي، ويمكنك إضافة تقييمات الكتابة إليه.
ذاكر الدروس المسجلة. ابدأ بالكتابة والمحادثة لأنهما الأكثر تأثيراً على درجة NMC، مع تدريب يومي قصير على الاستماع والقراءة.
أرسل رسائلك للتصحيح. كل رسالة تعود بدرجة تقديرية وتصحيح تفصيلي وملاحظة صوتية على واتساب، فتعرف بالضبط ما تغيّره في الرسالة التالية.
جلسة محادثة ثم امتحان تجريبي. جلسة المحادثة الفردية تصحح أسلوبك مع المريض، والامتحان التجريبي يخبرك إن كنت جاهزاً للحجز.
أسئلة شائعة عن كورس OET للتمريض
إجابات قصيرة قبل أن تبدأ.
ما درجة OET المطلوبة للتمريض في بريطانيا؟
تطلب NMC نسخة التمريض من OET بدرجة B أي 350 في الاستماع والقراءة والمحادثة، ودرجة C+ أي 300 في الكتابة. ويمكن الجمع بين جلستين خلال 12 شهراً بشرط ألا تقل أي درجة عن 300 في الاستماع والقراءة والمحادثة وعن 250 في الكتابة.
هل كورس التمريض مسجل؟
نعم، الكورس مسجل بأكثر من 30 ساعة ويمكنك إعادة الدروس طوال 6 أشهر من تاريخ الشراء. والباقة المميزة للتمريض تشمل جلسة محادثة فردية مباشرة، ويمكن إضافة جلسات المحادثة إلى الكورس الكلاسيكي.
ما الفرق بين باقتي التمريض؟
كورس التمريض الكلاسيكي يشمل الدروس المسجلة والمواد وأرصدة التدريب ورفيق SAMI. أما الباقة المميزة للتمريض، وهي الموصى بها، فتضيف 5 تقييمات شخصية للكتابة مع ملاحظات صوتية على واتساب، وجلسة محادثة فردية، وكورس الإنجليزي التأسيسي، وكتاب TutorBook.
هل أستطيع استخدام OET@Home لأستراليا؟
لا. لا تقبل Ahpra اختبار OET@Home، وتقبل الاختبار الورقي أو اختبار الكمبيوتر في مركز معتمد. أما NMC في بريطانيا فتقبل OET@Home.
ما أنواع رسائل الكتابة في التمريض؟
أغلب رسائل التمريض رسائل خروج مريض أو نقل أو تحويل إلى ممرضة مجتمعية أو دار رعاية أو طبيب عام، والمطلوب فيها اختيار المعلومات التي يحتاجها القارئ لمتابعة رعاية المريض.
ابدأ تحضيرك لـ OET اليوم
اعرف مستواك مجاناً، ثم اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك، أو راسل فريق د. أحمد هشام على واتساب بمهنتك وموعد امتحانك والدولة المستهدفة.
اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني واتساب

## كورس OET للأطباء أونلاين | د. أحمد هشام

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/ar/oet-course-for-doctors.html

كورس OET للأطباء أونلاين: أكثر من 40 ساعة مسجلة لـ OET Medicine وتصحيح رسائل التحويل ومحادثة فردية للوصول إلى درجات GMC وECFMG.

OET Medicine
كورس OET للأطباء أونلاين
كورس OET للأطباء مع د. أحمد هشام كورس مسجل لـ OET Medicine يقدمه طبيب، بمكتبة تدريب كبيرة وتصحيح شخصي لرسائل التحويل وجلسة محادثة فردية مباشرة، للأطباء المتجهين إلى التسجيل في GMC ببريطانيا أو شهادة ECFMG في أمريكا أو أستراليا وأيرلندا.
بقلم د. أحمد هشام ، طبيب ومؤسس OET with Dr Hesham · تحديث 24 أكتوبر 2026 Read in English
ابدأ اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني
اسأل على واتساب
الباقات
+40 ساعة دروس OET Medicine مسجلة
+160 امتحان استماع في مكتبة التدريب
+90 مهمة كتابة بأنواع الرسائل الرئيسية
لمن يناسب كورس OET للأطباء؟
الكورس مصمم للأطباء الدوليين الذين يحتاجون OET Medicine للتسجيل في بريطانيا عبر GMC أو لشهادة ECFMG في أمريكا أو للتسجيل في أستراليا وأيرلندا. يقدمه د. أحمد هشام، وهو طبيب، فيركز على ما يحتاجه الطبيب فعلاً: كتابة رسالة تحويل واضحة، وإدارة حوار مع مريض بلغة بسيطة.
أطباء مسار PLAB وGMC
تحتاج B في الأجزاء الأربعة من نفس الجلسة، لذلك الخطة تغطي المهارات الأربع بالتوازي.
أطباء مسار ECFMG
350 في الاستماع والقراءة والمحادثة و300 في الكتابة، مع مواعيد نهائية مهمة لـ Match 2027.
OET for ECFMG
من رسب سابقاً
التصحيح الشخصي للكتابة وجلسة المحادثة الفردية يحددان بالضبط ما الذي يمنعك من الدرجة المطلوبة.
ما درجات OET المطلوبة للأطباء؟
راجعنا هذه المتطلبات على المواقع الرسمية في 24 أكتوبر 2026. تأكد من صفحة الجهة قبل الحجز لأن القواعد تتغير.
الجهة Listening Reading Writing Speaking ملاحظات
GMC (بريطانيا) 350 350 350 350 جلسة واحدة، ويقبل OET@Home
ECFMG (أمريكا، مسارات 2027) 350 350 300 350 جلسة واحدة بعد 1 يناير 2025، وOET@Home فقط إذا لم يوجد مركز في بلدك
Ahpra / Medical Board (أستراليا) 350 360 350 360 للاختبارات من 23 أبريل 2026، ولا يقبل OET@Home
Medical Council of Ireland (أيرلندا) 350 350 350 350 جلسة واحدة خلال سنتين، ولا يقبل OET@Home
للخليج راجع دليل OET للترخيص الصحي في الخليج ، ولكل الجهات OET Score Requirements .
ماذا يشمل كورس OET للأطباء؟
ثلاثة مستويات بنفس الكورس المسجل: الكورس الكلاسيكي، ثم الكورس مع ممارسة الموقع، ثم الباقة الشاملة + TutorBook الموصى بها. وصلاحية الكورس 6 أشهر من تاريخ الشراء.
الكورس الكامل الكلاسيكي + SAMI للطب
أكثر من 40 ساعة مسجلة في المهارات الأربع، وأكثر من 160 امتحان استماع، وأكثر من 100 امتحان قراءة بالإجابات والشرح، وأكثر من 90 مهمة كتابة، وأكثر من 100 بطاقة محادثة، وريكولز حديثة وقديمة منذ 2023، و5 تقييمات كتابة شخصية، وجلسة محادثة فردية، و5 أرصدة تدريب، ودعم مستمر للأسئلة، ورفيق التعلّم SAMI على مدار الساعة.
الباقة الشاملة + TutorBook
المسار الموصى به للأطباء: الكورس المسجل مع ممارسة الموقع وكتاب TutorBook لعام 2026 في باقة واحدة. تشمل كل ما في الكورس مع ممارسة الموقع، و5 رسائل كتابة شخصية من د. أحمد هشام وجلسة محادثة فردية مع خبير، وتدريب الكتابة والمحادثة على الموقع، و12 امتحان استماع و12 امتحان قراءة على الموقع للمتقدمين للامتحان على الكمبيوتر، ورفيق SAMI، وكتاب TutorBook المبني على ريكولز 2026 بعشرة امتحانات كاملة مع وصول دائم.
إضافات حسب الحاجة
تقييمات كتابة إضافية (3 أو 5 أو 7 أو 10 رسائل)، وجلسات محادثة فردية، وامتحانات تجريبية كاملة يُقيَّم فيها الكتابة والمحادثة بالتفصيل.
Add-ons
قارن الباقات في صفحة Pricing .
كيف تكتب رسالة تحويل قوية في OET Medicine؟
مهمة الكتابة 5 دقائق قراءة ثم 40 دقيقة لكتابة رسالة واحدة في حدود 180 إلى 200 كلمة، وغالباً تكون رسالة تحويل إلى أخصائي أو طبيب عام.
سبب التحويل أولاً
اذكر في الفقرة الأولى سبب التحويل ودرجة الاستعجال والمطلوب من الطبيب المستقبل، فهذا جوهر معيار Purpose.
اختر المعلومات بذكاء
النتائج غير الطبيعية والأدوية الحالية وعوامل الخطورة أهم من كل تفاصيل التاريخ المرضي. ما لا يغير قرار الطبيب المستقبل لا مكان له.
لغة مهنية مختصرة
جمل كاملة واضحة بلا اختصارات غير مفهومة، وتنظيم منطقي من الأهم للأقل أهمية.
شاهد مثالاً كاملاً: OET Writing Sample for Doctors ، ثم أرسل رسالتك للتصحيح عبر OET Writing Correction .
كيف تتعامل مع محادثة OET للأطباء؟
المحادثة حوالي 20 دقيقة، فيها لعب أدوار مرتين، لكل منهما 3 دقائق تحضير وحوالي 5 دقائق حوار، والممتحن يلعب دور المريض أو أحد أقاربه.
مواقف متكررة للأطباء
شرح تشخيص أو نتيجة تحليل بلغة بسيطة، ومناقشة الفحوصات والعلاج، وإبلاغ خبر سيئ بتعاطف وخطة واضحة، والتعامل مع قريب قلق أو غاضب، وإقناع مريض متردد.
أخطاء شائعة
استخدام مصطلحات طبية بدون شرح، والتحدث أكثر من المريض، وتجاهل مخاوفه، وإنهاء الحوار بلا خطة متفق عليها.
تدرّب مع تقييم
جلسة المحادثة الفردية 1:1 تمنحك تقييماً تفصيلياً للأداء على عدة بطاقات.
OET Speaking Tips
خطوات التحضير لـ OET للأطباء
خطة عملية تناسب الطبيب المشغول.
اعرف مستواك مجاناً. اختبار تحديد المستوى يقيس المهارات الأربع ويعطيك مستوى CEFR تقريبياً. Free placement test .
حدد الجهة والموعد النهائي. GMC تطلب B في الأجزاء الأربعة من نفس الجلسة، وECFMG يطلب 300 في الكتابة مع موعد نهائي لـ Match 2027، فخطط موعد امتحانك على هذا الأساس.
ذاكر الدروس المسجلة. ركز أولاً على تحليل الحالة واختيار المعلومات في رسالة التحويل، وعلى هيكل الحوار في المحادثة.
صحح رسائلك. التقييمات الخمسة للكتابة في الكورس تعطيك درجة تقديرية وتصحيحاً تفصيلياً وملاحظة صوتية على واتساب لكل رسالة.
جلسة محادثة ثم امتحان تجريبي. احجز الامتحان الحقيقي عندما تصل إلى درجتك المستهدفة في الامتحان التجريبي بشكل ثابت.
أسئلة شائعة عن كورس OET للأطباء
إجابات قصيرة قبل أن تبدأ.
ما درجة OET المطلوبة للأطباء في بريطانيا؟
تطلب GMC نسخة الطب من OET بدرجة B أي 350 في الأجزاء الأربعة من نفس الجلسة، وتكون من آخر جلسة، وتقبل الاختبار الورقي والكمبيوتر وOET@Home، والنتيجة صالحة لمدة سنتين حسب قواعد GMC.
هل يقبل ECFMG امتحان OET؟
نعم. لمسارات 2027 يطلب ECFMG امتحان OET Medicine بدرجة 350 في الاستماع والقراءة والمحادثة و300 في الكتابة، في جلسة واحدة بعد 1 يناير 2025، وتحتاج رقم MyIntealth لإرسال النتائج الصادرة من 14 مايو 2026.
هل كورس الأطباء مسجل أم مباشر؟
الكورس مسجل بأكثر من 40 ساعة ويمكنك إعادة الدروس طوال 6 أشهر، ويشمل 5 تقييمات كتابة وجلسة محادثة فردية مباشرة.
ما الفرق بين الكورس الكلاسيكي والباقة الشاملة + TutorBook؟
كلاهما يحتوي على الكورس المسجل الكامل لـ OET Medicine و5 تقييمات كتابة شخصية وجلسة محادثة فردية ورفيق SAMI. تضيف الباقة الشاملة + TutorBook ممارسة الموقع وكتاب TutorBook لعام 2026 بعشرة امتحانات كاملة مبنية على الريكولز مع وصول دائم.
ما أصعب جزء على الأطباء عادةً؟
غالباً الكتابة، لأن الطبيب يميل إلى نقل كل التفاصيل في رسالة التحويل. المطلوب هو اختيار ما يحتاجه الطبيب المستقبل وتنظيمه بوضوح، وهذا ما يركز عليه التصحيح الشخصي.
ابدأ تحضيرك لـ OET اليوم
اعرف مستواك مجاناً، ثم اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك، أو راسل فريق د. أحمد هشام على واتساب بمهنتك وموعد امتحانك والدولة المستهدفة.
