01 Read the case notes Five minutes, no writing, just planning.
02 Write your letter Forty minutes, about 180–200 words in the body.
03 Compare and get marked Check the model answer, then send your letter for correction.
What is a nursing referral letter in OET Writing?
OET Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. In a nursing referral, you ask another health professional, often a specialist nurse or clinic, to take on part of the patient's care, so the request and the reason for it must be clear from the first paragraph. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
What the examiner checks Six criteria: Purpose, Content, Conciseness & Clarity, Genre & Style, Organisation & Layout, and Language.
Case notes: diabetes review for Mr Raymond Doyle
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the specialist nurse needs before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mr Raymond Doyle
DOB: 11/02/1958 (68 y.o.)
Address: 14 Orchard Lane, Westbridge
Seen at Westbridge Health Centre for annual diabetes review: 21/10/2026
Social background Widowed April 2026; lives alone; cooking for himself since
Daughter visits weekly; happy to attend appointments with him
Retired postman; enjoys gardening
Ex-smoker (stopped 2010); occasional beer
Medical history and medicines T2DM (2016): metformin 1 g PO BD
Hypertension (2018): ramipril 5 mg OD
Cataract surgery R eye (2022)
NKDA
Nursing notes 21/10 HbA1c 75 mmol/mol (58 mmol/mol six months ago)
Reports increased thirst; diet irregular since wife's death (more takeaways and sweet snacks)
BP 136/82 mmHg; weight 92 kg (88 kg six months ago)
Foot check: reduced sensation both feet (monofilament); dry skin; small callus R heel; no ulcers
Often wears slippers outdoors as shoes feel tight
Pt keen to 'get back on track'
Plan Refer to diabetes specialist nurse: treatment review and education (diet, foot care)
Referred to community podiatry service
Advised daily foot checks and well-fitting footwear
GP informed of HbA1c result
Writing task
You are the practice nurse at Westbridge Health Centre. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter of referral to Ms Angela Brooks, Diabetes Specialist Nurse, Diabetes Centre, Westbridge General Hospital, Hill Road, Westbridge.
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences.
Do not use note form.
Use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task.
Model answer: nursing referral to a diabetes specialist nurse
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Ms Angela Brooks
Diabetes Specialist Nurse
Diabetes Centre
Westbridge General Hospital
Hill Road
Westbridge
21 October 2026
Dear Ms Brooks,
Re: Mr Raymond Doyle, DOB 11/02/1958
I am writing to refer Mr Doyle, aged 68, for a review of his type 2 diabetes, which has recently become poorly controlled, and for education on diet and foot care.
Mr Doyle was diagnosed in 2016 and takes metformin 1 g twice daily. At his annual review today, his HbA1c had risen from 58 to 75 mmol/mol over six months, and he reported increased thirst. Since his wife died in April, he has been cooking for himself and his diet has become irregular. He has also gained 4 kg.
On examination, monofilament testing showed reduced sensation in both feet. He has dry skin and a small callus on his right heel, but no ulcers. He often wears slippers outdoors because his shoes feel tight.
I would be grateful if you could review his treatment and provide education on diet and foot care. I have referred him to the community podiatry service and advised him to check his feet daily and wear well-fitting shoes.
Mr Doyle is motivated to improve his control. He lives alone, but his daughter visits weekly and is happy to attend appointments with him. Please contact me if you require further information.
Yours sincerely,
Practice Nurse
Westbridge Health Centre
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 196 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. According to OET, a Grade B letter typically scores 2 out of 3 for Purpose and 5 out of 7 for each of the other criteria. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The first sentence asks for two things, a treatment review and education, and says why: his diabetes has become poorly controlled. The specialist nurse knows the request before reading any history.
Content
Every included note supports the referral: the rising HbA1c, thirst, weight gain, the diet change after his bereavement, the foot findings and what has already been done. Stable history such as the cataract surgery is left out.
Conciseness & Clarity
The review is summarised in five short paragraphs. Several foot findings become two clear sentences, and the diet notes become one cause-and-effect point.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional, nurse to specialist colleague. The request is polite and specific, using “I would be grateful if you could”, and the bereavement is mentioned briefly and respectfully.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose first, then diabetes control, then the foot findings, then the request and actions already taken, then social support. Standard letter layout with the recipient, date and Re: line.
Language
Accurate tenses (past simple for today's findings, present perfect for the diet change since April), precise results and doses copied from the notes, and no note-form abbreviations such as BD, OD or R.
Included because the reader needs it Reason for referral: poor diabetes control and education needs
Metformin dose and year of diagnosis
HbA1c rise, thirst and weight gain
Irregular diet since his wife's death
Reduced sensation, dry skin and heel callus, with no ulcers
Slippers worn outdoors because shoes feel tight
Podiatry referral and advice already given
Motivation, living alone and daughter's support
Left out because it does not change the next step Retired postman and gardening
Cataract surgery in 2022
Ex-smoker since 2010 and occasional beer
Hypertension, ramipril and blood pressure (stable, not the reason for referral)
Exact details of takeaways and snacks
GP informed of the result (internal, not for the specialist nurse)
Common mistakes in OET nursing referral letters
These errors cost marks in nursing referrals again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Opening with the patient's history instead of the reason for referral.
Asking vaguely for the patient to be “seen” without saying what you want the specialist to do.
Copying every reading from the notes, including stable blood pressure and old surgery.
Leaving out what you have already done, such as the podiatry referral and foot-care advice.
Describing the bereavement at length instead of linking it briefly to the diet change.
Using note-form abbreviations such as BD, T2DM or y.o. in the letter.
Forgetting the social support that will help the specialist plan appointments.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips or see the OET course for nurses . Try the other practice letters too: the nursing discharge letter , the nursing referral letter , the nursing transfer letter , the medicine referral letter , the medicine discharge letter , the pharmacy letter to a GP , the physiotherapy discharge letter and the occupational therapy referral letter . All of them are listed on the free OET sample tests page.

Write your own nursing referral letter for this task in 40 minutes, then send it for OET writing correction . Each corrected letter comes back with an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp. If you are not sure your English is ready for OET yet, start with the free placement test .
Get your letter marked Writing assessment packages Free placement test
OET nursing referral letter FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET nursing referral letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
What should the first paragraph of a nursing referral say?
Who the patient is, what you are asking the reader to do and why. The examiner looks for the purpose straight away, so name the request, such as a treatment review and education, in the opening paragraph.
Should I mention personal or social details in a referral letter?
Only when they affect the care the reader will give. Here the bereavement explains the diet change and the daughter's support helps with appointments, but his former job and hobbies do not change the next step.
Can I get my OET nursing referral letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.

OET Medicine Writing
OET Medicine Discharge Letter Sample: Hospital to GP
This OET medicine discharge letter sample gives you a complete practice task: hospital case notes for a patient treated for pneumonia, the writing instructions, a model discharge letter to the GP and a criterion-by-criterion explanation of why it works. Write your own letter first, then compare.

How to use this sample
Write first, compare second.
Reading a model letter teaches far less than writing your own and then comparing. Use the timings below and treat it like the real test.
01 Read the case notes Five minutes, no writing, just planning.
02 Write your letter Forty minutes, about 180–200 words in the body.
03 Compare and get marked Check the model answer, then send your letter for correction.
What is a medicine discharge letter in OET Writing?
OET Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. In a discharge letter, a hospital doctor tells the GP what happened during the admission and, most importantly, what the GP needs to do next. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
What the examiner checks Six criteria: Purpose, Content, Conciseness & Clarity, Genre & Style, Organisation & Layout, and Language.
Case notes: discharge of Mr Graham Pierce
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the GP needs to act on before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mr Graham Pierce
DOB: 30/07/1964 (62 y.o.)
Admitted: 15/10/2026; discharged: 19/10/2026
Ward 4 (Respiratory), Riverside General Hospital
GP: Dr Sarah Lin, Riverside Surgery
Social background Lives with wife; works as a delivery driver
Smoker: 20 cigarettes/day for 40 years; wants to stop
Alcohol: 6 units/week
Medical history and medicines Hypertension (2019): ramipril 5 mg OD
Appendicectomy (1985)
NKDA
Hospital course 15/10: productive cough, fever 38.6°C, breathlessness; SpO2 92% on air
CXR: R lower lobe consolidation; diagnosis community-acquired pneumonia
IV amoxicillin + oral clarithromycin started
17/10: afebrile; switched to oral amoxicillin 500 mg TDS
19/10: SpO2 96% on air; mobilising independently; appetite improving
Discharge plan Complete oral amoxicillin 500 mg TDS until 22/10/2026
Continue ramipril 5 mg OD
Referred to community stop-smoking service
GP: arrange follow-up CXR in 6/52 to confirm resolution (age and smoking history)
Return advice: worsening breathlessness or fever
Writing task
You are the doctor on Ward 4, Riverside General Hospital. Mr Pierce is being discharged today. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to his GP, Dr Sarah Lin, Riverside Surgery, 22 Mill Street, Riverside.
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences.
Do not use note form.
Use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task.
Model answer: medicine discharge letter to the GP
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Dr Sarah Lin
General Practitioner
Riverside Surgery
22 Mill Street
Riverside
19 October 2026
Dear Dr Lin,
Re: Mr Graham Pierce, DOB 30/07/1964
I am writing to inform you that Mr Pierce, aged 62, was discharged today following treatment for community-acquired pneumonia. I would be grateful if you could arrange a follow-up chest X-ray in six weeks.
He was admitted on 15 October with a productive cough, fever and breathlessness, and his chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation. He was treated with intravenous amoxicillin and oral clarithromycin, and his fever settled within 48 hours. He was then switched to oral amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily, which he should complete on 22 October.
On discharge, his oxygen saturation was 96% on room air and he was mobilising independently. He should continue taking ramipril 5 mg once daily for his hypertension.
Given his age and his 40-year history of smoking 20 cigarettes a day, the follow-up chest X-ray is needed to confirm that the consolidation has resolved. He is keen to stop smoking and has been referred to the community stop-smoking service.
He has been advised to seek medical help if his breathlessness or fever returns. Please do not hesitate to contact me if you require further information.
Yours sincerely,
Ward Doctor
Ward 4, Riverside General Hospital
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 185 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. According to OET, a Grade B letter typically scores 2 out of 3 for Purpose and 5 out of 7 for each of the other criteria. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The opening paragraph says why the GP is receiving the letter and states the main action straight away: a follow-up chest X-ray in six weeks. The reason for that request is explained later, where it fits.
Content
The letter gives the diagnosis, the key findings, the treatment and the response, then everything the GP must act on or know: the antibiotic end date, the continued ramipril, the X-ray and the stop-smoking referral. Old surgery and alcohol are left out.
Conciseness & Clarity
Four days of ward notes become one paragraph on the admission. Observations are reduced to the two that matter, the fever settling and the oxygen saturation on discharge.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional, hospital doctor to GP colleague. Requests are polite (“I would be grateful if you could”), and the clinical terms suit a medical reader without over-explaining.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose and main request first, then the admission and treatment, then the discharge status and medicines, then the reason for the X-ray and the smoking plan, then safety-netting. Standard letter layout with the recipient, date and Re: line.
Language
Accurate tenses (past for the admission, present and modal verbs for the plan), dates and doses copied correctly, and no note-form abbreviations such as CXR, TDS, OD or SpO2.
Included because the reader needs it Reason for writing: discharge after community-acquired pneumonia
Request for a follow-up chest X-ray in six weeks, and why
Presenting symptoms and chest X-ray finding
Antibiotic treatment, response and end date of the oral course
Oxygen saturation and mobility on discharge
Continued ramipril for hypertension
Smoking history and stop-smoking referral
Advice to seek help if symptoms return
Left out because it does not change the next step Appendicectomy in 1985
Alcohol intake (6 units a week)
Job as a delivery driver
Exact temperature and admission oxygen saturation
Day-by-day ward observations
Improving appetite
Common mistakes in OET medicine discharge letters
These errors cost marks in discharge letters again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Hiding the GP's action, the follow-up chest X-ray, in the last paragraph without explaining why it is needed.
Retelling the admission day by day instead of summarising it.
Forgetting the end date of the antibiotic course.
Leaving out medicines the GP must continue, such as ramipril.
Copying every observation, including values that no longer matter.
Using note-form abbreviations such as CXR, TDS and SpO2 in the letter.
Missing the safety-netting advice the patient was given.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips or see the OET course for doctors . Try the other practice letters too: the nursing discharge letter , the nursing referral letter , the nursing transfer letter , the medicine referral letter , the medicine discharge letter , the pharmacy letter to a GP , the physiotherapy discharge letter and the occupational therapy referral letter . All of them are listed on the free OET sample tests page.

OET medicine discharge letter FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET medicine discharge letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
What does the GP need most from a discharge letter?
What to do next: medicines to finish or continue, follow-up tests and any referrals already made. Summarise the admission briefly, then make the actions easy to find.
Should I include every test result from the admission?
No. Include the results that explain the diagnosis and the follow-up, such as the chest X-ray finding and the oxygen saturation on discharge, and leave out readings that no longer affect care.
Can I get my OET discharge letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.

## OET Writing Sample for Occupational Therapy: Model Letter

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-writing-sample-occupational-therapy.html

Free OET writing sample for occupational therapists: home assessment case notes after a fall, a model referral letter and marking notes.

OET Occupational Therapy Writing
OET Writing Sample for Occupational Therapists: Referral Letter
This OET writing sample for occupational therapists gives you a complete practice task: hospital occupational therapy notes after a fall, including a home assessment, the writing instructions, a model referral to the community occupational therapy team and a criterion-by-criterion explanation of why it works. Write your own letter first, then compare.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 24 Oct 2026

How to use this sample
Write first, compare second.
Reading a model letter teaches far less than writing your own and then comparing. Use the timings below and treat it like the real test.
01 Read the case notes Five minutes, no writing, just planning.
02 Write your letter Forty minutes, about 180–200 words in the body.
03 Compare and get marked Check the model answer, then send your letter for correction.
What is the OET Writing task for occupational therapists?
OET Writing gives you 5 minutes to read the case notes and 40 minutes to write one letter, with a body of about 180–200 words. For occupational therapists, the letter is often a referral or handover to a community team, explaining the patient's function, what has been provided and what still needs to happen at home. This page gives you a full practice task, a model answer and an explanation of every selection decision.
Reading time: 5 minutes You read the case notes and the task before the writing time starts. Use it to decide who the reader is and what they must do next.
Writing time: 40 minutes You write one letter. A useful split is 5 minutes planning, 30 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking purpose, dates and doses.
How to use this sample Read the case notes, write your own letter under time and only then compare it with the model answer. Copying the model teaches far less than finding your own selection mistakes.
What the examiner checks Six criteria: Purpose, Content, Conciseness & Clarity, Genre & Style, Organisation & Layout, and Language.
Case notes: home assessment for Mrs Edna Fowler
These case notes describe a fictional patient and were written for practice. Read them for five minutes and decide what the community team needs before you look at the task.
Patient details Name: Mrs Edna Fowler
DOB: 03/09/1945 (81 y.o.)
Address: 6 Beech Road, Kingsford
Admitted after fall at home: 14/10/2026; discharge: 21/10/2026
Elderly Care Ward, Kingsford Hospital
Social background Widowed; lives alone in two-storey house; only bathroom upstairs
Daughter lives nearby and visits daily
Retired librarian; enjoys reading and baking
Previously independent; walked to local shops
Medical history Osteoarthritis both knees
Hypertension (on medication)
Cataracts (surgery 2021)
Fall 14/10: tripped on hallway rug; bruising L hip; X-ray: no fracture
Occupational therapy notes Mobilising independently with walking stick on the ward
Stairs: unsteady; managed safely with one rail and supervision
Home assessment 20/10: loose rugs removed (with pt's agreement)
Equipment provided: raised toilet seat, perching stool, bath board
Recommended second stair rail (not yet fitted)
Pt would prefer level-access shower in future
Pt anxious about falling again but keen to stay at home
Plan Refer to community occupational therapy team: second stair rail, review of bathing
Pendant alarm requested
Physiotherapy outpatient follow-up booked (balance)
Writing task
You are the occupational therapist on the Elderly Care Ward, Kingsford Hospital. Mrs Fowler is being discharged today. Using the information in the case notes, write a letter of referral to the Community Occupational Therapy Team, Kingsford Community Health Services, 40 Park Avenue, Kingsford.
Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences.
Do not use note form.
Use letter format.
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task.
Model answer: occupational therapy referral to the community team
Compare this model with your own letter. There is more than one way to score highly, but strong answers make the same selection decisions.
Community Occupational Therapy Team
Kingsford Community Health Services
40 Park Avenue
Kingsford
21 October 2026
Dear Colleagues,
Re: Mrs Edna Fowler, DOB 03/09/1945
I am writing to refer Mrs Fowler, aged 81, for community occupational therapy follow-up after a fall at home. She is being discharged today and needs further home adaptations to remain safely independent.
On 14 October, Mrs Fowler tripped on a rug in her hallway and bruised her left hip, but an X-ray showed no fracture. She now mobilises independently with a walking stick but is unsteady on the stairs. She lives alone in a two-storey house, and her only bathroom is upstairs.
During a home assessment on 20 October, the loose rugs were removed with her agreement, and she was given a raised toilet seat, a perching stool and a bath board. She managed the stairs safely with one rail and supervision.
I would be grateful if you could arrange the fitting of a second stair rail, which I have recommended, and review her bathing, as she would prefer a level-access shower in future. A pendant alarm has been requested.
Mrs Fowler is anxious about falling again but is keen to stay at home. Her daughter lives nearby and visits daily. Please contact me if you require further information.
Yours faithfully,
Occupational Therapist
Elderly Care Ward, Kingsford Hospital
Practice material written by OET with Dr Hesham. It is not an official OET test task. The body of this model answer is 190 words.
Why this letter works
The model is mapped to the six criteria examiners use. According to OET, a Grade B letter typically scores 2 out of 3 for Purpose and 5 out of 7 for each of the other criteria. Selection is the skill behind most of them, so the lists below show which case notes were kept and which were left out.
Purpose
The opening paragraph names the referral, community occupational therapy follow-up after a fall, and why it matters: further adaptations so she can stay safely at home. The detailed requests follow later, where they make sense.
Content
The letter keeps the fall and its outcome, her current mobility, the stair and bathroom problem, everything already done at the home visit, the two outstanding needs and her support. Hobbies, old surgery and her former job are left out.
Conciseness & Clarity
The home assessment becomes two sentences: what was removed and provided, then how she managed the stairs. The reader can see at a glance what is done and what is still needed.
Genre & Style
The tone is professional, therapist to therapist. Because the letter goes to a team rather than a named person, it opens with “Dear Colleagues” and closes with “Yours faithfully”.
Organisation & Layout
Purpose first, then the fall and current function, then the home assessment, then the requests, then her concerns and support. Standard letter layout with the recipient, date and Re: line.
Language
Accurate tenses (past for the fall and the visit, present for her current function), passive voice for actions completed by staff, and no note-form abbreviations such as pt or L.
Included because the reader needs it Reason for referral: community follow-up after a fall
Fall, bruised hip and no fracture
Walking stick, unsteady on stairs
Lives alone; only bathroom upstairs
Rugs removed and equipment provided
Second stair rail recommended but not yet fitted
Bathing review and preference for a level-access shower
Pendant alarm, anxiety about falling and daughter's support
Left out because it does not change the next step Retired librarian, reading and baking
Cataract surgery in 2021
Osteoarthritis and hypertension (not affecting this referral)
Walking to the shops before the fall
Physiotherapy outpatient follow-up (another team's plan)
Length of her hospital stay
Common mistakes in OET occupational therapy letters
These errors cost marks in occupational therapy letters again and again, and each one is easy to fix once you can see it.
Listing equipment without saying what still needs to be done at home.
Burying the main requests, the second stair rail and the bathing review, in the middle of the history.
Describing the whole medical history instead of the function that affects safety at home.
Forgetting that the only bathroom is upstairs, which explains why the stairs matter.
Using “Dear Sir or Madam” or a personal name when writing to a team.
Using note-form abbreviations such as pt, L and OT in the letter.
Leaving out her support at home and her wish to stay independent.
For the method behind these decisions, read the OET Writing tips or see OET for allied health professionals . Try the other practice letters too: the nursing discharge letter , the nursing referral letter , the nursing transfer letter , the medicine referral letter , the medicine discharge letter , the pharmacy letter to a GP , the physiotherapy discharge letter and the occupational therapy referral letter . All of them are listed on the free OET sample tests page.
Write your own version and get it marked
Write your own occupational therapy letter for this task in 40 minutes, then send it for OET writing correction . Each corrected letter comes back with an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp. If you are not sure your English is ready for OET yet, start with the free placement test .
Get your letter marked Writing assessment packages Free placement test
OET occupational therapy writing sample FAQ
More exam questions are answered on the full OET FAQ page .
How long should an OET occupational therapy letter be?
The body of the letter should be about 180–200 words. Writing a little more or less is not penalised on its own, but long letters usually include irrelevant case notes, which costs marks for content and conciseness.
Who do occupational therapists write to in OET Writing?
Often a community occupational therapy team, a GP or another service that will continue the patient's care at home. The reader decides what to include, so focus on function, safety and what still needs to happen.
How do I start and end a letter to a team rather than a person?
Use “Dear Colleagues” or a similar greeting when no individual is named, and close with “Yours faithfully”. When you write to a named person, use their name and close with “Yours sincerely”.
Can I get my OET occupational therapy letter marked?
Yes. Write your own version of this task under timed conditions, then send it for OET writing correction. You receive an estimated score, detailed correction and voice-note feedback on WhatsApp.
Next step Find out what your occupational therapy letter would score
Write this task under time, send it for correction and get an estimated score with voice-note feedback on exactly what to change.

## شرح Speaking OET ونصائح الـ Role-play للحصول على B

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/ar/oet-speaking-tips.html

شرح Speaking في OET: مدة الامتحان والـ role-plays ومعايير التقييم التسعة، وعبارات إنجليزية مفيدة لكل مرحلة، وأخطاء شائعة تمنعك من الدرجة B.

OET Speaking
شرح Speaking في OET: نصائح عملية للـ Role-play
امتحان المحادثة في OET مدته حوالي 20 دقيقة، وفيه موقفان (role-plays) خاصان بمهنتك: لكل موقف 3 دقائق تحضير ثم حوالي 5 دقائق تتحدث فيها مع محاور يؤدي دور المريض أو أحد أقاربه. سر الدرجة B ليس الإنجليزية المعقدة، بل حوار منظم بلغة يفهمها المريض، مع تعاطف حقيقي وتعامل آمن مع مخاوفه.
بقلم د. أحمد هشام ، طبيب ومؤسس OET with Dr Hesham · تحديث 24 أكتوبر 2026 Read in English
ابدأ اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني
اسأل على واتساب
الباقات
20 دقيقة تقريباً مدة امتحان المحادثة
2 موقف role-play خاص بمهنتك
9 معايير يُقيَّم عليها الأداء
كيف يكون امتحان المحادثة في OET؟
امتحان المحادثة حوار مهني قصير في موقف صحي حقيقي، وليس محادثة عامة. المحاور يؤدي دور المريض أو أحد أقاربه أو مرافقه، وأنت تؤدي دورك المهني كممرض أو طبيب أو صيدلي.
المدة
حوالي 20 دقيقة في المجموع، تبدأ بمقدمة قصيرة لا تدخل في الدرجة.
موقفان (role-plays)
موقفان خاصان بمهنتك، لكل موقف 3 دقائق تحضير ثم حوالي 5 دقائق أداء.
التسجيل والتصحيح
يُسجَّل الأداء صوتياً ويقيّمه مصححان على تسعة معايير منشورة.
على أي أساس تُقيَّم المحادثة في OET؟
تُقيَّم المحادثة على 4 معايير لغوية لكل منها 6 درجات، و5 معايير للتواصل الإكلينيكي لكل منها 3 درجات. يقول OET إن الدرجة B تعني غالباً 5 من 6 في كل معيار لغوي و2 من 3 في معايير التواصل الإكلينيكي.
المعيار النوع ماذا يعني
Intelligibility لغوي (من 6) وضوح النطق والتنغيم بحيث يفهمك المريض بسهولة.
Fluency لغوي (من 6) سلاسة الكلام وسرعته المناسبة دون توقف أو تردد زائد.
Appropriateness of Language لغوي (من 6) اختيار كلمات وأسلوب يناسبان المريض والموقف، بلا مصطلحات طبية معقدة.
Resources of Grammar and Expression لغوي (من 6) تنوع ودقة القواعد والتعبيرات التي تستخدمها.
Relationship-building تواصل إكلينيكي (من 3) بناء علاقة طيبة مع المريض واحترامه وإظهار التعاطف الحقيقي.
Understanding and incorporating the patient's perspective تواصل إكلينيكي (من 3) فهم مخاوف المريض وأفكاره وتوقعاته، وأخذها في الاعتبار عند الشرح.
Providing structure تواصل إكلينيكي (من 3) تنظيم الحوار في مراحل واضحة، واستخدام عبارات انتقالية تساعد المريض على المتابعة.
Information-gathering تواصل إكلينيكي (من 3) أسئلة منظمة ومفتوحة ثم محددة، مع الإصغاء الجيد وعدم المقاطعة.
Information-giving تواصل إكلينيكي (من 3) شرح المعلومات بالترتيب والقدر المناسبين، والتأكد من فهم المريض.
المصدر: OET Speaking .
طريقة ثابتة للـ Role-play مع عبارات مفيدة
بدلاً من حفظ حوار كامل، احفظ طريقة ثابتة من ست مراحل، واستخدم العبارات التالية بشكل طبيعي حسب ما يقوله المريض. العبارات بالإنجليزية كما ستقولها في الامتحان.
1. البداية
عرّف بنفسك ودورك، وتأكد من اسم المريض، ثم اسأله عن سبب حضوره بسؤال مفتوح. &ldquo;Hello, I'm one of the nurses here. Could you confirm your name for me, please?&rdquo; &ldquo;What can I help you with today?&rdquo;
2. جمع المعلومات
ابدأ بسؤال مفتوح ثم أسئلة محددة، واسمع قبل أن تشرح، واسأل عن مخاوف المريض. &ldquo;Could you tell me a bit more about that?&rdquo; &ldquo;Is there anything in particular that's worrying you?&rdquo;
3. الشرح بلغة بسيطة
حوّل المصطلح الطبي إلى كلام يفهمه المريض، واشرح خطوة بخطوة. &ldquo;In simple terms, this means…&rdquo; &ldquo;Let me explain what happens next.&rdquo;
4. التعاطف والتعامل مع المخاوف
اعترف بشعور المريض بكلام طبيعي غير محفوظ، ثم تعامل مع المخاوف مباشرة وبأمان دون طمأنة غير مسؤولة. &ldquo;I can see this is worrying for you.&rdquo; &ldquo;That's a very understandable concern.&rdquo;
5. الانتقال وتنظيم الحوار
استخدم عبارات انتقالية قصيرة تخبر المريض بما ستتحدثان عنه بعد ذلك. &ldquo;Now I'd like to talk about your medication.&rdquo; &ldquo;Before we finish, I'd like to check one more thing.&rdquo;
6. التأكد من الفهم والختام
اطلب من المريض أن يلخص ما فهمه، ثم اختم بخطوات واضحة ومتى يطلب المساعدة. &ldquo;Just to make sure I've explained that clearly, could you tell me what you'll do at home?&rdquo; &ldquo;Is there anything else you'd like to ask me?&rdquo;
نصائح عملية للحصول على B في المحادثة
هذه أهم النقاط من نصائح د. أحمد هشام الإحدى عشرة للمحادثة، والتي تفرق بين أداء يحصل على C وأداء يحصل على B.
حوار صحي، لا إنجليزية عامة
المصحح يقيّم تواصلك كممارس صحي، وليس فقط طلاقتك في الكلام.
البداية تحدد الانطباع
البداية الضعيفة أو المحفوظة تؤثر سريعاً على انطباع المصحح. ابدأ بشكل مهني وطبيعي ومرتبط بالموقف.
لغة يفهمها المريض
الكلام مع المريض يختلف عن الكلام مع زميل. حوّل المصطلحات الطبية إلى كلام بسيط واضح.
تعاطف حقيقي
المصحح يميز بين التعاطف الحقيقي والعبارات المحفوظة. استخدم التعاطف في مكانه الصحيح.
أسئلة منظمة
الأسئلة العشوائية تضعف الأداء. اتبع ترتيباً داخلياً واضحاً مع الحفاظ على حوار طبيعي.
لا تتجاهل مخاوف المريض
تجاهل القلق أو الاستعجال في الرد عليه من أسرع طرق خسارة الدرجات.
الشرح من أكثر المهارات تقييماً
قدّم المعلومات بالترتيب الصحيح وبالقدر المناسب، وتأكد من فهم المريض.
الطمأنة غير الآمنة خطر
لا تَعِد المريض بشيء لا تستطيع ضمانه. اعرف ما تقوله وما لا تقوله عندما يكون المريض قلقاً.
إدارة الوقت
كل موقف قصير. الطريقة الثابتة تساعدك على تغطية المطلوب دون استعجال.
أخطاء شائعة تمنعك من الدرجة B
كثير من المرشحين يتدربون كثيراً، لكن الدرجة لا تتحسن إلا عندما يصحح التدريب المشكلة الصحيحة.
استخدام إنجليزية عامة غير مهنية. الامتحان يكافئ التواصل المهني في المجال الصحي، لا الحديث اليومي.
بداية محفوظة. الحوار المحفوظ نادراً ما يناسب الموقف الموجود في البطاقة.
الشرح بالمصطلحات الطبية. المريض يحتاج كلاماً واضحاً، لا لغة الزملاء.
تجاهل مخاوف المريض. كل قلق يجب الاعتراف به والتعامل معه بأمان.
طمأنة غير مسؤولة. عبارات مثل الوعد بأن كل شيء سيكون بخير قد تبدو غير آمنة للمصحح.
نفاد الوقت. الموقف بلا ترتيب داخلي غالباً ينتهي مستعجلاً أو ناقصاً.
نماذج Role-play مع إجابات نموذجية
أفضل طريقة للتطبيق: حضّر البطاقة في 3 دقائق، ونفّذ الموقف بصوت عالٍ في 5 دقائق، ثم قارن أداءك بالإجابة النموذجية. النماذج التالية باللغة الإنجليزية مثل الامتحان.
Role-play للتمريض
موقفان تدريبيان للتمريض مع إجابة نموذجية كاملة وشرح لكل خطوة.
Nursing role-play cards
Role-play للأطباء
موقفان تدريبيان للأطباء، منهما شرح تشخيص جديد لمريض قلق، مع إجابة نموذجية.
Medicine role-play cards
Role-play للصيادلة
موقفان تدريبيان للصيادلة، منهما شرح استخدام بخاخ جديد، مع إجابة نموذجية.
Pharmacy role-play cards
Role-play للعلاج الطبيعي
موقفان تدريبيان للعلاج الطبيعي، منهما ألم أسفل الظهر، مع إجابة نموذجية.
Physiotherapy role-play cards
تريد ملاحظات على أدائك؟ احجز جلسة Speaking فردية مباشرة مع ملاحظات تفصيلية بعد الجلسة.
أسئلة شائعة عن المحادثة في OET
إجابات مختصرة لأكثر الأسئلة شيوعاً.
كم مدة امتحان المحادثة في OET؟
حوالي 20 دقيقة: مقدمة قصيرة لا تدخل في الدرجة، ثم موقفان (role-plays) خاصان بمهنتك. لكل موقف 3 دقائق تحضير ثم حوالي 5 دقائق أداء مع المحاور.
على أي أساس يُقيَّم الـ Speaking في OET؟
على 4 معايير لغوية لكل منها 6 درجات، و5 معايير للتواصل الإكلينيكي لكل منها 3 درجات. يُسجَّل الأداء ويقيّمه مصححان، ويقول OET إن الدرجة B تعني غالباً 5 من 6 في المعايير اللغوية و2 من 3 في معايير التواصل الإكلينيكي.
ما الدرجة المطلوبة في المحادثة؟
تطلب NMC وGMC وNMBI وECFMG درجة 350 (B) في المحادثة. أما Ahpra فتطلب 360 للاختبارات من 23 أبريل 2026، وتطلب CGFNS VisaScreen للممرضين المسجلين 360 للاختبارات من 12 مايو 2026.
هل أحفظ جملاً جاهزة للـ Speaking؟
لا تحفظ حواراً كاملاً، لأن كل موقف مختلف والمصحح يلاحظ الكلام المحفوظ. احفظ طريقة ثابتة للحوار وبعض العبارات المفيدة لكل مرحلة، واستخدمها بشكل طبيعي حسب ما يقوله المريض.
هل يمكن التدرب على الـ Speaking مع مدرس؟
نعم. جلسة Speaking الفردية المباشرة مع د. أحمد هشام تستخدم مواقف OET مختلفة وتنتهي بملاحظات تفصيلية على أدائك، ويمكن حجز جلسة واحدة أو جلستين.
ابدأ تحضيرك لـ OET اليوم
اعرف مستواك مجاناً، ثم اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك، أو راسل فريق د. أحمد هشام على واتساب بمهنتك وموعد امتحانك والدولة المستهدفة.
اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني واتساب

## نماذج امتحان OET مجانية 2026: رسمية وتدريبية

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/ar/oet-sample-tests.html

نماذج امتحان OET المجانية لكل مهنة من موقع OET الرسمي، ونماذج رسائل ومواقف role-play بإجابات نموذجية، وطريقة التدريب الصحيحة على الوقت.

OET Sample Tests
نماذج امتحان OET المجانية ومواد التدريب
ينشر OET نماذج امتحانات رسمية مجانية لكل مهنة على موقعه، بالشكل الورقي وشكل الكمبيوتر. في هذه الصفحة تجد روابطها مرتبة حسب المهنة، ومعها نماذج رسائل ومواقف role-play مجانية بإجابات نموذجية من د. أحمد هشام، وطريقة التدريب عليها في نفس توقيت الامتحان.

نماذج OET الرسمية لكل مهنة
ينشر OET نماذج امتحانات رسمية على موقعه لكل مهنة، بالشكل الورقي وشكل الكمبيوتر. الاستماع والقراءة واحدان لكل المهن، أما الكتابة والمحادثة فاختر نموذج مهنتك. بعض المهن ليس لها صفحة كمبيوتر منفصلة، فالرابط يوصلك إلى صفحة نماذج الكمبيوتر العامة.

حاسبة درجات OET

شرح كتابة رسالة OET
المعايير الستة وخطوات الكتابة والأخطاء الشائعة بالعربي.
شرح الكتابة
شرح Speaking في OET
معايير التقييم التسعة وعبارات مفيدة لكل مرحلة بالعربي.
شرح المحادثة
كيف تتدرب على نماذج OET بالطريقة الصحيحة؟
النموذج يفيدك فقط إذا تدربت عليه في نفس ظروف الامتحان ثم راجعت أخطاءك.
الاستماع في وقته. حوالي 40 دقيقة و42 سؤالاً في 3 أجزاء، ويُسمع كل تسجيل مرة واحدة فقط. لا توقف التسجيل أثناء التدريب.
القراءة في وقتها. 60 دقيقة و42 سؤالاً، والجزء A وحده 15 دقيقة بالضبط. التزم بالوقت لأن الجزء A يُسحب بعد 15 دقيقة.
الكتابة في وقتها. 5 دقائق قراءة ثم 40 دقيقة كتابة لرسالة واحدة، وحوالي 180 إلى 200 كلمة في متن الرسالة.
المحادثة بصوت عالٍ. 3 دقائق تحضير ثم حوالي 5 دقائق لكل موقف، ويُفضل أن تسجل صوتك وتراجعه.
راجع نتيجتك بواقعية. يقول OET إن الدرجة B في الاستماع والقراءة تحتاج عادةً 30 من 42 على الأقل، لكن الحد يختلف قليلاً من نسخة لأخرى.
اطلب تقييماً للكتابة والمحادثة. لا يمكنك تصحيح الكتابة والمحادثة بنفسك بدقة. استخدم تصحيح الكتابة و جلسة Speaking فردية ، أو امتحاناً تجريبياً كاملاً مصححاً.
هل الـ recalls نماذج امتحان؟
الـ recalls هي ما يتذكره المرشحون من امتحانات سابقة ويتداولونه بعد الامتحان، وليست مادة رسمية من OET. قد تفيدك في معرفة نوع المواضيع، لكن لتتعلم الشكل الحقيقي للامتحان وتوقيته اعتمد على نماذج OET الرسمية.
أسئلة شائعة عن نماذج امتحان OET
إجابات مختصرة لأكثر الأسئلة شيوعاً.
هل نماذج امتحان OET مجانية؟
نعم. ينشر OET نماذج امتحانات رسمية لكل مهنة على موقعه، للاختبار الورقي واختبار الكمبيوتر. ونماذج الرسائل ومواقف الـ role-play وحاسبة الدرجات واختبار تحديد المستوى عندنا مجانية أيضاً.
أين أجد نماذج OET للتمريض؟
النموذج الرسمي للتمريض بالشكل الورقي موجود على موقع OET، ونماذج الكمبيوتر موجودة في صفحة نماذج الكمبيوتر على نفس الموقع. وللتدريب الإضافي استخدم نموذجي رسالة الخروج والنقل ومواقف الـ role-play للتمريض عندنا.
كم إجابة صحيحة أحتاج للدرجة B في الاستماع والقراءة؟
في الاستماع والقراءة 42 سؤالاً لكل منهما. يقول OET إن من يحصل على الدرجة B (350) يحصل عادةً على 30 من 42 على الأقل، لكن الحد يتغير قليلاً من نسخة امتحان لأخرى.
هل الـ recalls هي نفسها نماذج الامتحان؟
لا. الـ recalls هي ما يتذكره المرشحون من امتحانات سابقة ويتداولونه بعد الامتحان، وليست مادة رسمية من OET. استخدم نماذج OET الرسمية لتتعلم الشكل الحقيقي للامتحان وتوقيته.
هل يمكن تصحيح الرسالة التي أكتبها على النموذج؟
نعم. اكتب الرسالة في الوقت المحدد، ثم استخدم خدمة تصحيح الكتابة: يصحح د. أحمد كل رسالة يدوياً ويعطيك درجة تقديرية وتصحيحاً تفصيلياً وملاحظات صوتية على واتساب.
ابدأ تحضيرك لـ OET اليوم
اعرف مستواك مجاناً، ثم اختر الباقة المناسبة لمهنتك، أو راسل فريق د. أحمد هشام على واتساب بمهنتك وموعد امتحانك والدولة المستهدفة.
اختبار تحديد المستوى المجاني واتساب

Our History
Our Story of Growth & Impact
2018
2019
2020
2021
2022
2023
2024
2026
2018 - The Beginning
OET with Dr Hesham started with a clear mission: to help healthcare professionals prepare for the exam with practical guidance instead of generic lessons.
The early focus was simple and strong: build confidence in communication, make feedback clear, and support learners with realistic exam expectations.
That foundation shaped the coaching style learners still know today: direct, structured, and results-focused.
2019 - Building Trust
More nurses, doctors, and pharmacists began joining the program for speaking and writing support.
The coaching approach became more personalized, with stronger correction cycles and more direct exam preparation.
Word-of-mouth growth came from learners who valued practical support and visible progress.
2020 - Stronger Online Support
Remote learning became a bigger part of OET preparation, and the teaching model adapted quickly.
Learners gained easier access to guided materials, live practice, and clearer communication around exam strategy.
This period strengthened the digital side of the coaching experience.
2021 - Focused Skill Training
Speaking role-plays, writing correction, reading technique, and listening strategies became even more targeted.
Training moved closer to the realities of the actual exam and the professional communication learners needed in the UK.
This helped students prepare with greater confidence and clarity.
2022 - Pathway Guidance Expanded
Learners increasingly needed support beyond exam practice, especially around UK job preparation and next steps.
Guidance expanded to include more pathway-focused coaching alongside core OET preparation.
That made the learning journey more complete and more relevant.
2023 - Community Growth
More learners joined through online communities, referrals, and shared success stories.
The brand became a trusted place for practical OET help, especially for healthcare professionals preparing for the UK pathway.
Community support became a major strength of the platform.
2024 - More Structure, More Results
Preparation pathways became more organized, with clearer session goals and stronger learner follow-through.
The coaching model continued improving around accountability, speed, and focused feedback.
That made performance gains more measurable and consistent.
2026 - Looking Ahead
The vision continues to grow: better preparation, stronger learner support, and more practical guidance for healthcare professionals aiming to work in the UK.
The goal remains the same: make OET preparation more human, more focused, and more effective.
Every new section of the platform is built around that promise.

## OET FAQs: Exam Format, Scores, Booking & Results | Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/faq.html

Answers to 30+ OET exam questions: test format, sub-tests, score requirements and retakes, booking, OET@Home, results and review of marking.

Frequently Asked Questions
OET Exam FAQs
A complete candidate reference guide with 32 frequently asked questions, organised by topic for healthcare professionals preparing for OET.
Q1–Q3
Before Starting OET
Start with the right English foundation before serious exam preparation.
Q1 Can I take OET if my English level is B1?
Answer: You can technically start preparing, but you are usually not ready for the real OET exam at B1 level.
Recommendation: Start with a Basic English Course first, then move to OET preparation when your English is closer to B2 level.
Q2 What English level do I need before starting OET?
Answer: Most candidates need at least a strong B1+/B2 foundation before serious OET preparation.
Recommendation: If your grammar, vocabulary, listening or sentence structure is weak, start with Foundation English and Medical English before full OET training.
Q3 Is OET easier than IELTS?
Answer: OET may feel easier for healthcare professionals because the topics are medical and healthcare-related, but it is still a high-level English exam.
Recommendation: Choose OET if you are a doctor, nurse, pharmacist, dentist, physiotherapist or another healthcare professional.
Q4–Q8
Exam Format
Understand the structure, profession-specific tasks, and preparation timeline.
Q4 What are the four OET sub-tests?
Answer: OET has four sub-tests: Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking.
Recommendation: Prepare for all four skills because most regulators require scores in each sub-test, not just an overall result.
Q5 Which professions can take OET?
Answer: OET is designed for healthcare professionals, including doctors, nurses, pharmacists, dentists, physiotherapists and other healthcare-related professions.
Recommendation: Choose the correct profession when booking because Writing and Speaking are profession-specific.
Q6 Is OET Writing the same for all professions?
Answer: No. Writing is profession-specific. For example, Medicine candidates receive medical case notes, while Nursing candidates receive nursing-related case notes.
Recommendation: Study writing letters specific to your profession, not generic OET letters.
Q7 Is OET Speaking the same for all professions?
Answer: No. Speaking role-plays are profession-specific and based on realistic healthcare situations.
Recommendation: Practise role-plays related to your profession, common patient concerns and real clinical communication.
Q8 Can I prepare for OET in one month?
Answer: It depends on your current English level. Strong candidates may improve quickly, but weaker candidates usually need more time.
Recommendation: Take a level assessment first. If your basics are weak, do not rush to book the exam.
Q9–Q16
Scores, Requirements and Retake Rules
Clarify score requirements, validity, clubbing, resits, and regulator rules.
Q9 Can I pass OET without a course?
Answer: Some candidates can, especially if their English is already strong and they understand the exam format.
Recommendation: A structured course is better if you struggle with Writing, Speaking, time management or exam strategy.
Q10 What score do I need to pass OET?
Answer: There is no single pass score for everyone. Required scores depend on the regulator, country and profession. For example, some organisations require Grade B (350) in specific sub-tests, while Australia (AHPRA) now uses a numeric scoring system with separate minimums for each sub-test.
Recommendation: Check the exact requirement for your target regulator before booking the exam. Do not assume a generic Grade B will be enough.
Q11 What is Grade B in OET?
Answer: Grade B usually corresponds to a score of 350 or above on the OET scale (0–500). Letter grades range from A (highest) to E (lowest).
Recommendation: Aim higher than the minimum because small mistakes can affect your final score.
Q12 How long is my OET score valid?
Answer: OET does not set a validity period: each regulator decides. Most, including the NMC, GMC, HCPC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, Ahpra and the Medical Council of New Zealand, accept results up to 2 years old, while the Nursing Council of New Zealand allows sittings within the 3 years before your application.
Recommendation: If your registration or application process may take longer than two years, plan to retake OET before your current score expires. Always confirm the validity rule with your specific regulator.
Q13 Is OET accepted for visa or immigration purposes?
Answer: OET is primarily used for professional registration of healthcare workers. Some countries also accept OET for healthcare-related visa categories, but acceptance for general immigration purposes is limited and depends on the country.
Recommendation: If you need English for a visa, confirm directly with the immigration authority or your registered advisor before booking — do not assume acceptance based on professional registration alone.
Q14 Can I retake only one sub-test (Single Sub-Test Resit)?
Answer: OET offers a Single Sub-Test Resit booking option, but only on OET Test on Paper and only at venues outside the USA. Acceptance is decided by your regulator, not by OET. The major regulators that do NOT accept single sub-test resits include: the UK NMC (nurses), the UK GMC (doctors), the UK Foundation Programme (UKFPO), Australia (AHPRA), and the USA (where single sub-test resits cannot be booked at USA venues at all). Some other regulators may accept it, but this is the exception, not the rule.
Recommendation: Before booking a single sub-test resit, confirm in writing with your regulator that they accept it. If you are applying to the UK, USA or Australia, do not rely on a single sub-test resit — plan a full retake or use clubbing where the regulator allows it.
Q15 What is OET score clubbing, and which regulators accept it?
Answer: Clubbing means combining results from two FULL OET sittings (not single sub-test resits) to meet the required scores. Each sitting must include all four sub-tests, and strict conditions apply on minimum scores per sub-test and the time window between sittings. Regulators that DO accept clubbing include: the UK NMC (two sittings within 12 months, with no score below C+ (300) in Listening, Reading or Speaking or below C (250) in Writing in either sitting), Australia's AHPRA (two sittings within 12 months, with minimum floors in each sitting), the Nursing Council of New Zealand and the Medical Council of New Zealand. Regulators that do NOT accept clubbing include the UK GMC, Ireland's NMBI and Medical Council, and ECFMG in the USA, which require all four scores from one sitting.
Recommendation: Clubbing is your main safety net if you miss one or two sub-tests by a small margin. Before booking the second sitting, check your regulator's exact rules — time window, minimum sub-test scores and allowed combinations — and plan strategically. Do not assume clubbing is available; it is regulator-specific.
Q16 What OET score do I need for AHPRA registration in Australia?
Answer: AHPRA (Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency) updated its OET requirements on 23 April 2026 to align with new score concordance research. The required English proficiency level has NOT changed — only the scoring format has changed. Your test date determines which rules apply. For tests taken on or before 22 April 2026: the old letter-grade requirements apply — Grade B (350) in Listening, Reading and Speaking, and Grade C+ (300) in Writing. For tests taken on or after 23 April 2026: numeric requirements apply — Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350, Speaking 360. The letter-grade system no longer applies to AHPRA assessments from this date. AHPRA accepts results from one sitting or from clubbing two sittings within a 12-month period (where the first sitting is assessed against the old standard and the second against the new). AHPRA does NOT accept OET@Home and does NOT accept single sub-test resits.
Recommendation: Check your test date carefully. If you are still preparing for the test, aim for the new numeric thresholds — Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350, Speaking 360 — because these are now the standard for any test taken from 23 April 2026 onwards.
Q17–Q21
Sub-test Details
Review marks, timings, grading criteria, and smart exam technique.
Q17 How many marks are there in OET Listening?
Answer: OET Listening has 42 marks in total. Part A has 24 marks, Part B has 6 marks, and Part C has 12 marks.
Recommendation: Do not focus only on Part A. Parts B and C are very important for reaching Grade B.
Q18 How many questions are there in OET Reading?
Answer: OET Reading has 42 questions, and each correct answer gives one mark before conversion to the OET score scale.
Recommendation: Practise Reading Part A under strict timing because it is often the most stressful part.
Q19 Is there negative marking in OET?
Answer: No. There is no penalty for wrong answers in Listening or Reading, so it is better to attempt every question than to leave it blank.
Recommendation: If you are not certain, make your best informed guess. An empty answer cannot earn marks; a guess might.
Q20 How long does each OET sub-test take?
Answer: Listening takes approximately 40 to 45 minutes, Reading takes 60 minutes, Writing takes 45 minutes, and Speaking takes around 20 minutes. Listening, Reading and Writing are usually delivered back-to-back; Speaking may be scheduled separately.
Recommendation: Train your stamina with full-length timed mocks, not just isolated practice tasks. Exam-day fatigue is real.
Q21 How are OET Writing and Speaking graded?
Answer: OET Writing is marked by trained assessors against criteria including purpose, content, conciseness and clarity, genre and style, organisation and layout, and language. OET Speaking is marked against criteria including intelligibility, fluency, appropriateness of language, resources of grammar and expression, and clinical communication skills. Raw marks are then converted to the 0–500 OET scale.
Recommendation: Do not just write or speak more — match the assessment criteria. Knowing what the assessors look for is more important than producing extra content.
Q22–Q26
Booking, Test Modes and Exam Day
Choose the right test mode and avoid booking or ID mistakes.
Q22 Can I take OET on computer?
Answer: Yes. OET can be taken on computer in available locations. The Listening, Reading and Writing sections are completed on computer.
Recommendation: If you type faster than you write, computer-based OET may be the better choice for you.
Q23 Can I take OET on paper?
Answer: Yes. OET Test on Paper is available in selected locations and includes the four sub-tests: Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking.
Recommendation: Choose paper-based OET if you are more comfortable handwriting your Writing letter.
Q24 Is OET@Home accepted everywhere?
Answer: Not necessarily. Acceptance depends on the regulator or organisation you are applying to. The NMC and the GMC accept OET@Home, and ECFMG accepts it only when there is no test venue in your country. Ahpra, the HCPC, the GPhC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, the Nursing Council of New Zealand and CGFNS VisaScreen do not accept it.
Recommendation: Before booking OET@Home, confirm in writing that your target regulator accepts it.
Q25 What ID do I need on exam day?
Answer: You must bring the same valid, government-issued photo ID (usually a passport) that you used when booking the test. Expired IDs are not accepted, and the name on your booking must match the ID exactly.
Recommendation: Check your passport expiry well before the test date and book in the exact name on your passport — no nicknames, shortened forms or different spellings.
Q26 Can I cancel or reschedule my OET booking?
Answer: Yes, for a fee. Rescheduling costs AU$120 up to the booking closing date and AU$200 after it, and a paper test cannot be rescheduled after 11:59 pm local time on the day before the test. Cancelling costs AU$120 before the booking closing date and AU$200 after it: a paper test can be cancelled up to one week before the test day, and a computer or OET@Home test up to 48 hours before the start, but not once you have taken any sub-test. In the USA, rescheduling a computer or OET@Home test costs US$95, or US$155 less than 7 days before the test.
Recommendation: If you are not confident you will be ready, postpone before the cut-off date. Do not waste a booking on a date you are not prepared for.
Q27–Q32
Preparation, Results and Review
Prepare strategically, check readiness, and understand results or reviews.
Q27 What is the hardest OET sub-test?
Answer: It depends on the candidate. Many candidates find Writing and Listening Part C difficult, while others struggle with Reading Part A timing.
Recommendation: Take a mock test first to identify your weakest sub-test, then focus your preparation accordingly.
Q28 How can I know if I am ready for OET?
Answer: You are ready when you can consistently achieve your target score in timed mock tests across all four sub-tests.
Recommendation: Do not rely on one good practice test. You need repeated, stable performance before booking.
Q29 Should I memorise OET letters?
Answer: No. Memorising full letters is risky because case notes change in every exam.
Recommendation: Learn structure, selection of relevant information, professional tone and common letter types instead.
Q30 What should I do if I failed OET before?
Answer: Do not repeat the exam immediately without analysing why you failed.
Recommendation: Check your score breakdown, identify the weak sub-test, take targeted training, then book again when your mock scores are stable.
Q31 When will I receive my OET results?
Answer: For OET on Computer and OET@Home, results can arrive in as little as 48 hours after you finish all four sub-tests, and 95% of OET on Computer results are released within 6 calendar days. For OET on Paper, results are released from 13 days after the test date, or from 5 days in India and the Philippines. Results appear in your OET candidate account, and OET describes all timeframes as indicative.
Recommendation: Use the waiting period productively — plan your next step (registration, application or further preparation) rather than refreshing the results page.
Q32 Can I request a review of marking if I disagree with my score?
Answer: Yes. OET offers a Review of Marking service for candidates who believe their score is lower than expected. Requests must be made within 72 hours of results being released. The fee is AU$120 (US$95 in the USA) per sub-test and is refunded if your grade changes.
Recommendation: Request a review only if your sub-test score is much lower than your consistent mock test performance — not just because you hoped for a higher grade.
Ready to prepare? Start with the free placement test , then compare the OET course for nurses , the OET course for doctors and OET writing correction . Planning your sitting? See the OET test dates and fees , the score requirements by regulator and the OET score calculator . Registering abroad? Check the UK , USA , Australia and Gulf pathway guides.

Complete OET Writing Tips
OET Writing Tips That Protect Your Score
These writing tips from Dr Hesham form a clear study checklist for referral letters, discharge letters, transfer letters, and profession-specific OET writing tasks.
11 Writing priorities covering letter type, reader awareness, selection, tone, accuracy, closing requests, and final review.
01 Letter type matters more than you think
Every OET task belongs to a specific letter type, and recognising which one changes your structure, tone, and final request. Most candidates skip this step and lose marks they could easily have kept.
Why this matters: Your structure should change before you write the first sentence.
02 Know who is reading
A doctor, nurse, pharmacist, employer, and patient each need the letter written differently. Writing the same way for every reader is one of the most common reasons candidates plateau at Grade C.
Why this matters: Audience awareness controls tone, detail, and the final request.
03 Selection is the real skill
OET Writing is not about including everything from the case notes. The harder skill, and the one that separates Grade B from Grade A, is choosing what to leave out.
Why this matters: Featured because relevance is often the difference between a busy letter and a scoring letter.
04 A weak introduction costs you marks fast
Examiners want to understand instantly why the letter exists. There is a specific way of opening that works for almost every case, and most candidates never learn it.
Why this matters: The opening gives the examiner confidence that you understood the task.
05 Order matters more than candidates realise
A strong letter follows a clear internal sequence. A weak letter jumps between problems and dates without a clear path. Most candidates feel they have a system until they see one that actually works.
Why this matters: Organisation makes clinical information easier to assess.
06 Long letters are usually weak letters
Writing more does not mean scoring higher. A focused, well-organised letter consistently outperforms a long one full of unnecessary detail.
Why this matters: Concise writing shows judgement and protects accuracy.
07 Tone is assessed in every paragraph
Casual, emotional, or judgemental wording quietly drags your score down. Professional language is a skill, not a default, and small word choices make a big difference to your final band.
Why this matters: Professional tone must be maintained from start to finish.
08 Accuracy beats complexity
Trying to sound advanced often introduces grammar mistakes. The strongest candidates write more simply than you would expect.
Why this matters: Clear, correct language beats risky phrasing.
09 The closing paragraph is more important than candidates think
The final request is one of the most heavily assessed parts of the letter. Getting this wrong can pull down your score even when the rest is strong.
Why this matters: Featured because the final request must match the task and recipient precisely.
10 Memorising letters does not work
Every case is different, and memorisation fails the moment the task changes. What works is a repeatable method - the same one strong candidates use across every letter type.
Why this matters: A method adapts. A memorised letter breaks.
11 The strongest candidates always review
Before submitting, every letter needs a final check against a clear list of criteria. Most candidates skip this. The ones who pass never do.
Why this matters: Reviewing catches avoidable scoring errors before submission.
Grade B+ insight
These tips show you what examiners are looking for. Knowing the exact techniques, structures, and phrasing that earn Grade B and above is what we teach inside the course.
Get writing resources
Read Writing Tips Ask for writing support
Complete OET Speaking Tips
OET Speaking Tips for Patient-Centred Role-Plays
These speaking tips help healthcare professionals move beyond general English and practise the exact communication behaviours examiners expect in OET role-plays.
11 Speaking priorities covering openings, patient-friendly language, empathy, questioning, concerns, explanation, signposting, reassurance, and timing.
01 OET Speaking is a healthcare conversation
It is not casual English. Examiners assess how well you communicate as a healthcare professional, and that is very different from everyday speaking.
Why this matters: You are assessed on professional communication, not just fluency.
02 Your opening sets the tone
A weak or memorised opening immediately affects the examiner's impression. There is a way of starting that consistently works, and most candidates do not use it.
Why this matters: The first seconds establish control, warmth, and purpose.
03 Patient-friendly language is essential
Speaking to a patient is not the same as speaking to a colleague. Medical terms need to be reshaped into clearer wording, and this is something many candidates underestimate until they fail.
Why this matters: Featured because patient-friendly explanation is central to OET role-play performance.
04 Empathy must sound real
Examiners can tell the difference between genuine and memorised empathy. Where and how you use it matters as much as what you say.
Why this matters: Empathy has to respond to the patient, not sound pasted in.
05 Questioning needs structure
Random questions weaken your role-play. Strong candidates follow a quiet internal structure that still sounds completely natural to the patient.
Why this matters: Structured questions help you gather information without sounding robotic.
06 Patient concerns must be handled correctly
Ignoring, rushing, or dismissing a concern is one of the fastest ways to lose marks. There is a specific way of responding that examiners look for.
Why this matters: Featured because concerns are where safety, empathy, and communication meet.
07 Explanation is one of the most assessed skills
Giving information clearly, in the right order, at the right depth, is also one of the most commonly mishandled parts of the role-play.
Why this matters: Good explanations are organised, simple, and checked for understanding.
08 Signposting guides the conversation
Strong candidates lead the role-play without dominating it. This is done through small linking phrases that most candidates never use.
Why this matters: Signposting helps the patient follow your reasoning.
09 Reassurance can be dangerous
The wrong type of reassurance sounds unsafe to an examiner. Knowing what to say, and what not to say, is critical.
Why this matters: Safe reassurance avoids false promises and keeps trust realistic.
10 Patient-centred communication scores higher
Speaking to the patient is not the same as speaking with them. The role-play must feel like a real two-way interaction.
Why this matters: The patient should feel involved, not lectured.
11 Time management changes everything
Each role-play is short. Strong candidates cover every required area without rushing, and they do it the same way every time.
Why this matters: A repeatable flow helps you finish calmly and completely.
Examiner-focused communication
These tips show you what examiners are looking for. Knowing the exact techniques, structures, and phrasing that earn Grade B and above is what we teach inside the course.
Practise speaking

Quick answers to common OET questions
These short answers are designed for learners who need clarity before joining a class, group, or orientation session.
Quick answer: How do I improve OET writing fast? Practise task selection, paragraph order, and purpose-driven language. One corrected letter with detailed feedback is usually more valuable than writing five unreviewed letters.
Best for nurses Focus on discharge, referral, and patient education letters plus speaking role-plays that require empathy, reassurance, and safe instructions.
Best for doctors Prioritise concise clinical explanation, patient-friendly speaking, and letters that communicate risk, urgency, and follow-up clearly.
Common mistake Many candidates copy too much from case notes. OET rewards selection and communication, not information dumping.
What to do next Join exam recalls, choose one weekly writing task, record one speaking role-play, and review mistakes before adding new material.
UK pathway tip OET preparation should support your professional communication goals, not only the exam score. Practise the language you will use with patients and employers.
Profession-specific OET preparation focus
Choose the route that matches your healthcare role and build practice around realistic communication tasks.
Nurses
Use nursing role-plays, patient education, discharge advice, and referral writing to build confidence for real clinical communication.
Doctors
Practise diagnosis explanation, risk communication, treatment options, and concise clinical letters for patient-centred outcomes.
Pharmacists
Strengthen medication counselling, safety advice, patient questions, and clear written communication for pharmacy scenarios.
OET tips FAQ
Short answers to the questions learners ask before they choose materials, groups, or guided coaching.
What is the best way to start OET preparation?
Start with a diagnostic writing task and one speaking role-play. Then build a weekly plan around your weakest skill and your profession.
Are OET tips different for nurses and doctors?
The scoring criteria are shared, but the scenarios, role-play language, patient concerns, and letter purposes differ by profession.
Can free OET materials be enough?
Free materials can help you start, but feedback is what reveals repeated mistakes. Use free groups for exposure and corrections for targeted improvement.

Letter-focused route

How to approach OET Writing with a repeatable method
These are the points examiners look for. This section turns them into a practical preparation route.
Letter type and reader
Start by identifying whether the task is a referral, discharge, transfer, update, request or patient-facing letter. Then adjust tone and detail for the reader.
Selection and organisation
Choose the details that serve the purpose. Group related information logically so the reader can act without searching.
Tone, accuracy and final review
Use professional, concise language. Prioritise accurate sentences over complex grammar, then check purpose, content, layout and final request.
Common mistakes that keep writing scores stuck
Most candidates do more practice, but the score improves when the practice starts correcting the right problem.
Writing before identifying the task The letter type and recipient decide structure, tone and final request.
Including everything from the notes Case notes are raw material, not a checklist to copy.
Making the letter too long Long letters usually hide weak selection and unclear purpose.
Using casual or emotional wording Professional tone is assessed throughout the letter.
Skipping the final review Names, dates, final request, tense and layout must be checked before submission.

Short answers for healthcare professionals choosing their next preparation step.
How many tips are on this OET Writing page?
The page contains all 11 of Dr Hesham's writing tips, expanded into practical exam guidance.
What is the biggest OET Writing mistake?
Most candidates include too many case notes and do not write tightly for the reader and letter purpose.
Should I memorise OET letters?
No. Memorisation breaks when the case changes. A repeatable method for purpose, selection, organisation and review is stronger.
Can Dr Hesham correct my OET Writing?
Yes. The page directs candidates to WhatsApp and course support for profession-specific writing correction and feedback.

OET Speaking tips for nurses and doctors: patient-friendly language, empathy, structure, signposting and time control in role-plays.

Speaking
OET Speaking Tips 2026: 11 Expert Strategies for Healthcare Professionals
Use these OET Speaking tips to sound like a safe healthcare professional, open the role-play properly, explain clearly, respond to concerns, signpost, and manage time.

Role-play route
Do not memorise scripts. Train the conversation skills examiners score.
OET Speaking is a short professional healthcare conversation. The score improves when your opening, questions, explanations, empathy, concern-handling and timing follow a safe repeatable method.
01 Open naturally Start with purpose, role and patient comfort.
02 Guide the patient Use structured questions, signposting and clear explanations.
03 Close safely Handle concerns and finish with practical next steps.

How to approach OET Speaking with a repeatable method

Open naturally, identify the patient concern, ask structured questions, explain clearly and close with shared next steps.
Patient language and empathy

Concerns, signposting and timing

Using casual English The exam rewards professional healthcare communication, not everyday conversation.
Starting with a memorised opening A fixed script often fails to match the role-play card.
Explaining with jargon Patients need clear wording, not colleague-level terminology.
Ignoring patient concerns Concerns must be acknowledged and handled safely.
Running out of time A role-play without internal structure usually becomes rushed or incomplete.
How Dr Hesham helps OET Speaking candidates
Move from knowing the tips to applying them in timed, profession-specific practice.

Identify the exact reason your score is stuck before repeating the same practice.
Targeted feedback
Get clear corrections and next steps instead of vague advice.
Course framework
Follow a structured method for Grade B and above preparation.

Short answers for healthcare professionals choosing their next preparation step.
How many tips are on this OET Speaking page?
The page contains all 11 of Dr Hesham's speaking tips, expanded into practical role-play guidance.
What does OET Speaking assess?
It assesses healthcare communication, including fluency, language, intelligibility, appropriateness and clinical communication skills.
Is memorised empathy enough for OET Speaking?
No. Empathy must fit the patient concern and moment. Memorised lines often sound artificial.

## OET Listening Tips 2026: 10 Expert Strategies | Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-listening-tips.html

OET Listening tips for nurses and doctors: Part A, B and C strategies, note-taking, accents and distractors, from Dr Ahmed Hesham.

Listening
OET Listening Tips 2026: 10 Expert Strategies for Healthcare Professionals
Use these OET Listening tips to train Part A, Part B and Part C with accent awareness, shorthand notes, distractor control, vocabulary recognition, and smarter mock review.
