10 Expert listening tips from the 2026 guide
A B C Strategies for all three OET Listening parts
2026 Built for healthcare professionals preparing now
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 18 May 2026 · Updated 2 Nov 2026
Score-focused route
Do not practise randomly. Train the exact skill each part tests.
If you are preparing for the OET Listening sub-test, you already know this is the part where most healthcare professionals lose marks. The exam tests three very different skills across three parts, and most candidates apply the same approach to all of them.
01 Understand the part Know whether the task rewards speed, detail, inference, or trap recognition.
02 Use a repeatable method Apply the same controlled process until it becomes automatic under pressure.
03 Review with feedback Track why errors happen instead of collecting more unreviewed mock tests.
Complete Listening Guide
10 expert OET Listening tips that actually work
If you are preparing for the OET Listening sub-test, you already know this is the part where most healthcare professionals lose marks. The exam tests three very different skills across three parts, and most candidates apply the same approach to all of them.
10 Tips covering structure, timing, vocabulary, traps, Part C thinking, and smart practice.
01 Master the Three-Part Structure (But There is a Catch)
OET Listening is divided into Part A (consultation extracts), Part B (short workplace extracts), and Part C (extended presentations or interviews). Each part demands a fundamentally different listening mindset. Many candidates lose marks because they apply the same approach to all three - and that is exactly where the exam catches them out.
Inside the complete method: The specific mindset shift required for each part, and the precise moment to switch, is what we drill in Module 1 of the course.
02 Train Your Ear for Multiple Accents
OET says you might hear a variety of accents in the Listening sub-test. Most free practice resources do not replicate the OET specific style of medical English. Generic YouTube listening practice will not prepare you for the accent shifts in Part A consultations or the layered delivery of Part C presentations.
Inside the complete method: Inside the course, you access a curated audio bank of OET-style accents with structured progression drills.
03 Note-Taking Is a Skill, Not an Instinct
The single biggest mistake we see is candidates trying to write full words. By the time you have finished writing, the speaker has moved on and you have missed the next answer. High-scoring candidates use a structured shorthand system that captures the answer before the speaker even finishes the sentence.
Inside the complete method: The full shorthand system, including medical abbreviations, symbols, and decision trees, is taught in Module 2.
04 Use the Reading Time Before Each Extract Strategically
Before each extract, you are given time to read the questions: 30 seconds before each Part A extract, 15 seconds before each Part B extract and 90 seconds before each Part C recording. Most candidates treat this as a break. Top scorers treat it as the most valuable part of the exam. There is a specific reading order, prediction technique, and prioritisation method that transforms these short windows into your biggest advantage.
Inside the complete method: Module 3 teaches the exact pre-pause framework most candidates have never heard of.
05 Beware the Distractor Trap
In Parts B and C, OET says you will often hear elements of each answer option in the audio, and you must choose the option that answers the question. Hearing a word from an option does not make it correct. Knowing exactly when to commit to an answer, and when to wait, is half the battle in Part A and the entire battle in Part C.
Inside the complete method: We teach the distractor recognition framework with over 80 worked examples.
06 Synonyms, Paraphrasing, and Why Vocabulary Wins
The OET Listening questions rarely use the same words as the audio. Your medical vocabulary needs to flex between formal terminology and informal patient language. If a patient says "I get out of breath walking upstairs," the question may use "breathlessness on exertion" or "exertional dyspnoea." Recognising these shifts under time pressure separates B-grade candidates from A-grade ones.
Inside the complete method: Our bilingual OET vocabulary dictionary with 512 English and Arabic entries is included with every Tutor Book purchase.
07 Part C Is Not Just Harder Part B
OET says Part C tests gist, attitude and opinion: the overall meaning of a longer talk, how a speaker feels and what they think. Many candidates lose marks in Part C because they listen for the same kind of information they used in Part A and B. The questions are designed to reward candidates who can read between the lines and identify the speaker underlying viewpoint.
Inside the complete method: Module 5 is dedicated entirely to Part C inference techniques.
08 Spelling Still Matters in Listening
OET accepts British and American spelling conventions, so "colour" and "color" are both fine. What costs candidates is inaccurate spelling of the words they hear: medication names, symptoms and everyday words written under time pressure. Practise the words that come up most often in consultations until you can write them without hesitation.
Inside the complete method: Use the course spelling checklist of high-frequency medical words.
09 Time Pressure Is a Mental Game
On paper, you have two minutes at the end of the Listening sub-test to check your answers; on computer or OET@Home, there is a short pause at the end of each question instead. Candidates who freeze on one question can lose the next few as well. There is a specific recovery technique that high scorers use to stay in flow after a difficult question - and most candidates have never been taught it.
Inside the complete method: The recovery protocol is part of our exam-day mental conditioning module.
10 Practice Smart, Not Hard
Completing 50 mock tests without strategy will not improve your score. We see this every week: candidates exhaust themselves with practice that never addresses their actual weaknesses. Targeted practice with structured feedback is what moves a B grade to an A.
Inside the complete method: Every mock test inside the course comes with a personalised band-by-band diagnostic built by Dr Ahmed Hesham.
Ready to pass OET Listening?
These 10 tips are the surface. The complete system includes the shorthand note-taking method, distractor recognition framework, accent training audio bank, and Part C inference drills. Join thousands of healthcare professionals who passed with Dr Ahmed Hesham. Enrol today through app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk.
Ask WhatsApp Support
How to approach OET Listening Part A, Part B and Part C
Each part rewards a different mindset. Use this section as a quick route before you start timed practice.
Part A: consultation extracts
Use the pre-pause to predict answer type, then listen for patient details while writing in controlled shorthand.
Part B: workplace extracts
Expect short workplace contexts where the best answer often depends on purpose, policy, or the speaker main point.
Part C: presentations and interviews
Listen for gist, attitude and opinion rather than chasing isolated facts. The obvious answer is often a trap.
Common mistakes that keep listening scores stuck
Most candidates do more practice, but the score improves when the practice starts correcting the right problem.
Using one method for all three parts Part A, Part B, and Part C reward different listening behaviours. A single method creates repeated errors.
Writing full words Full-word notes are too slow. Shorthand protects the next answer while the speaker keeps moving.
Committing too early You will often hear elements of more than one option. Wait for confirmation before locking your response.
Ignoring spelling accuracy British and American spellings are both accepted, but careless spelling of the words you hear is an avoidable risk.
Practising without diagnostics Repeated mocks do not fix the problem if you never identify the cause of each mistake.
Freezing after one missed answer One missed answer should not become four. Recovery is a trainable exam-day skill.
A smarter weekly Listening practice framework
Use this framework before booking more mock tests or collecting more free materials.
Diagnose first
Identify whether your errors come from timing, vocabulary, prediction, distractors, inference, or exam pressure.
Practise under time
Train the clock from the beginning. Untimed practice builds understanding, but timed review builds exam control.
Review with feedback
One analysed paper is more valuable than several unreviewed mocks because it shows the repeat error pattern.
OET Listening tips FAQ
Short answers for healthcare professionals choosing their next preparation step.
How do I improve OET Listening quickly?
Start by separating Part A, Part B, and Part C practice. Then review whether mistakes come from accents, note-taking, distractors, vocabulary, inference, or time pressure.
Is OET Listening mainly about medical vocabulary?
Vocabulary matters, but it is not enough. Strong listening requires prediction, shorthand notes, accent exposure, and the ability to wait through distractors.
Why do I lose marks in Part C?
Part C tests gist, attitude and opinion. If you listen only for facts, you can miss the speaker viewpoint and choose the obvious distractor.
Should I do many mock tests?
Mock tests help only when they are reviewed. Targeted practice with diagnostics is more useful than completing many papers without understanding why answers were wrong.

## OET Reading Tips 2026: 10 Expert Strategies | Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-reading-tips.html

OET Reading tips for healthcare professionals: Part A scanning, Part B and C distractors, inference and a weekly mock strategy.

Reading
OET Reading Tips 2026: 10 Expert Strategies for Healthcare Professionals
Use these OET Reading tips to handle Part A scanning, keyword anchors, 45-second timing, Part B distractors, Part C inference, vocabulary in context, and smarter mock review.

10 Expert reading tips from the 2026 guide
A B C Strategies for all three OET Reading parts
2026 Built for healthcare professionals preparing now
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 18 May 2026 · Updated 27 Oct 2026
Score-focused route
Do not practise randomly. Train the exact skill each part tests.
The OET Reading sub-test is where time pressure breaks even well-prepared candidates. With only 15 minutes for Part A and 45 minutes for Parts B and C, every second counts, and the questions are designed to make you waste them.
01 Understand the part Know whether the task rewards speed, detail, inference, or trap recognition.
02 Use a repeatable method Apply the same controlled process until it becomes automatic under pressure.
03 Review with feedback Track why errors happen instead of collecting more unreviewed mock tests.
Complete Reading Guide
10 expert OET Reading tips that actually work
The OET Reading sub-test is where time pressure breaks even well-prepared candidates. With only 15 minutes for Part A and 45 minutes for Parts B and C, every second counts, and the questions are designed to make you waste them.
10 Tips covering structure, timing, vocabulary, traps, Part C thinking, and smart practice.
01 Do Not Read Part A - Scan It
Part A is not a reading test, it is a search task. Candidates who try to read all four texts run out of time within the first five minutes. Top scorers never read Part A in the conventional sense - they use a specific scanning pattern that moves across all four texts simultaneously.
Inside the complete method: The exact scanning pattern, including eye movement direction and text-priority logic, is taught in Module 1 of the course.
02 The Keyword Anchor Technique
Every Part A question contains an anchor word - a unique, locatable term that points you to the right text. Find the anchor, locate it in the text, extract the answer. The challenge is that OET disguises anchors as synonyms. Knowing which words to anchor on is the difference between 30/42 and 42/42.
Inside the complete method: We teach the full anchor identification system with over 50 worked examples.
03 Part A Time Management Is Brutal
Fifteen minutes for 20 questions across four texts means roughly 45 seconds per question, including locating, reading, and writing. Most candidates spend two minutes on question 1 and never recover. There is a specific pacing rhythm that high scorers use to stay on track.
Inside the complete method: Inside the course, you practise the 45-second drill with real-time feedback on every attempt.
04 Part B Is Distractor Recognition, Not Comprehension
All three options in OET Reading Part B usually sound correct. The right one is often the option that is least specific, or the one that mirrors the exact emphasis of the text without overstating it. There is a method to spotting the trap - and it is not intuition.
Inside the complete method: Module 3 breaks down Part B distractor logic across all five major question types.
05 Stop Referencing Paragraph Numbers
This is not an exam rule, it is a thinking trap. Candidates who think "the answer is in paragraph 3" miss synthesis questions where the answer spans the whole text. Part C in particular is built to punish paragraph-locked thinking.
Inside the complete method: We teach a whole-text mapping technique that flips this habit on its head.
06 Build a Medical Synonym Bank
Reduce, lessen, alleviate, mitigate, attenuate, blunt. OET will use the rare one. Your job is to recognise it instantly under timed pressure. Memorising long vocabulary lists is the slowest way to prepare. Encountering vocabulary in OET-style passages is up to four times more effective, but only with the right passages.
Inside the complete method: The bilingual OET vocabulary dictionary with 512 English and Arabic entries and passage-based context is included with The Tutor Book.
07 Part C Is About Attitude, Not Facts
The hardest Part C questions test the author tone, viewpoint, and stance - not what the text says, but what the text means. This shift in thinking is what separates B-grade candidates from A-grade ones. Most people fail Part C because they are still hunting for facts.
Inside the complete method: Module 5 is dedicated entirely to tone, attitude, and inference techniques.
08 Beware the Trap of the Obvious
In Part C, the most obvious answer is usually wrong. OET rewards readers who can hold two ideas in mind simultaneously and choose the more nuanced one. If your gut tells you the answer is obviously B, that is usually the moment to pause and reconsider.
Inside the complete method: We teach the two-step verification method that catches the trap every time.
09 Vocabulary in Context Beats Vocabulary Lists
Flashcards and memorisation are the slowest way to build OET-ready vocabulary. Reading authentic OET-style passages with structured glossary support is up to four times faster. The trick is knowing which words to learn first, and most candidates waste weeks on vocabulary that never appears on the exam.
Inside the complete method: Our Tier 1, 2, and 3 vocabulary system tells you exactly what to learn first.
10 Mock Strategy Matters More Than Mock Quantity
Two well-analysed mocks beat ten unreviewed ones. Most candidates burn through mock tests without ever understanding why they got questions wrong, so they repeat the same mistakes on exam day. Targeted analysis with structured feedback is what moves a B grade to an A.
Inside the complete method: Every mock test inside the course comes with a personalised band-by-band diagnostic built by Dr Ahmed Hesham.
Ready to pass OET Reading?
These 10 tips are the surface. The complete system includes the Part A scanning pattern, keyword anchor framework, distractor recognition drills, and Part C inference methodology. Join thousands of healthcare professionals who passed with Dr Ahmed Hesham. Enrol today through app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk.
Ask WhatsApp Support
How to approach OET Reading Part A, Part B and Part C
Each part rewards a different mindset. Use this section as a quick route before you start timed practice.
Part A: speed scanning
Treat Part A as a search task. Use anchor words, scan all texts, and protect the 45-second rhythm.
Part B: distractor logic
Do not choose the option that merely sounds familiar. Match the exact emphasis of the short workplace text.
Part C: whole-text inference
Move beyond paragraph hunting. Track tone, stance, and how ideas connect across the text.
Common mistakes that keep reading scores stuck
Most candidates do more practice, but the score improves when the practice starts correcting the right problem.
Reading Part A like an article Part A is a timed search task, not conventional reading. Reading every line wastes the limited 15 minutes.
Choosing weak anchor words If the anchor is too general, you scan the wrong text and lose time before the question even begins.
Trusting the obvious Part C answer The most obvious option is often a trap. Nuanced verification protects your score.
Memorising vocabulary lists only Vocabulary without context is slow. OET-style passage review builds faster recognition.
Doing too many unreviewed mocks Mock quantity does not fix repeated errors. Analysis is what changes the next attempt.
Locking answers to paragraph numbers Some answers depend on whole-text meaning, not one paragraph alone.
A smarter weekly Reading practice framework
Use this framework before booking more mock tests or collecting more free materials.
Diagnose first
Identify whether your errors come from timing, vocabulary, prediction, distractors, inference, or exam pressure.
Practise under time
Train the clock from the beginning. Untimed practice builds understanding, but timed review builds exam control.
Review with feedback
One analysed paper is more valuable than several unreviewed mocks because it shows the repeat error pattern.
OET Reading tips FAQ
Short answers for healthcare professionals choosing their next preparation step.
How do I improve OET Reading quickly?
Stop reading everything in the same way. Part A needs scanning, Part B needs distractor recognition, and Part C needs whole-text thinking and inference.
What is the biggest mistake in OET Reading Part A?
The biggest mistake is trying to read all four texts normally. Part A is a search task under severe time pressure, so scanning and anchor words matter.
Why is Part C difficult?
Part C often tests attitude, tone, and meaning across the text. Candidates who search only for facts often choose the obvious but wrong option.
Are vocabulary lists enough for OET Reading?
No. Vocabulary improves faster when learned in OET-style passages with context, synonyms, and review of why each word matters.

## OET for UK Registration 2026: NMC, GMC, GPhC and HCPC Guide

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/uk-pathway-guide.html

UK registration guide for OET candidates: NMC, GMC, GPhC and HCPC scores, steps, documents and common mistakes for 2026.

UK Pathway Guidelines
UK Pathway Guide 2026 for OET Healthcare Professionals
A practical UK registration roadmap for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and physiotherapists preparing for OET and regulator applications. Use it to choose the right regulator, test version, documents and preparation route.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 19 May 2026 · Updated 27 Oct 2026
Message on WhatsApp for Pathway Guidance
Join the Course
Join Free Community
Last updated: 19 May 2026. Educational guidance only - always verify final rules with the official regulator.
4 UK regulators covered
2026 Pathway guide, updated for 2026
1:1 WhatsApp pathway guidance
Identify GMC, NMC, GPhC or HCPC
Confirm the accepted OET or English evidence
Collect verified documents early
Prepare profession-specific Writing and Speaking
Align exam, application and visa timing
Regulator overview
Choose the regulator before choosing the test date
The UK route is profession-specific. Each regulator has its own accepted English evidence, application portal, exam route, document standards and processing timeline.
Important: This page is educational guidance, not legal, immigration or regulator advice. Requirements, scores, fees and document rules can change. Verify on the official regulator website before booking OET or paying any fee.
Profession Authority Route English planning note
Doctors GMC PLAB, approved postgraduate qualification or sponsorship route OET Medicine, IELTS or another GMC-accepted route; verify current GMC evidence before booking.
Nurses and midwives NMC CBT, OSCE and NMC registration checks OET Nursing B in Listening, Reading, Speaking and C+ in Writing; combining only when NMC rules are met.
Pharmacists GPhC OSPAP, foundation training and registration assessment OET Pharmacy with B in all four sub-tests in one sitting, on paper or computer (GPhC does not accept OET@Home).
Physiotherapists HCPC International application and standards mapping OET Physiotherapy 1400 total with no element below 300 under current HCPC guidance.
Doctors - GMC pathway
GMC PLAB or approved postgraduate route OET Medicine
For international medical graduates preparing for GMC registration with a licence to practise. The route commonly includes GMC Online, EPIC verification, PLAB 1 and PLAB 2, or an approved postgraduate qualification such as MRCP or MRCS. Preparing for the GMC score? See the OET course for doctors .
English-test planning: OET Medicine is accepted by GMC as English evidence when it meets the current GMC requirements. Candidates must release scores to GMC through the OET portal and confirm certificate validity before applying.
Pathway steps
Confirm the route Check your primary medical qualification and choose PLAB, postgraduate qualification, sponsorship or another approved GMC route.
Prepare English evidence Book the correct OET Medicine test and prepare all four subtests, especially writing and speaking.
Complete exams and documents Plan PLAB 1, PLAB 2 or your approved alternative route, plus EPIC verification and certificates of good standing.
Apply and move to practice Submit through GMC Online, attend ID checks where required, then move toward NHS/private roles and visa planning.
Common mistakes
Booking a non-Medicine OET version.
Preparing with IELTS-style essays instead of OET letters.
Submitting before checking current GMC evidence rules.
Forgetting to release OET results to GMC.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
Referral, discharge and transfer letters with selective relevance and formal medical register.
Speaking
History taking, explaining diagnosis or investigations, refusals, concern handling and safety-netting.
Reading
Medical abstracts, NHS-style guidance, drug information and workplace clinical texts.
Listening
Doctor-patient consultations, clinical presentations and workplace exchanges in varied accents.
Nurses and midwives - NMC pathway
NMC CBT and OSCE OET Nursing
For internationally educated nurses and midwives joining the NMC register. The pathway usually includes NMC Online, eligibility checks, CBT, English evidence, OSCE in the UK, health and character checks, and receiving the NMC PIN. Preparing for the NMC score? See the OET course for nurses .
English-test planning: NMC accepts OET Nursing with B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing. Combining rules can apply only when all NMC conditions are met, so candidates must check the official NMC page before relying on combined scores.
Pathway steps
Self-assess and apply Use the NMC route for internationally trained applicants and prepare identity, qualification and registration evidence.
Pass CBT Complete the computer-based test through the accepted testing route.
Submit English evidence Use OET Nursing or another accepted route according to current NMC rules.
Complete OSCE and final checks Travel to the UK, pass OSCE, complete health/character checks and receive your PIN.
Common mistakes
Treating Writing as easy because the minimum is C+.
Using doctor-style letters for nursing tasks.
Booking OET Medicine by mistake.
Trying to combine scores without meeting all NMC combining conditions.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
Nursing referrals, discharge letters, community team updates and patient education letters in a nursing voice.
Speaking
Patient education, calming anxious patients or relatives, health promotion and safe handover-style communication.
Reading
Care plans, infection control guidance, medicines safety bulletins and workplace policies.
Listening
Nurse-patient interactions, ward briefings and nursing-focused presentations.
Pharmacists - GPhC pathway
GPhC OSPAP OET Pharmacy
For pharmacists qualified outside Great Britain who need the Overseas Pharmacists Assessment Programme, foundation training and the GPhC registration assessment before joining the register.
Preparing for OET Pharmacy? See the OET course for pharmacists .
English-test planning: GPhC accepts OET Pharmacy (B in all four sub-tests in one sitting, on paper or computer) or IELTS, but OSPAP universities can set additional entry conditions, so check those too.
Pathway steps
Confirm OSPAP eligibility Check degree equivalence and GPhC eligibility before applying to an OSPAP provider.
Prepare English evidence Use OET Pharmacy, IELTS or accepted evidence only if it matches current GPhC and university rules.
Complete OSPAP and training Finish the postgraduate diploma and 52-week foundation training at an approved site.
Pass registration assessment Complete the knowledge and calculations papers, then meet fitness-to-practise and registration requirements.
Common mistakes
Using Medicine or Nursing materials for Pharmacy writing.
Underestimating the calculations paper.
Missing university-specific English rules.
Assuming training or assessment steps can be skipped.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
Community pharmacy letters, dispensing-incident notes, supplier requests and GP communication.
Speaking
Medication counselling, adherence conversations, side-effect explanation and OTC sale refusal.
Reading
SmPCs, BNF-style entries, MHRA drug-safety alerts and pharmacy workplace policies.
Listening
Pharmacist-patient counselling, ward conversations and pharmacy team handovers.
Physiotherapists - HCPC pathway
HCPC International application OET Physiotherapy
For internationally trained physiotherapists applying through the HCPC international route. The pathway requires evidence of qualification, registration, programme content, clinical experience and standards mapping where applicable.
Preparing for OET Physiotherapy? See the OET course for physiotherapists ; other HCPC professions can use OET for allied health .
English-test planning: HCPC accepts profession-specific OET for physiotherapists when it meets the current score rules. Current HCPC guidance lists OET Physiotherapy with a total of 1400 and no element below 300, taken at an official test centre.
Pathway steps
Check HCPC eligibility Confirm the international route and whether any English-language exemption applies.
Collect evidence Prepare qualification certificates, transcripts, programme details, clinical hours and registration evidence.
Submit English and mapping evidence Prepare OET/IELTS/TOEFL evidence and the Standards of Proficiency mapping document where required.
Respond and register Answer HCPC evidence requests promptly and move toward NHS or private-sector applications after registration.
Common mistakes
Practising with doctor or nurse role-play cards only.
Using vague language for mobility, gait, balance and rehabilitation progress.
Submitting an English certificate that is too old.
Skipping the Standards of Proficiency mapping document when required.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
Referral, discharge and progress letters using physiotherapy terminology.
Speaking
Explaining conditions, home exercises, rehabilitation plans, adherence and chronic pain concerns.
Reading
Rehabilitation guidance, return-to-work material, ergonomic policies and clinical texts.
Listening
Physiotherapy consultations, MDT briefings and rehabilitation presentations.
Candidate checklist
Before you start the UK pathway
Identify the correct UK regulator for your profession.
Read the current English policy before booking OET.
Book the correct OET profession version, not the nearest available version.
Plan Writing and Speaking with profession-specific feedback.
Check certificate validity and document timelines before application.
Verify separate UK visa English requirements where relevant.
Official sources
Verify these before paying any fee
GMC English evidence Doctors, PLAB and registration English evidence. NMC OET requirements Nurses and midwives OET scores and combining rules. GPhC international pharmacists OSPAP and international pharmacist registration. HCPC English certificate Physiotherapy and allied health English evidence.
UK pathway FAQ
Short answers for healthcare professionals planning OET and UK registration.
Is OET accepted for UK healthcare registration? OET is accepted by several UK healthcare regulators for specific professions and routes, including GMC, NMC and HCPC routes when the exact score and test version match current official rules.
Which OET profession should I book for the UK? Book the profession version that matches your regulator route: Medicine for doctors, Nursing for nurses and midwives, Pharmacy for pharmacists, and Physiotherapy for physiotherapists.
Can I use the same OET score for registration and visa? Regulator English evidence and UK immigration English requirements are separate. Candidates must verify UKVI rules independently.
Can Dr Hesham help me choose the right pathway? Yes. Send your profession, target regulator, current OET level and timeline on WhatsApp for preparation guidance. This is educational support, not legal or regulator advice.
Not sure which UK pathway applies to you?
Send your profession, current OET level, target regulator and timeline. We will guide you toward the right preparation step.

## OET for the USA 2026: ECFMG, VisaScreen and State Boards

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/usa-pathway-guide.html

Professional USA pathway guide for healthcare professionals covering ECFMG, USMLE, NCLEX, FPGEC, NPTE, TOEFL/OET rules, state boards and WhatsApp guidance.

USA Pathway Guidelines
USA Pathway Guide 2026 for Healthcare Professionals
A practical USA licensure roadmap for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and physical therapists. Understand where OET fits, where TOEFL or IELTS is usually needed, and how to avoid paying for the wrong test.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 19 May 2026 · Updated 27 Oct 2026
Message on WhatsApp for Pathway Guidance
Join the Course
Join Free Community
Last updated: 19 May 2026. Educational guidance only - verify final rules with the official authority and target state board.
50+ State-board rules can differ
4 Professions covered
OET? Mostly ECFMG doctor route
Choose profession and target state early
Confirm OET, TOEFL or IELTS before booking
Order the correct credential report
Plan USMLE, NCLEX, FPGEE/NAPLEX or NPTE
Treat visa planning as a separate process
USA overview
The USA is state based, not one national licence
National exams exist, but the actual licence is issued by a state board. That means the correct English test, credential report and application route can change by profession and state.
Important: This page is educational guidance, not legal, immigration, employment or licensure advice. Requirements change by state and cycle. Verify official sources before booking OET, TOEFL, IELTS or paying any application fee.
Profession Authority Route English planning note
Doctors ECFMG / Intealth and state boards USMLE, Pathways, ECFMG Certification, ERAS/NRMP OET Medicine is required for ECFMG Pathways applicants under current ECFMG communication skills rules.
Nurses State Boards of Nursing / NCSBN Credential evaluation, BON application, NCLEX-RN, VisaScreen where needed CGFNS VisaScreen accepts OET (new minimums for tests from 12 May 2026: S 360, R 340, W 350, L 320); state boards vary, so check yours.
Pharmacists NABP / FPGEC and state boards FPGEC, FPGEE, NAPLEX, MPJE/state law and internship hours FPGEC requires TOEFL iBT, not OET Pharmacy.
Physical therapists FSBPT and state PT boards Credential evaluation, NPTE, jurisprudence/state requirements TOEFL iBT is the usual English-test route; verify the exact state board.
Doctors - ECFMG / Intealth pathway
ECFMG USMLE and Pathways OET Medicine
For international medical graduates aiming for ECFMG Certification, ERAS, the NRMP Match, residency training and later state medical licensure. OET Medicine is part of the communication skills requirement for Pathways applicants. See the OET course for doctors for ECFMG-focused preparation.
English-test planning: Official ECFMG 2027 guidance requires OET Medicine for Pathways applicants, with 350 in Listening, Reading and Speaking and 300 in Writing in one test administration. Always follow the current ECFMG rules.
Pathway steps
Confirm school eligibility Check the World Directory Sponsor Note and create the correct MyIntealth account.
Pass USMLE steps Plan Step 1 and Step 2 CK with your Pathway and OET timing.
Complete ECFMG Pathway and OET Choose the correct Pathway, sit OET Medicine, and release scores to ECFMG with the correct ID.
Apply for the Match After certification, use ERAS/NRMP, then work with your program on visa and state licensure steps.
Common mistakes
Assuming USMLE scores remove the OET requirement.
Using OET@Home when a physical test venue is available and ECFMG rules do not allow it.
Missing Match-related timing for OET results.
Forgetting to release scores to ECFMG/MyIntealth correctly.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
Structured medical letters with selective relevance, formal tone and safe clinical summary.
Speaking
Consultations, diagnosis explanation, bad news, patient concerns and shared decisions.
Reading
Medical journal extracts, guideline summaries, drug information and workplace texts.
Listening
Multi-accent clinical consultations, ward briefings and presentations.
Nurses - State BON / NCLEX pathway
State Boards of Nursing CGFNS/TruMerit NCLEX-RN
For internationally educated nurses applying state by state. NCSBN owns the NCLEX-RN, but each Board of Nursing decides application requirements, credential evaluation, English testing, fingerprinting, SSN policy and authorization to test.
English-test planning: Do not assume OET Nursing will count for US nursing. TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic is often the English route for US nurses, depending on the state board; CGFNS VisaScreen also accepts OET.
Pathway steps
Choose a target state Check BON rules before paying for any test or credential report.
Order credential evaluation Use the report required by the state, such as CGFNS/TruMerit CES or a state-specific route.
Complete English and BON application Meet the state English rule, submit the BON application and receive authorization to test.
Pass NCLEX and plan VisaScreen Sit Next Generation NCLEX and prepare VisaScreen/employer sponsorship where required.
Common mistakes
Booking OET Nursing for a US state without checking acceptance.
Choosing a state without checking SSN, fingerprinting and concurrency rules.
Ordering the wrong CGFNS/TruMerit report.
Preparing NCLEX with memorisation instead of clinical judgement.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
If you also target the UK, OET Nursing supports NMC preparation, but it may not support your US BON route.
Speaking
NCLEX communication preparation should focus on patient safety, prioritisation and clinical judgement.
Reading
Read state board instructions carefully, especially concurrency and report-type language.
Listening
Prepare for US accents and workplace communication, but choose the English test your target authority accepts.
Pharmacists - NABP / FPGEC pathway
NABP FPGEC and FPGEE TOEFL iBT
For foreign pharmacy graduates seeking FPGEC Certification before state board eligibility, NAPLEX, MPJE or a state law equivalent, internship hours and final licensure.
If your route also needs OET (for example for UK, Irish or Australian registration), see the OET course for pharmacists .
English-test planning: NABP/FPGEC requires TOEFL iBT as part of FPGEC Certification. Current NABP guidance says all four sections must be completed in one testing session, MyBest scores are not accepted, and remote-proctored/at-home TOEFL is not accepted.
Pathway steps
Create NABP e-Profile Use the correct NABP account and follow the current Candidate Application Bulletin.
Prepare TOEFL iBT correctly Use the current NABP score scale and test-location rules before submitting the FPGEC application.
Submit ECE and documents Arrange ECE evaluation, license evidence, identity documents, translations and score reports.
Pass FPGEE then state exams Complete FPGEC Certification, then NAPLEX, MPJE/state law exam and internship hours as required.
Common mistakes
Booking OET Pharmacy for FPGEC.
Using TOEFL Home Edition or an ineligible test site.
Trying to use MyBest scores.
Submitting ECE or license documents incorrectly.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
OET Pharmacy can help UK or Australia planning, but it does not replace FPGEC TOEFL rules.
Speaking
Pharmacists need English preparation aligned with TOEFL iBT if the sole target is the US.
Reading
Read NABP document-sealing and ECE instructions carefully to avoid delays.
Listening
Plan FPGEE timing because exam windows and certification timelines are strict.
Physical therapists - FSBPT / State PT pathway
FSBPT Credential evaluation NPTE
For foreign-educated physical therapists applying through state boards. Each state decides evaluation agency, English testing, supervised practice and jurisprudence rules, while the NPTE is administered nationally through FSBPT.
If your route also needs OET (for example for UK, Irish or Australian registration), see the OET course for physiotherapists .
English-test planning: TOEFL iBT is the usual English-test route for US physical therapists. Do not book OET Physiotherapy for the US unless your exact state board explicitly confirms acceptance; OET Physiotherapy is primarily useful for UK HCPC and selected non-US bodies.
Pathway steps
Choose state and evaluator Check whether FCCPT, ECE, IERF or another agency is required by the target state.
Complete credential review Use the correct Coursework Tool and submit verified documents.
Meet English and state application rules Prepare TOEFL iBT or the state-accepted evidence, then apply for authorization.
Pass NPTE and state steps Take the NPTE, complete law exams or supervised practice if required, and plan Type 1/VisaScreen where relevant.
Common mistakes
Assuming OET Physiotherapy counts for US PT licensure.
Choosing an evaluator not accepted by the target state.
Missing NPTE registration windows.
Ignoring attempt limits or state law exam requirements.
OET / English preparation focus
Writing
Use OET Physiotherapy only for countries and regulators that accept it, such as HCPC where criteria are met.
Speaking
For US PT, English preparation usually needs TOEFL-style planning.
Reading
Read state board rules for attempts, deadlines and evaluator choice.
Listening
Prepare communication around functional status, rehabilitation and patient education for workplace readiness.
Candidate checklist
Before you start the USA pathway
Identify the correct body: ECFMG/Intealth, state BON, NABP/FPGEC or FSBPT/state PT board.
Choose a target state early because rules are not uniform.
Confirm the accepted English test before booking.
Order the exact credential report required by your profession and state.
Plan 12 to 24 months where credentialing, exams and documentation overlap.
Separate licensure planning from visa planning and seek qualified visa advice where needed.
Official sources
Verify these before paying any fee
ECFMG OET / Pathways Current OET Medicine communication skills rules for Pathways. NCSBN international nurses US nursing licensure orientation for internationally educated nurses. NABP FPGEC Foreign pharmacy graduate certification and TOEFL iBT rules. FSBPT foreign educated PTs Physical therapy credential and NPTE pathway resources.
USA pathway FAQ
Short answers for healthcare professionals planning US licensure and English testing.
Do USA doctors need OET Medicine? Yes, current ECFMG Pathways guidance requires OET Medicine for Pathways applicants and states there are no exceptions for native language, medical school language or citizenship.
What OET score does ECFMG currently require? Current 2027 ECFMG guidance lists 350 in Listening, Reading and Speaking and 300 in Writing in one test administration. Candidates must verify the current ECFMG cycle before booking.
Can nurses use OET Nursing for the USA? Not automatically. US nursing is state-board dependent, so check your Board of Nursing. CGFNS VisaScreen does accept OET: for tests taken on or after 12 May 2026, registered nurses need Speaking 360, Reading 340, Writing 350 and Listening 320, and at-home tests are not accepted.
Is US licensure the same as a visa? No. Licensure, certification, credentialing and visas are separate. Candidates should verify official licensing rules and seek licensed immigration advice for visa questions.
Not sure whether OET or TOEFL fits your USA plan?
Send your profession, target state, current English level and timeline. We will guide you toward the correct preparation decision before you pay for the wrong test.

## OET for Australia 2026: Ahpra Scores and Registration Guide

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/australia-pathway-guide.html

Australia pathway guide for OET doctors, nurses, pharmacists and physiotherapists covering AHPRA, AMC, NMBA, APC, APEP, English scores and OET preparation.

Free Resource - Edition 2026 Australia Pathway Guide for OET Candidates
A practical Australia pathway guide for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and physiotherapists preparing for OET, AHPRA registration and profession-specific assessment routes.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 19 May 2026 · Updated 27 Oct 2026
Message on WhatsApp for Pathway Guidance Join Free Community
Confirm profession and regulator route
Match OET scores to AHPRA date rules
Prepare verification and assessment evidence
Plan exams, supervised practice or OBA
Get pathway-focused OET support
Australia pathway overview
Australia uses a single national registration system administered by AHPRA with profession-specific National Boards. Every candidate must match the correct regulator route, English evidence, assessment body and document verification process.
Important: This guide is educational orientation only. It is not legal, immigration or regulator advice. Always verify requirements on AHPRA, the relevant National Board and assessment council before booking a test or paying a fee.
Profession Main route OET relevance
Doctors Medical Board, AHPRA and AMC: Standard, Competent Authority or Specialist Pathway. OET Medicine for English evidence and clinical communication readiness.
Nurses and midwives NMBA Self-Check, Stream A or Stream B OBA with NCLEX-RN and OSCE. OET Nursing with writing and speaking in nursing register.
Pharmacists Pharmacy Board and APC Knowledge Stream, OPRA, internship and intern exams. OET Pharmacy for pharmacy-specific communication.
Physiotherapists Physiotherapy Board and Australian Physiotherapy Council APEP route. OET Physiotherapy with rehab-focused writing and speaking.
AHPRA English language standard at a glance
All four professions in this guide use the AHPRA English Language Skills registration standard. Ahpra changed its minimum scores on 23 April 2026, so your test date matters.
On or before 22 April 2026
OET minimums: Listening B, Reading B, Writing C+ and Speaking B. The writing minimum was lowered from B to C+ on 18 March 2025.
On or after 23 April 2026
OET numerical minimums: Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350 and Speaking 360.
Test-centre rule
AHPRA accepts paper or computer OET taken at an OET test centre. At-home OET is not accepted by AHPRA.
Two sittings rule
AHPRA can accept a maximum of two test sittings within 12 months, with all four sub-tests taken at each sitting.
Before booking: AHPRA also accepts IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT and Cambridge tests under specific rules. Verify the current standard and your National Board page before paying for any test.
Medical Board + AMC Doctors: Medical Board and AMC pathway
For IMGs with a recognised primary medical qualification listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools. The main routes are Standard Pathway, Competent Authority Pathway and Specialist Pathway.
Step What to prepare
1 Confirm your medical school is acceptable to AMC for your graduation year.
2 Create an AMC account and establish your AMC portfolio.
3 Complete Primary Source Verification through ECFMG EPIC / MyIntealth.
4 Meet the AHPRA English Language Skills standard with OET Medicine or another approved test.
5 For Standard Pathway, pass AMC CAT MCQ, then AMC Clinical Exam or an AMC-accredited WBA.
6 Apply through AHPRA for limited or provisional registration and complete 12 months / minimum 47 weeks FTE supervised practice.
7 For Competent Authority Pathway, confirm category A to F eligibility, secure supervised employment and complete the supervised practice route to general registration.
OET preparation focus
Writing: referral, discharge and transfer letters with selective relevance and Australian clinical register.
Speaking: chronic disease, bad news, shared decision making, patient concerns and Indigenous health considerations.
Reading: clinical guidelines, drug information and workplace texts.
Listening: multi-accent medical consultations and ward briefings.
Common mistakes to avoid
Choosing Standard Pathway when Competent Authority Pathway could avoid AMC exams.
Booking AMC Clinical before checking whether WBA and supervised practice are a better fit.
Using an OET sitting around the April 2026 transition without checking the correct score table.
Forgetting to release OET scores to AMC / Medical Board in the myOET portal.
NMBA + AHPRA Nurses and midwives: NMBA outcomes-based assessment
For internationally qualified nurses and midwives who want RN, EN or midwife registration. Since March 2020, NMBA has used Outcomes-Based Assessment instead of the old bridging-program model.
Step What to prepare
1 Complete the free AHPRA Self-Check on the IQNM Assessment Portal.
2 If referred, pay the assessment fee and submit documents and portfolio.
3 Complete Orientation Part 1 and receive the OBA referral letter if eligible.
4 Pass the NCLEX-RN cognitive component.
5 Meet the AHPRA English Language Skills standard with OET Nursing or another approved test.
6 Travel to Adelaide Health Simulation for the OSCE behavioural component.
7 Complete Orientation Part 2 and submit final NMBA registration documents for registration and AHPRA number.
OET preparation focus
Writing: nursing referrals, discharge letters and patient education letters in a nursing voice.
Speaking: patient education, handover, distressed patients and culturally safe communication.
Reading: care plans, infection-control bulletins and workplace policies.
Listening: nurse-patient interactions and Australian ward briefings.
Common mistakes to avoid
Skipping Self-Check before planning OBA.
Selecting the wrong graduation year or degree title and being misclassified.
Booking OSCE before passing NCLEX-RN.
Travelling for OSCE on an unsuitable visa or without checking attendance rules.
Pharmacy Board + APC Pharmacists: Pharmacy Board and APC Knowledge Stream
For internationally qualified pharmacists outside Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the USA who need the APC Knowledge Stream toward provisional registration.
2025 change: OPRA replaced KAPS from March 2025. Confirm the current APC route before paying for any exam.
Step What to prepare
1 Confirm a recognised pharmacy qualification of at least four years full-time tertiary study and current or eligible home registration.
2 Apply for APC Skills Assessment eligibility check through the APC Candidate Portal.
3 Receive the Skills Assessment Eligibility Letter and book OPRA.
4 Meet AHPRA English evidence with OET Pharmacy or another approved test.
5 Pass OPRA, the computer-based exam that replaced KAPS from March 2025.
6 Apply through AHPRA for provisional registration and approved supervised practice.
7 Complete the internship and pass Intern Written and Intern Oral exams within the required window for general registration.
OET preparation focus
Writing: community pharmacy letters to GPs, supplier requests and counselling notes.
Speaking: medication counselling, adherence, side effects and OTC sale refusals.
Reading: AMH-style entries, TGA alerts, medicine information and workplace policies.
Listening: pharmacist-patient counselling, ward conversations and pharmacy handovers.
Common mistakes to avoid
Booking retired KAPS instead of OPRA.
Trying to book OPRA without a valid eligibility letter.
Missing the Intern Written and Intern Oral timing window.
Using OET Medicine or Nursing material instead of OET Pharmacy material.
Physio Board + APC Physiotherapists: APEP and Physiotherapy Board route
For internationally qualified physiotherapists with an entry-level physiotherapy qualification and unrestricted right to practise who want Australian physiotherapy registration.
2025 change: APEP replaced the old Standard Assessment Pathway for new applicants from 1 October 2025.
Step What to prepare
1 Confirm eligibility with a diploma-level or higher physiotherapy qualification and unrestricted right to practise.
2 Apply to the Australian Physiotherapy Council for Eligibility Assessment.
3 Complete Cultural Safety Training online.
4 Use the APC Interim Certificate to apply for AHPRA limited registration for supervised practice where applicable.
5 Meet the AHPRA English Language Skills standard with OET Physiotherapy or another approved test.
6 Pass the APEP Written Assessment and Remote Capability Assessment.
7 Attend the one-day Clinical Workshop in Melbourne and then apply for general registration.
OET preparation focus
Writing: referrals, progress letters and discharge summaries in physiotherapy register.
Speaking: diagnosis, prognosis, home exercises, adherence and chronic pain conversations.
Reading: rehab guidelines, return-to-work guidance and clinical workplace texts.
Listening: physiotherapy consultations and multidisciplinary team briefings.
Common mistakes to avoid
Preparing for the retired Standard Assessment Pathway instead of APEP.
Assuming the Clinical Workshop can be completed remotely.
Assuming FLYR eligibility without checking the current APC country list.
Preparing with non-physiotherapy OET role-play material.
Candidate checklist before you start
Confirm your profession route before choosing a test date.
Check your OET profession version and current AHPRA score table.
Prepare passport, qualification, transcript, registration and experience evidence early.
Plan PSV, council assessment, exams and supervised practice timing together.
Keep official AHPRA, National Board and assessment council links as your final source.
Official sources to verify
AHPRA registration process and English Language Skills standard.
Medical Board of Australia and Australian Medical Council for doctors.
NMBA and AHPRA IQNM Self-Check for nurses and midwives.
Australian Pharmacy Council and Pharmacy Board for pharmacists.
Australian Physiotherapy Council and Physiotherapy Board for physiotherapists.
How we help Australia pathway candidates
The goal is not only to pass OET. It is to prepare with the right profession version, the right register and a test timeline that supports your registration route.
Writing correction
Profession-specific letters with feedback on purpose, selection, tone, organisation and register.
Speaking role-play
Patient-centred practice for Australian healthcare communication and common clinical scenarios.
Listening and reading
Practice for workplace texts, clinical consultations, guidelines and multi-accent audio.
Pathway timing
Guidance on aligning OET preparation with assessment, PSV, exam and application milestones.
Frequently asked questions
Quick answers for Australia pathway candidates planning OET and registration.
Is OET accepted for Australia healthcare registration? OET is accepted across the AHPRA professions covered here, but the exact score table depends on test date and National Board rules. Verify the current AHPRA standard before booking.
What changed in 2026 for AHPRA English scores? AHPRA's minimum scores changed on 23 April 2026. Tests on or before 22 April 2026 follow the previous grade table; tests on or after 23 April 2026 use numerical OET scores.
Can I combine two OET sittings for AHPRA? AHPRA can accept a maximum of two sittings within a 12-month period when each sitting includes all four sub-tests. Always confirm the current standard before relying on combined results.
Which profession version of OET should I book? Book the version that matches your profession: Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy or Physiotherapy. Using another profession version can make your preparation and evidence unsuitable.
Can Dr Hesham help with Australia OET preparation? Yes. Support can focus on your profession, weak sub-tests, writing corrections, speaking role-plays and a realistic timeline before your test date.
Not sure which pathway applies to you?
Send your profession, target country, current OET stage and application timeline. We will guide you toward the right preparation step.

## Gulf Pathway Guide 2026: OET for Qatar and Gulf Licensing

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/gulf-pathway-guide.html

OET for Gulf licensing: Qatar DHP verification and qualifying exam steps, UAE PQR and Saudi SCFHS rules, for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and physiotherapists.

Gulf Pathway Guide - Qatar Focus Gulf Pathway Guide for OET Healthcare Professionals
A practical Gulf pathway guide for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and physiotherapists, with detailed Qatar DHP steps and a wider Gulf licensing overview.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 19 May 2026 · Updated 2 Nov 2026
Message on WhatsApp for Pathway Guidance Join Free Community
Apply on the regulator's online system
Complete primary source verification
Track the six-month preliminary evaluation
Sit the regulator's licensing exam
Build profession-specific OET readiness
Qatar pathway overview
Most Qatar healthcare applicants follow the same broad workflow: an application on DHP's Registration and Licensing System, primary source verification (PSV), preliminary evaluation, the qualifying examination unless an exemption applies, a licensed employer and licence issuance.
Important: This guide is educational orientation only. It is not legal, immigration, employment or regulator advice. Always verify with DHP / MOPH, DataFlow and your employer before paying any fee.
Stage What it means Planning risk
DHP online application Apply on DHP's Registration and Licensing System. The preliminary evaluation can be requested without an employer. Wrong scope or specialty can delay everything.
Primary source verification Verify qualifications, registration and experience through a DHP-approved provider such as DataFlow; the report is attached to the online evaluation. DHP lists PSV as mandatory for all healthcare practitioners, and the evaluation is not complete without the report.
Preliminary evaluation DHP evaluates your application and documents. Valid for six months only; if you do not apply for a temporary or permanent licence in that time, you need a new evaluation.
Qualifying exam Computer-based Prometric exam: 150 MCQs in 3 hours for every exam on the DHP list. Pass marks differ by profession; DHP allows an unlimited number of attempts.
Licence The licensing application is completed once you have a licensed employer facility. A police clearance certificate and a medical report are required at licensing, so missing documents delay issue.
Key Qatar Prometric and English facts
DHP uses computer-based qualifying exams; book the OET version for your profession and check your employer's English requirements before booking.
Prometric format
Every exam on the DHP qualifying examination list is a computer-based Prometric exam of 150 MCQs in 3 hours.
Pass mark
DHP lists 60 percent for General Practitioner, General Dentist and Pharmacist, 50 percent for nursing, midwifery, physiotherapy and other allied health exams, and 65 percent for most specialist physician exams.
Attempts
DHP says applicants may attempt the qualifying exam an unlimited number of times. Confirm with DHP how long a pass stays valid for your application.
OET target
The DHP guidelines we checked do not set an OET score. Ask your employer in writing which English test and score it needs, and book the OET version for your profession.
DHP / MOPH Qatar Doctors: Qatar DHP physician pathway
For IMGs and specialists applying as General Practitioner, Specialist or Consultant in Qatar. Classification depends on qualification, experience and specialty rules applied in DHP's evaluation.
Step What to prepare
1 Apply on DHP's Registration and Licensing System and submit the evaluation request for your scope.
2 Submit documents for primary source verification through a DHP-approved provider such as DataFlow. DHP lists PSV as mandatory for all healthcare practitioners.
3 Receive the preliminary evaluation, which is valid for six months.
4 Sit the Qatar qualifying exam for your specialty. Circular DHP/2025/24 (30 December 2025) limits qualifying exam exemptions to Qataris, offspring of Qatari women and graduates of universities and higher education institutions in Qatar, so confirm any other exemption with DHP in writing.
5 Ask your employer which English evidence it requires, for example OET Medicine; the DHP guidelines we checked do not set an OET score.
6 Secure employment with a licensed healthcare facility in Qatar.
7 Submit the licensing documents, including the verification report, a police clearance certificate and a medical report.
OET preparation focus
Writing: referral, discharge and transfer letters for Gulf hospital systems.
Speaking: chronic disease, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, Ramadan medication adjustment and culturally sensitive bad news.
Reading: abstracts, clinical guideline summaries and workplace texts.
Listening: multi-accent consultations in a diverse Gulf workforce.
Common mistakes to avoid
Assuming PLAB, USMLE or MRCP removes the Qatar qualifying exam or PSV without written confirmation from DHP.
Not following up the Certificate of Good Standing, which DHP makes the applicant’s responsibility.
Booking the wrong physician specialty Prometric exam.
Letting the six-month preliminary evaluation expire.
DHP / MOPH Qatar Nurses: Qatar DHP nursing pathway
For internationally qualified nurses, specialist nurses, nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists, educators and midwives targeting Qatar healthcare employers.
Step What to prepare
1 Apply on DHP's Registration and Licensing System and submit the nursing evaluation request.
2 Send degree, transcript, registration, experience letters and passport for PSV through a DHP-approved provider such as DataFlow.
3 Receive the DHP preliminary evaluation, which is valid for six months.
4 Sit the Qatar nursing qualifying exam: 150 MCQs in 3 hours, with a 50 percent cut score for Registered General Nurse and Registered Midwife.
5 Ask your employer which English evidence and score it requires, for example OET Nursing; the DHP Guidelines for Nurses do not set an OET score.
6 Secure an employment offer from a Qatari healthcare facility.
7 Submit the licensing documents (including a police clearance certificate from the Qatari Ministry of Interior and a medical report), pay any fees and receive a temporary or permanent DHP licence; a temporary licence lasts up to six months and cannot be renewed.
OET preparation focus
Writing: nursing referrals, discharge letters and patient education for bilingual Arabic / English settings.
Speaking: education, calming distressed patients and culturally sensitive family communication.
Reading: care plans, infection-control bulletins and workplace policies.
Listening: ward briefings and nurse-patient interactions in multinational teams.
Common mistakes to avoid
Booking OET Medicine instead of OET Nursing.
Assuming a US NCLEX pass automatically bypasses all Qatar requirements.
Letting English certificates expire during the application.
Submitting police clearance without required attestation.
DHP / MOPH Qatar Pharmacists: Qatar pharmacy licensing pathway
For pharmacists and pharmacy technicians applying through DHP. The Pharmacist qualifying exam on the DHP list is 150 MCQs in 3 hours, with a 60 percent cut score.
Police clearance note: DHP’s Guidelines for Pharmacists list a valid police clearance certificate from the Qatari Ministry of Interior, addressed to the Ministry of Public Health and valid for 3 months, as a licensing requirement. A temporary licence applied for without a QID needs a home-country police clearance attested by MOFA.
Step What to prepare
1 Apply on DHP's Registration and Licensing System and submit the pharmacy or pharmacy technician evaluation.
2 Submit degree, transcript, home registration, experience letters and passport for PSV through a DHP-approved provider such as DataFlow.
3 Receive the preliminary evaluation, which is valid for six months.
4 Sit the Qatar Pharmacist qualifying exam unless you fall in an exempt category under Circular DHP/2025/24.
5 Ask your employer which English evidence it requires, for example OET Pharmacy; DHP’s Guidelines for Pharmacists do not set an OET score.
6 Secure a job offer from a DHP-recognised community, hospital or institutional pharmacy.
7 Submit the licensing documents, including the verification report, a Qatari Ministry of Interior police clearance and a medical report, and pay any fees.
OET preparation focus
Writing: pharmacy letters to GPs or consultants, supplier requests and dispensing-incident notes.
Speaking: medication counselling, Ramadan advice, adherence and OTC sale refusal.
Reading: SmPCs, MoPH drug safety alerts and pharmacy policies.
Listening: counselling, ward conversations and pharmacy team handovers.
Our OET course for pharmacists trains these pharmacy letters and counselling role-plays with pharmacy scenarios.
Common mistakes to avoid
Using OET Medicine or Nursing preparation for OET Pharmacy.
Submitting expired home registration evidence.
Assuming a Gulf exemption transfers automatically to Qatar.
Letting the six-month preliminary evaluation expire.
DHP / MOPH Qatar Physiotherapists: Qatar allied health pathway
For physiotherapists applying under DHP allied healthcare practitioner rules, whether you are aiming for hospital, primary care, sports medicine or private clinic roles.
Step What to prepare
1 Apply on DHP's Registration and Licensing System and submit the physiotherapy evaluation.
2 Submit degree, transcript, registration, experience letters and passport for PSV through a DHP-approved provider such as DataFlow.
3 Receive the preliminary evaluation, which is valid for six months.
4 Sit the Qatar Physiotherapist qualifying exam (150 MCQs in 3 hours, 50 percent cut score) unless DHP confirms an exemption.
5 Ask your employer which English evidence it requires, for example OET Physiotherapy; the DHP guidelines we checked do not set an OET score.
6 Secure employment from a DHP-recognised physiotherapy provider.
7 Submit the licensing documents, including the verification report, a police clearance certificate stamped by MOFA and addressed to MOPH, and a medical report, and pay any fees.
OET preparation focus
Writing: referrals, progress letters and discharge summaries for rehabilitation teams.
Speaking: diagnosis, prognosis, home exercises, sports rehab and return-to-play advice.
Reading: rehab guidelines, return-to-work and return-to-sport documents.
Listening: physiotherapy consultations and MDT briefings.
Physiotherapists can follow the OET course for physiotherapists , and other allied health professionals will find their OET route in OET for allied health professions .
Common mistakes to avoid
Using non-physiotherapy OET speaking cards.
Using vague functional language instead of specific physiotherapy terminology.
Letting English evidence expire during licensing.
Submitting documents in a language other than Arabic or English without an official translation.
Wider Gulf at a glance
Across the GCC, the workflow is broadly similar: online portal, PSV, licensing exam, employer sponsorship and final regulator approval. Each country has its own rules.
Country / authority Main regulator Typical exam / verification
Qatar DHP / MOPH Qatar qualifying exam (Prometric) plus PSV through a DHP-approved provider such as DataFlow.
UAE Federal MOHAP Unified PQR: the authority licensing exam (unless exempt) plus primary source verification.
Dubai DHA Unified PQR: the authority licensing exam (unless exempt) plus primary source verification.
Abu Dhabi DOH Unified PQR: the authority licensing exam (unless exempt) plus primary source verification.
Saudi Arabia SCFHS Classification through Mumaris+, document verification by an SCFHS-approved company and Saudi licensing exams (the pharmacist exam, SPLE, runs at SCFHS-approved Prometric centres).
Bahrain NHRA Licences follow the PQR published on the NHRA website (Decision No. 23 of 2017).
Kuwait Kuwait MOH Not checked against an official source for this guide; confirm directly with Kuwait MOH.
Oman OMSB / MOH OMSB Occupational Classification exams, booked through Pearson VUE and used by the Ministry of Health and other institutions for licensing.
Score caution: The UAE Unified PQR (MOHAP, DOH, DHA and SHA) lists OET at grade C or above as one accepted proof of English in specific cases, such as some experience or exam exemptions based on a licence from a listed country. The Qatar DHP guidelines and SCFHS classification requirements we checked do not set an OET score. Employers can set their own requirement, so confirm the test and score in writing before booking.
Candidate checklist before you start
Create your account on DHP's Registration and Licensing System or the correct Gulf regulator portal.
Identify your exact scope, specialty and profession category.
Start primary source verification early with an approved provider and keep document source details consistent.
Book the correct OET profession version and check how recent your result must be.
Track the six-month preliminary evaluation window.
Prepare the police clearance, medical report, official translations and employer documents.
Official sources to verify
Checked on 2 November 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the regulator and your employer before paying any fee.
Qatar DHP: Primary Source Verification
Qatar DHP: Qualifying Examinations
Qatar DHP: Circular DHP/2025/24 (30 December 2025)
Qatar DHP: Guidelines for Pharmacists
Qatar DHP: Guidelines for Nurses
Qatar DHP: Guidelines for Allied Health Professions
UAE: Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements (PQR), April 2025
SCFHS: professional classification requirements
SCFHS: SPLE applicant guide
NHRA Bahrain: Decision No. (23) of 2017
OMSB Oman: Occupational Classification examinations
How we help Gulf pathway candidates
Gulf candidates need healthcare English that fits real patient-facing practice, not generic grammar study. Preparation should match profession, target country and licensing timeline.
Writing correction
Profession-specific letters for hospital, clinic, pharmacy and rehabilitation contexts.
Speaking role-play
Practice for Gulf-appropriate patient education, family communication and cultural sensitivity.
Listening and reading
Build speed for clinical audio, policy texts, medicine information and workplace instructions.
Timeline planning
Align OET study with DataFlow, Prometric, employer documents and licence deadlines.
Frequently asked questions
Quick answers for Qatar and Gulf pathway candidates.
Is this Gulf guide only for Qatar? The detailed pathway focuses on Qatar: DHP's Registration and Licensing System, primary source verification and the Qatar qualifying exam. The page also includes a wider Gulf comparison for the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman.
Is DataFlow required for Qatar? DHP lists primary source verification as a mandatory requirement for all healthcare practitioners, and the verification report is attached to the online evaluation application. DataFlow is one of the DHP-approved verification providers.
How many Qatar Prometric attempts are allowed? DHP's qualifying examination page says applicants may attempt the qualifying exam an unlimited number of times. Each exam on its list is 150 MCQs in 3 hours; confirm with DHP how long a pass stays valid for your application.
What OET score should Gulf candidates target? There is no single Gulf score. The UAE Unified PQR lists OET at grade C or above as English evidence in specific cases, while the Qatar DHP guidelines and SCFHS requirements we checked set no OET score. Use the score your regulator or employer confirms in writing.
Can Dr Hesham help me choose between Qatar, UAE and Saudi routes? Yes. Send your profession, current documents, OET stage and target country on WhatsApp for pathway-focused preparation guidance.
Not sure which pathway applies to you?
Send your profession, target country, current OET stage and application timeline. We will guide you toward the right preparation step.
Ask on WhatsApp

How the learning journey works
The page is designed to convert confusion into a clear preparation route.
1
Understand the task
Use orientation lessons to understand OET expectations and avoid common preparation mistakes.
2
Diagnose weak areas
Find whether writing, speaking, reading, listening, grammar or timing is holding you back.
3
Practice with feedback
Move from passive watching to corrected writing, role-play practice and targeted improvement.
4
Check readiness
Book the exam when your performance is more controlled, not when you are still guessing.

Doctors, nurses, pharmacists, physiotherapists and allied health professionals who want structured OET preparation rather than random tips.

## Free English Placement Test (CEFR) Before OET | Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/english-placement-test

Free English placement test online: Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking with an indicative CEFR level (Pre-A1 to C2) before OET or IELTS.

100% Free — No Card Required
Free General English Placement Test
Get an indicative CEFR placement estimate across Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking — on the CEFR scale from Pre‑A1 to C2 . Suitable for OET, IELTS, PTE, TOEFL and General English learners.
Free account required. Results saved to your profile.
Listening
Everyday conversations and announcements that test real understanding.
Reading
Short practical texts that pinpoint how much you genuinely comprehend.
Writing
Brief written tasks that reveal your grammar, vocabulary and organisation.
Speaking
Spoken responses measured for fluency, clarity and range.
Start Free Placement Test
Approximately 60–85 minutes. Exact duration may vary because the assessment adapts to the learner’s responses. Your answers save as you go — you can pause and continue later.
CEFR Pre‑A1 to C2 — where do you sit today?
Whether you are just starting with English or already operating at an advanced level, the placement test maps each skill to the CEFR scale and shows your strongest areas and where to focus next — before you invest in OET, IELTS, PTE or TOEFL preparation.
How does the free English placement test work?
Create a free account. Your answers save automatically, so you can pause and come back later.
Complete the four skills. Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking tasks adapt to your responses and take approximately 60–85 minutes in total.
Get an indicative CEFR level for each skill. See where you sit from Pre‑A1 to C2, your strongest skill and where to focus next.
Choose the right preparation. Use your result to decide whether to build general English first or start profession-specific OET preparation.
Who should take the placement test?
Nurses, doctors, pharmacists and allied health professionals planning to take OET for registration in the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, the USA or the Gulf.
Candidates who are not sure whether to start with a foundation English course or go straight into OET preparation.
Learners preparing for IELTS, PTE or TOEFL who want a free starting-point check across all four skills.
Anyone who has taken OET before and wants to see which skill is holding their score back.
What should you do with your result?
Your placement result is a guide, not an exam score. As a rough starting point:
Pre‑A1 to B1
Build grammar, healthcare vocabulary and sentence control first. The recorded Basic English Course is designed for learners at Beginner, A1, A2 or B1 level before intensive OET work.
See the Basic English Course
Around B2
OET benchmarks Grade B (350) to CEFR C1, so most B2 learners need structured practice to close the gap. Start profession-specific OET preparation and get regular feedback on Writing and Speaking, where most candidates lose marks.
OET course for nurses · OET course for doctors
C1 and above
Focus on exam technique: timed letters, role-play structure and Part A speed. Corrected letters usually move scores faster than more reading.
OET writing correction · OET tips
Placement test FAQ
Is the placement test really free?
Yes. The test is free. You need a free account so your answers save as you go and your results stay in your profile.
How long does the placement test take?
Approximately 60 to 85 minutes. The exact time varies because the assessment adapts to your responses, and you can pause and continue later.
Is this an official OET or IELTS test?
No. It is a free General English placement test from OET with Dr Hesham. It gives an indicative CEFR estimate for each skill to guide your preparation; it does not replace an official OET, IELTS, PTE or TOEFL result.
Which level should I reach before starting OET preparation?
As a rough guide, if your estimate is B1 or below in most skills, build your general English first; if you are around B2 or above, move straight into profession-specific OET preparation.

OET practice FAQ
Short answers before you choose where to practise.
Is any OET practice free?
Yes. The sample tests guide, model letters, role-play cards, score calculator and placement test are free. A free learner account also includes free Writing and Speaking sample results.
Can I practise OET on a computer?
Yes. Mock exams in the learner app can be set to computer, paper or OET@Home mode so you practise in the format you will sit.
Do I need an account to practise?
The website guides need no account. Timed practice, mocks and feedback run inside the learner app, which needs a free account.
Which skill should I practise first?
Start with the sub-test furthest from your target grade. The placement test and a first mock show where that gap is.
